npc:aelthalyste.text: Aelthalyste. In the Undercity's War Quarter, Aelthalyste teaches Forsaken priests the power of Shadow. She guides their discipline and sends troll acolytes to their own elders in Orgrimmar. Aelthalyste trains Forsaken priests in the power of Shadow. Many priests across Azeroth revere the Holy Light, but her students have turned from it. She rose as an incorporeal banshee and shares the spectral agony and relentless resolve of Sylvanas Windrunner's followers. From her chamber in the Undercity's War Quarter, she calls aspiring priests from distant outposts to master their darker arts. She teaches them to wield suffering as a weapon. Aelthalyste respects the spiritual traditions of other Horde practitioners. She sends troll initiates away from her shadow teachings and across the sea to Ur'kyo in Orgrimmar, where they can learn Darkspear spiritualism. Her deference lets Horde spellcasters grow within their own traditions and strengthens ties between Kalimdor and Lordaeron.

npc:ahanu.text: Ahanu. At Hewa's Armory, Ahanu helps couriers arriving in Thunder Bluff. He crafts and trades leather armor for travelers and young braves setting out across Mulgore and the wider plains, and shows new couriers the way across the bluffs. Ahanu crafts leather gear in Hewa's Armory on Thunder Bluff's lower rise. His friend Jahan Hawkwing sends him hides from the Crossroads, which he works into durable armor for travelers across Kalimdor's grasslands. Travelers arriving by wind rider from the Crossroads can find him among the city's tradesfolk. He receives their deliveries and points messengers toward the local flight roosts.

npc:alamar-grimm.text: Alamar Grimm. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Alamar Grimm teaches young gnomes to wield fel magic. Since Gnomeregan fell, he has grown bitter toward outsiders and means to teach his students to summon an imp. At Anvilmar, Alamar Grimm still resents the fall of Gnomeregan. While other gnomes in Coldridge Valley work to recover and tinker, he distrusts ordinary adventurers and even the Ironforge dwarves sheltering his people. He grumbles that their allies care more for diplomacy with humans than for reclaiming the fallen city. Alamar seeks those who share his belief that his people may need ruthless power. Alamar Grimm guides young gnomes who take up fel magic. A tainted memorandum earns a rare warm welcome, and he begins teaching basic spells. Before sharing the dangerous knowledge needed to bind a demonic imp, he demands proof of each novice's magical and physical endurance. He sends them to retrieve strange feather charms carried by local Frostmane troll novices.

npc:altsoba-ragetotem.text: Altsoba Ragetotem. At Bloodvenom Post, Altsoba Ragetotem equips Horde travelers for the blighted woods of Felwood. The tauren weaponsmith offers maces, staves, and axes. Altsoba Ragetotem outfits Horde scouts and travelers bound for Felwood’s corrupted woods from Bloodvenom Post. The outpost stands in the forest’s heart, amid demonic corruption and tainted wildlife. Keeping supplies moving there is a grim necessity. Altsoba offers sturdy crescent axes and heavy war mauls, so warriors entering the corrupted timberlands have weapons at hand.

npc:alyissia.text: Alyissia. In Aldrassil, Alyissia teaches young night elves to fight with strength and discipline. Her lessons prepare warriors to defend the young world tree. Inside Aldrassil, Alyissia trains young night elves to fight with steel and shield. They learn a path apart from nature magic and the priesthood. Kaldorei forces are known for Sentinels and stealthy archers, yet danger across Kalimdor also calls for warriors who can hold the front line. Wild creatures and corrupted grells press into Shadowglen, where Alyissia teaches battle fury, stances, and endurance.

npc:amber-kearnen.text: Amber Kearnen. In Westfall, Amber Kearnen watches the Defias Brotherhood for SI:7. From cover, she tracks their unlawful activity for Master Mathias Shaw. Far from Stormwind Keep, Amber Kearnen scouts for SI:7 in Westfall. She watches an abandoned tower occupied by the Defias Brotherhood. Master Mathias Shaw directs her work. Kearnen briefs covert operatives sent to stop Defias threats and gather intelligence across the contested countryside.

npc:andron-gant.text: Andron Gant. In the Apothecarium, Andron Gant arranges commissions and relic recoveries for local scholars. The reclusive Forsaken is often drunk and rarely leaves the Undercity. Andron Gant keeps to the Apothecarium, among its noxious fumes, and seldom ventures beyond the Undercity's stone walls. He seems little more than a drunken scholar. Yet local mages sometimes have him send couriers to distant shores for obscure relics, including the Tablet of Markri.

npc:anduin-wrynn.text: Anduin Wrynn. Stormwind's throne rests with ten-year-old Anduin Wrynn while his father, King Varian Wrynn, is missing. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and the royal court bear the work of governing. Anduin Wrynn was born in the peace after the Second War. His name honors his grandfather, King Llane, and Sir Anduin Lothar, the legendary knight. When King Varian Wrynn vanished on the way to a diplomatic summit in Theramore, Anduin was crowned to keep the kingdom steady. Clever and compassionate, he is still only ten and has little say in affairs of state. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and royal councilor Lady Katrana Prestor share the work of ruling the realm. Stormwind Keep holds Anduin as tension grows at court. Highlord Bolvar watches over the kingdom's defenses and works to keep it whole. Lady Katrana Prestor presses her counsel upon the court and undermines troop deployments to outlying human settlements. Anduin feels how fragile his court has become and longs for his father. For now, nobles with designs of their own and guardians surround the young king.

npc:apothecary-helbrim.text:
Apothecary Helbrim. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim gathers unfamiliar reagents for the Royal Apothecary Society. Sent to Kalimdor, he studies the Barrens for the Forsaken. Apothecary Helbrim works beneath the sun at the Crossroads, far from the Royal Apothecary Society's quarters in Undercity. Sent across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, he searches the Barrens for useful plants, fungi, and other natural specimens.

Helbrim depends on travelers to bring him samples, including local fungal spores. He also works with Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff. Through his work, the Forsaken's alchemists reach beyond Lordaeron's ruined borders.

npc:apothecary-zinge.text: Apothecary Zinge. Beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, Apothecary Zinge studies specimens for the Forsaken. Her work also sends research shipments across Horde lands. In the Apothecarium beneath the Undercity, Apothecary Zinge serves the Forsaken. She works under Master Apothecary Faranell, searching for chemical and biological compounds that can advance their aims. Her research links her to field researchers and scouts far beyond Tirisfal Glades, even at distant outposts in Kalimdor. Apothecary Zinge relies on couriers and adventurers to carry test materials across the sea. She regularly writes to Apothecary Helbrim at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Her shipments include toxic wolf heart samples from Silverpine Forest, so he can study how Lordaeron's toxins affect Kalimdor's beasts.

npc:archaeologist-flagongut.text: Archaeologist Flagongut. At Menethil Harbor, Archaeologist Flagongut keeps in touch with field researchers across the Great Sea. The dwarven scholar of the Explorers' League is staying at the Deepwater Tavern on his way to the Whelgar Excavation Site. Archaeologist Flagongut rests over a mug at the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Like many members of Ironforge's Explorers' League, he traveled west across Khaz Modan to aid discoveries near the Whelgar Excavation Site in the Wetlands. Far from the high halls of the library, he keeps ties with field researchers, studying lost relics and reports brought across the Great Sea from distant expeditions. Dwarven curiosity reaches beyond one continent. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker in Darnassus sends Flagongut a mysterious fossil unearthed in Darkshore by the absent-minded Prospector Remtravel. Flagongut is amazed. He once brought a similar fossil to the Explorers' League's annual conference in Ironforge, convinced its power could somehow be unlocked.

npc:archaeologist-hollee.text: Archaeologist Hollee. In Auberdine, Archaeologist Hollee follows dwarven research across Darkshore. Ancient ruins draw Ironforge scholars to the coast, where she keeps in touch with prospectors seeking relics and unusual geological formations. Archaeologist Hollee works from Auberdine, among the night elves who guard and settle Darkshore. She is a regional contact for surveyors and expedition teams crossing the wilderness. The Explorers' League sends its people across the sea to uncover traces of ancient history, and Darkshore's ruins give them ground to study.

npc:archbishop-benedictus.text:
Archbishop Benedictus. In Stormwind City, Archbishop Benedictus leads the Church of the Holy Light from the Cathedral of Light. He guides the faithful and the Alliance through uncertain times. Archbishop Benedictus leads the Church of the Holy Light after the death of his mentor, Archbishop Alonsus Faol. He saw the First and Second Wars devastate the kingdoms and helped oversee the building of the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City. There he vowed to uphold the virtues of the faith.

After Lordaeron fell and the Scourge rose during the Third War, the human kingdoms looked to Benedictus for spiritual guidance. From the Cathedral, he counsels the royal court and trains newly initiated priests. He also directs holy crusades against the undead and demonic forces threatening Azeroth. Across the Alliance, people regard Archbishop Benedictus as a gentle, wise, and benevolent patriarch. He offers hope to the public and rallies heroes against dark threats, including Amnennar the Coldbringer in Kalimdor. He also helps purify cursed relics brought by faithful adventurers.

npc:archmage-ansirem-runeweaver.text: Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver. At the Violet Citadel, Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver oversees Kirin Tor work as Dalaran is rebuilt. A senior human wizard on the Council of Six, he survived the Scourge's destruction of the city. His willful daughter ran off to Booty Bay to become a pirate. Ansirem Runeweaver helped defend Dalaran for decades. He holds a seat on the Council of Six, which rules the Kirin Tor. He survived when Arthas Menethil and the Scourge marched on the city and Archimonde was summoned. After Dalaran fell, Ansirem joined the effort to rebuild it. The protective shield came down early, and he now works from the Violet Citadel. Ansirem's ties reach beyond the Alterac Mountains. His willful daughter, Catelyn, ran off to Booty Bay to become a pirate, taking an ancient troll dagger he found while researching in Stranglethorn. Ansirem has dealt with Baron Revilgaz there. He has also studied troll antiquities and keeps diplomatic conduits open across distant realms.

npc:archmage-malin.text: Archmage Malin. Outside the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind City, Archmage Malin directs the city's arcane affairs. Once a pupil of Archmage Trelane, he now coordinates agents seeking magical artifacts and rare reagents across the Eastern Kingdoms. In the Mage Quarter, Archmage Malin oversees Stormwind's arcane practitioners from beneath the Wizard's Sanctum. He learned magic under Archmage Trelane and now protects the scattered legacy of his former master. Acolytes study inside the tower. Malin watches over matters across the realm that need magical oversight. North in the perilous ruins of the Arathi Highlands, Archmage Malin's trusted associates search for Trelane's lost possessions and delicate spell components. Skuerto and Apprentice Kryten carry out that work. From the capital, Malin coordinates their efforts and depends on capable Alliance travelers to bring instructions, supplies, and intelligence into hostile territory.

npc:archmage-xylem.text:
Archmage Xylem. In northern Azshara, Archmage Xylem keeps apart from the world. He pursues arcane research in an isolated tower and receives only those who can aid his studies or settle his vendettas. Archmage Xylem lives in a secluded spire above northern Azshara's ruined elven coast. No road or trail reaches his sanctuary. His servant Sanath Lim-yo magically carries approved visitors up the cliffs.

Across Kalimdor, people know Xylem as profoundly eccentric and dangerous to approach. Even fellow scholars treat him with caution. He behaves unlike almost any other human mage.

npc:argent-guard-manados.text: Argent Guard Manados. At Darnassus, Argent Guard Manados keeps watch over corruption across Kalimdor. He serves the Argent Dawn and calls for aid against the Twilight's Hammer beneath Ashenvale's waves. Argent Guard Manados keeps the Argent Dawn's watch in Darnassus. Most of the order guards Lordaeron against the Scourge, while he stands among the artisans and tradefolk of the Craftsmen's Terrace. From there, he watches for threats to northern Kalimdor's balance. Word reaches him that the Twilight's Hammer has gained a foothold beneath Ashenvale's waves. So he calls on capable heroes to strike at Blackfathom Deeps and recover the cult's artifacts of dark devotion.

npc:argos-nightwhisper.text: Argos Nightwhisper. In Stormwind's Park, Argos Nightwhisper guides Alliance travelers toward Darkshore. His brother Gershala studies the corruption spreading there. Argos Nightwhisper lives among the night elves gathered in Stormwind's Park. Its quiet groves remind them of the kaldorei's ancestral woodlands. Like others of his kin in the human kingdom, Argos helps connect the new allies across the Great Sea. Reports from across the ocean trouble him. He urges capable Alliance champions to travel to Auberdine in Darkshore, where his brother Gershala needs help against the spreading corruption.

npc:ashlan-stonesmirk.text: Ashlan Stonesmirk. At Dun Modr, Ashlan Stonesmirk watches the border with the regiment guarding the Thandol Span. This dwarven explosives expert stays alert for dangers to Ironforge. In the northern Wetlands, Ashlan Stonesmirk serves with the regiment guarding the Thandol Span at Dun Modr. His knowledge of explosives makes him a useful contact when suspicious materials threaten dwarven defenses.

npc:austil-de-mon.text: Austil de Mon. In Brill, Austil de Mon teaches newly risen Forsaken to fight for the Dark Lady. He trains warriors at Gallows' End Tavern. In Brill, Austil de Mon trains Forsaken warriors at Gallows' End Tavern. Those leaving Deathknell find him among their first instructors. The living once drank and rested in the inn. Now Austil teaches the newly liberated undead martial discipline and combat against the foes surrounding the kingdom.

npc:ayanna-everstride.text: Ayanna Everstride. In Aldrassil, Ayanna Everstride guides young kaldorei in the hunter’s way. She teaches marksmanship, tracking, and survival beneath the World Tree. In Shadowglen, Ayanna Everstride trains newly awakened kaldorei hunters within Aldrassil. To the night elves, hunters guard the sacred forests. Their work reaches beyond trapping or shooting from afar. Ayanna teaches young hunters early martial skills, ranged combat, and ways to survive Teldrassil’s perilous woods.

npc:ayessa-dawnsinger.text: Ayessa Dawnsinger. In Valanaar on Zephras Isle, Ayessa Dawnsinger guides the Horde aligned Skyborne. She leads the Windshapers through their trials and politics. From Valanaar on Zephras Isle, Ayessa Dawnsinger leads the Windshapers, the Skyborne aligned with the Horde. She directs their efforts across the island as they face outside threats and divisions among themselves. She guides them through alliances in Kalimdor and beyond, with their survival at stake.

npc:azar-stronghammer.text: Azar Stronghammer. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Azar Stronghammer guides new dwarven paladins in the Holy Light. He sends promising recruits to Ironforge for further instruction after their training. Azar Stronghammer guides newly inducted dwarven paladins on Dun Morogh's freezing slopes. Humans are often linked to the great cathedrals, yet the dwarves of Khaz Modan have embraced the Holy Light. Having mastered his own martial and spiritual vows, Azar helps novices find their way. When a recruit shows dedication and spiritual maturity, he sends them up the mountain path to Ironforge, where veteran champions such as Tiza Battleforge can teach them further.

npc:azuregos.text:
Azuregos. Along Azshara’s coast, Azuregos keeps watch over Highborne relics. Malygos entrusted their great magic to him, though he would rather study in peace and drive off anyone who breaks his watch. Azuregos roams the shores and crags around Eldarath, the ancient ruins he has made his sanctuary. Relics from before the Great Sundering still lie along these shattered coasts. As Malygos’s servant, he keeps their powerful artifacts from careless mortals.

Azuregos does not hide in a dark cave. He patrols the region openly and calls himself its lord of all magic. His humor is often sardonic, yet he fiercely defends Azshara’s treasures from adventurers seeking fame or plunder.

npc:bailiff-conacher.text: Bailiff Conacher. In Lakeshire Town Hall, Bailiff Conacher upholds Stormwind law under Magistrate Solomon. With Redridge under siege, he relies on travelers to carry out local decrees. Bailiff Conacher works with Magistrate Solomon in Lakeshire Town Hall to uphold law across the Redridge Mountains. Blackrock orcs and local gnolls besiege the town, leaving Conacher without ordinary civic procedures or royal garrisons. So he issues legal decrees that let passing travelers carry out capital justice in the realm's name. When the dark mage Morganth took the Tower of Ilgalar, he bent the local Shadowhide gnolls to his will. The Court of Lakeshire judged the beasts guilty of high treason. Stormwind law sentences those who aid a fugitive and criminal to death. By Solomon's Law, Conacher sends travelers across the ridges to find Shadowhide gnolls and bring back their pendants as proof the crown's law has been carried out.

npc:bailor-stonehand.text: Bailor Stonehand. In Thelsamar, Bailor Stonehand waits on ore shipments stolen by Mo'grosh ogres. The skilled dwarven smith crafts a specialized alloy for masterwork armaments and once taught the human weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell. Bailor Stonehand tends the forge in Thelsamar. His knowledge of minerals and specialized alloys reaches beyond Khaz Modan. He taught Jordan Stilwell the foundations of metallurgy and shared formulas for blessed paladin armaments such as Verigan's Fist. Mo'grosh ogres in the hills northeast of Thelsamar stole ore shipments bound for Bailor's forge. Without the raw material, he cannot make his rare alloys. He needs travelers and allies to recover the supplies from the ogres' encampments.

npc:balir-frosthammer.text: Balir Frosthammer. In Coldridge Valley, Balir Frosthammer rallies recruits as Rockjaw troggs press into dwarven lands. Balir Frosthammer calls new recruits to defend Coldridge Valley. Dwarven and gnomish novices have long found safety and training there. But trouble underground has driven violent Rockjaw troggs to the surface. Balir is among the first to raise the alarm, urging recruits to thin their numbers before they push farther into Dun Morogh. Balir Frosthammer shares his name with Tannok Frosthammer of Kharanos. The two may belong to the same family, whose members stand by Ironforge. They help keep the cold mountain passes safe for travelers, miners, and mountaineers as threats grow across the region.

npc:barithras-moonshade.text: Barithras Moonshade. In Auberdine, Barithras Moonshade seeks travelers to gather rare plants from Darkshore’s shadowed wilds. Barithras Moonshade watches over Auberdine and helps the night elves study and care for Darkshore. He sends travelers into nearby caverns to gather fungi for study and use, including death cap mushrooms. Barithras also guides capable travelers south to meet Onu. The ancient works to heal Darkshore’s tainted soil and soothe its restless natural spirits.

npc:barkeep-daniels.text: Barkeep Daniels. At the Lakeshire Inn, Barkeep Daniels keeps drinks flowing while raiders trouble the roads. Town guards, fishermen, and travelers find welcome there, though supplies are running low. Near the bridge, Barkeep Daniels pours drinks and greets visitors at the Lakeshire Inn. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs have pressured Lakeshire for months, and its defenders turn to the tavern after grim patrols. Raids and severed roads have disrupted trade across the region. With liquor running low when the town needs good cheer, Daniels welcomes travelers willing to fetch shipments from safer settlements.

npc:baron-revilgaz.text:
Baron Revilgaz. On Booty Bay’s high balcony, Baron Revilgaz holds the port and its trade in his hands. He leads the Blackwater Raiders for the Steamwheedle Cartel, keeping the harbor open to Alliance and Horde while guarding his own interests. He hires help to watch rivals and seek ancient relics in the jungle. From the Salty Sailor Tavern, Baron Revilgaz watches Booty Bay’s docks with Fleet Master Seahorn, his trusted tauren advisor, beside him. Cutpurses, merchants, and privateers all answer to his firm hand. Blackwater Cove began as a human settlement, but trolls overwhelmed it before the First War. Goblins claimed and fortified the port, and it grew into the Blackwater Raiders’ commercial hub.

Revilgaz keeps Booty Bay officially open to Alliance and Horde travelers. He enforces neutrality within the harbor so trade can continue. When wars elsewhere in Azeroth slowed business, Revilgaz found a way to draw crowds back to Booty Bay. The discovery of tastyfish gave him the means: he created the Stranglethorn Fishing Extravaganza. Across Stranglethorn Vale, he keeps watch on rivals and threats.

He hires sabotage against the Venture Company at Lake Nazferiti. He also watches Nesingwary’s hunting expedition and rogue human military camps in the north. With Monte Gazlowe and Pozzik at the Mirage Raceway, he keeps trade ties active.

npc:bartleby.text: Bartleby. At the Pig and Whistle Tavern, Bartleby drinks and picks fights in Stormwind's Old Town. His stubborn grip on his ale makes him a test for aspiring warriors, who must face him in a tavern brawl. Bartleby spends his days at the Pig and Whistle Tavern in Stormwind's Old Town. Its crowd runs rougher than the taprooms of Cathedral Square. He clings to his favorite mug, drinks cheap ale, nurses grievances, and picks fights with anyone who disturbs him. Stormwind's warrior trainers make a practical test of Bartleby. Harry Burlguard sends fledgling fighters to find him and take his mug. They trade bare-knuckle blows with the intoxicated brawler, proving they have the grit to face an unruly opponent at close quarters.

npc:bashana-runetotem.text: Bashana Runetotem. On Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise, Bashana Runetotem studies plants and corruption. Daughter of Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem, she aids the Cenarion Circle. Bashana Runetotem carries her father Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem’s druidic legacy on Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise. While he guides tauren druids and advises Cairne Bloodhoof, she studies unusual plants and threats across the region. She gives travelers tools such as evergreen pouches to cultivate mysterious flora, including morrowgrain. She also coordinates Horde efforts against corruption spreading from places such as Blackfathom Deeps.

npc:bath-rah-the-windwatcher.text: Bath'rah the Windwatcher. Near Chillwind Point, Bath'rah the Windwatcher studies the northern winds in the Alterac Mountains. Far from his tropical homeland, the jungle troll shaman seeks champions strong enough to shape the tempest into weapons. Bath'rah the Windwatcher keeps to the cold ruins of the Alterac Mountains. Jungle trolls usually dwell among warm forests and coasts, far from these peaks. A seasoned shaman and craftsman, he listens to the wind and communes with nature spirits. He means to bind violent storms into weapons for those strong enough to wield them.

npc:beldin-steelgrill.text: Beldin Steelgrill. At Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh, Beldin Steelgrill keeps dwarven war machines running. Across Khaz Modan, he is renowned as a master technician, repairing siege engines and armored wagons with a steady supply of specialized tools. Just down the road from Kharanos, Steelgrill's Depot tests and services steam tanks and siege engines. The work strains heavy wrenches, cutters, and precision instruments against metal and rumbling boilers. Beldin needs replacements constantly, keeping local ironworkers busy at his bench.

npc:bingles-blastenheimer.text: Bingles Blastenheimer. On Loch Modan’s southeastern shore, Bingles Blastenheimer waits beside the wreck of his flying machine. Stranded among troggs and beasts, the gnomish aviator needs his tools and parts back. Bingles Blastenheimer took his customized flying craft into the skies, but the landing went badly. His gyrocopter malfunctioned and crashed on Loch Modan’s southeastern shore. Bingles survived, though the machine broke apart. Far from Ironforge, he stays near the wreck, wary of hungry crocolisks and hostile troggs. Troggs from a nearby island stole his tools and Blastencapper explosives, so he asks passing travelers to recover them.

npc:bink.text:
Bink. In Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries, Bink teaches aspiring mages the arcane arts. Her quick mind helps promising students find wizards across the Alliance. In Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries, Bink teaches the path of the mage. She works among the scholars, priests, and arcanists gathered in the Mystic Ward. Like many gnomes driven from Gnomeregan, she has made her home in the dwarven mountain stronghold. Her keen mind and skill in arcane craft guide those learning magic.

Bink knows wizards across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. She points promising apprentices toward mentors such as High Sorcerer Andromath in Stormwind and Tabetha in Dustwallow Marsh.

npc:bishop-delavey.text: Bishop DeLavey. In Stormwind Keep, Bishop DeLavey listens to the court's quiet concerns. He represents the Church of the Holy Light in the Petitioner's Chamber, where matters of faith and state meet. Bishop DeLavey advises Stormwind's court from within the keep. While Archbishop Benedictus tends the Cathedral of Light, DeLavey lives among nobles and petitioners. He offers spiritual counsel as he reckons with the kingdom's politics. From his place at court, he hears whispered rumors and delicate grievances before they reach Highlord Bolvar Fordragon or the young King Anduin.

npc:blanchy.text: Blanchy. Near the Jansen Stead, Blanchy rests beside the Furlbrows’ wagon in Westfall. The gentle mare travels through the troubled countryside with Theodore and Verna Furlbrow. Before Blanchy drew the Furlbrows’ wagon through Westfall, she worked their farm in Stormwind’s breadbasket. She was sweet-tempered and known for behaving well. Years of hard labor have worn her down, and the journey away from troubled homesteads has left her exhausted. Yet her appetite remains hearty. Verna offers Blanchy’s treasured blanket and feed pouch to travelers who bring nourishing handfuls of oats from nearby fields.

npc:bloodmage-drazial.text:
Bloodmage Drazial. At the northern pass, Bloodmage Drazial studies the Blasted Lands with his sister Lynnore. They examine its native beasts and brew mixtures for hardy travelers. Near the northern pass between the Swamp of Sorrows and the Blasted Lands, Bloodmage Drazial studies a strange magic. He and his sister Lynnore draw power from the harsh land through blood magic. Many high elves reject such forbidden arts or grieve for Quel'Thalas.

Scorpoks, snickerfangs, and blasted boars thrive with unnatural vigor. Drazial and Lynnore believe the Dark Portal's opening released the energy that changed them. They gather the beasts' organs and tissues, then brew volatile mixtures that grant great strength, agility, and endurance. Drazial works apart from the factions stationed in the Blasted Lands. He serves neither the Alliance nor the Horde. Instead, he trades his alchemical skill to anyone hardy enough to cross the wasteland and gather his ingredients. Travelers bring organs from local predators, and his cauldrons keep bubbling.

npc:bloodmage-lynnore.text: Bloodmage Lynnore. Near the Blasted Lands' northern entrance, Bloodmage Lynnore studies the power within local beasts. She camps with her brother Drazial and brews draughts from their organs. Near the northern entrance to the Blasted Lands, Bloodmage Lynnore studies blood magic with her brother Drazial. Few elves in the Eastern Kingdoms practice this forbidden art. The land is harsh and corrupting, yet Lynnore searches native beasts for arcane and vital energies. Travelers bring her brains and gizzards from local animals. She distills them into elixirs that sharpen intellect and spirit.

npc:bluff-runner-windstrider.text: Bluff Runner Windstrider. On Thunder Bluff's mesas, Bluff Runner Windstrider carries urgent messages across the city. He points Horde travelers toward far-off frontiers, including Ashenvale, Feralas, and the Plaguelands. Bluff Runner Windstrider carries messages across Thunder Bluff's high plateaus. His swift runs keep the city's leaders and visitors informed. He jogs along rope bridges and pathways, calling out news and bearing dispatches. When distant outposts need reinforcements, Windstrider calls on passing champions to carry word and answer the call to arms. Bluff Runner Windstrider sends messages far beyond Mulgore. He directs travelers north to join Senani Thunderheart's great hunt at Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. He points seasoned scouts south toward Camp Mojache in Feralas and bears grave warnings of the ongoing undead menace in the Western Plaguelands. His dispatches bind Mulgore's tribal heart to the Horde's wider conflicts.

npc:braelyn-firehand.text: Braelyn Firehand. At Sun Rock Retreat, Braelyn Firehand lives among the Horde and draws travelers into a campaign against the night elves of Stonetalon Peak. Braelyn Firehand is an elven mage, yet she lives openly among tauren lodges and orcish tents. The retreat’s shamans and chieftains tolerate her, apparently unaware of her true loyalties. She calls herself an observer of the region’s magic and hires passing Horde mercenaries for dangerous work among the crags.

npc:braenna-flintcrag.text: Braenna Flintcrag. In Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Braenna Flintcrag teaches the ways of the Holy Light. She trains priests in healing and spiritual discipline, and tells visiting night elf priests when they are called home to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Braenna Flintcrag trains priests in the Hall of Mysteries. There, in Ironforge's Mystic Ward, she teaches dwarven acolytes to heal and raise defensive wards with the Holy Light. Her lessons prepare them for a dangerous world. Through this work, she tends the spiritual needs of Khaz Modan, in a city renowned for its forges and warriors.

npc:brainwashed-noble.text: Brainwashed Noble. Deep in the caverns outside the Deadmines, Brainwashed Noble remains in Defias hands. Enchantment has stripped him of his will, and he now guards their refuge beside undead minions instead of walking Stormwind's grand halls.

npc:brandur-ironhammer.text: Brandur Ironhammer. In Ironforge, Brandur Ironhammer trains young paladins in the Holy Light and sends them across the Alliance. In the Hall of Mysteries, Brandur Ironhammer teaches novice paladins the ways of the Holy Light. He and Tiza Battleforge guide young dwarven champions through the trials of the Tome of Divinity. Tiza has spoken plainly of Brandur’s flaws. He works to master his envy and keep the inner purity expected of a warrior of the Light. Brandur links Ironforge to the wider Alliance brotherhood. Human initiates who come to the mountain are sent south to Duthorian Rall in the Cathedral of Light. Seasoned paladins go to battlegrounds such as Chillwind Camp in the Western Plaguelands. Veteran crusaders are directed to Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker for the demanding trials of the war charger.

npc:brann-bronzebeard.text: Brann Bronzebeard. In southern Silithus, Brann Bronzebeard's companions wait for word from his latest expedition. The youngest brother of King Magni and Muradin is famed across Azeroth as an explorer, archaeologist, and founding leader of the explorers' league. His search for titan ruins and ancient history has led him deep into the deadly wastes. Brann Bronzebeard chose the open wilds while his eldest brother Magni ruled Ironforge and Muradin served on the front lines. A veteran of the Second War, Brann turned his strength toward the forgotten past when peace came. As a leader of the explorers' league, he charted the Eastern Kingdoms, from Elwynn Forest to the jungles of Zul'Gurub. Then he crossed the Great Sea to seek the mysteries of ancient Kalimdor.

npc:branstock-khalder.text: Branstock Khalder. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Branstock Khalder guides dwarven priests in the Holy Light and watches the trogg threat beyond the outpost. At Anvilmar, Branstock Khalder teaches novice priests their first prayers and sacred runes. He guides them in the Light while troggs menace the local mountaineers. When a novice has learned enough, Branstock sends them through Coldridge Pass to Kharanos. There, they can seek further guidance from his superior, Father Maxan Anvol.

npc:brave-moonhorn.text: Brave Moonhorn. At the Barrens' southern border, Brave Moonhorn watches the Great Lift into Thousand Needles. From its heights, he warns travelers of dangers ahead. Brave Moonhorn guards the boundary between the northern plains and the canyonlands. From above Thousand Needles, he watches the canyon floor for threats, especially hostile centaur clans. Travelers often meet him before descending into the needles. He warns them of danger before they step onto the Great Lift's massive platforms. Brave Moonhorn distrusts the Grimtotem tauren. He tells traveling Horde allies to keep their distance because the tribe acts erratically and suspiciously around Thousand Needles. To help defend the region, he sends couriers to Freewind Post with warnings for Cliffwatcher Longhorn.

npc:brewmeister-bilger.text: Brewmeister Bilger. In Southshore's inn cellar, Brewmeister Bilger waits for deliveries from distant lands. The intoxicated dwarf spends his hours tasting potent spirits. Beneath Southshore's inn, Brewmeister Bilger paces the cellar with hiccups. He seeks the strongest brews Azeroth can offer. Even in a stupor, Brewmeister Bilger can judge spirits. He favors heavy dwarven moonshines and potent southern liquors. Special batches delight him, such as the moonshine Foggy MacKreel sends from the Thandol Span.

npc:brock-stoneseeker.text: Brock Stoneseeker. In Thelsamar, Brock Stoneseeker teaches mining to novice prospectors. At his School of Mining and Surveying, he trains them to find and extract ores and minerals. In Thelsamar, Brock Stoneseeker teaches miners at his School of Mining and Surveying. Loch Modan's hills hold rich mineral veins, and miners need a sure hand with a pickaxe and a keen eye for rock. Brock teaches them to find ore, extract raw metals, and survey underground deposits. His lessons help Alliance tradesfolk supply Ironforge's smithies.

npc:bromos-grummner.text: Bromos Grummner. In Anvilmar, Bromos Grummner guides young dwarven paladins in the Holy Light and welcomes them to its discipline. He teaches steadfast faith and the bond between dwarves and humans in the Knights of the Silver Hand. In Anvilmar, Bromos teaches young paladins the rites of battle and sacred invocations. Yet he speaks of more than combat. The Knights of the Silver Hand unite Ironforge and the human kingdoms of the Alliance in a shared righteous purpose.

npc:brother-joshua.text: Brother Joshua. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Brother Joshua guides those who come to learn the ways of the Holy Light. He trains novice priests to heal wounds and strengthen their allies. Brother Joshua waits near the main altar in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. As a priest of the Church of the Holy Light, he teaches new servants of the faith to heal, raise protective wards, and focus their minds to commune with the Light. Young human priests beginning their service to the Alliance find one of their first guides in him.

npc:brother-kristoff.text:
Brother Kristoff. In Cathedral Square, Brother Kristoff preaches beneath Uther's statue. The human priest seeks practical books for sermons on spiritual strength. Brother Kristoff serves the Church of the Holy Light in Cathedral Square, beneath the statue of Uther the Lightbringer. He works among the citizens and pilgrims who pass through the plaza, rather than within the Cathedral of Light.

For sermons such as the Fortitude of the Spirit, he turns to worldly comparisons. In The Stresses of Iron, he finds a way to explain how the soul endures pressure. The Holy Light's gift of inner resolve, he teaches, is like the tempered strength of worked metal.

npc:brother-neals.text: Brother Neals. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Neals keeps the food and drink stores supplied. He oversees shipments and samples wine from the local vineyard. From his rooms in the upper belfry, Brother Neals follows grape manifests from the Northshire vineyards. Frequent tastings let him check each vintage. He also tracks deliveries from the valley’s fields, keeping the abbey’s stores supplied.

npc:brother-sarno.text: Brother Sarno. At the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City, Brother Sarno welcomes visitors and worshipers. He also sends Alliance travelers to Ironforge, where Tinkmaster Overspark needs help reclaiming Gnomeregan. Pilgrims and travelers pass Brother Sarno first, just inside the cathedral's main entrance. A brother of the Church of the Holy Light, he welcomes those seeking prayer, comfort, or guidance. His kind manner puts visitors at ease amid the cathedral’s daily life. Brother Sarno also helps the Alliance beyond the cathedral. When word reached him that Tinkmaster Overspark in Ironforge needed help with his rogue invention, Techbot, in Gnomeregan, Sarno directed capable travelers toward Dun Morogh. His aid supports gnomes displaced from their home.

npc:brother-wilhelm.text: Brother Wilhelm. Behind Goldshire's smithy, Brother Wilhelm guides young paladins into the wider forest. They come from Northshire Abbey to take their first steps in Elwynn. Brother Wilhelm trains new paladins behind Goldshire's smithy. Northshire Valley shelters those who begin their path in the Light, but many seek his guidance once they enter the wider forest. He teaches them their sacred duties as they leave the abbey. Then they take up the work of protecting the realm. Brother Wilhelm guides aspiring paladins toward the Tome of Divinity. Its rite teaches initiates the weight of sacrifice and the power of divine redemption. Through the trials, they test their devotion and learn to wield the Light. They can resurrect fallen comrades and uphold justice across the Kingdom of Stormwind.

npc:cain-firesong.text: Cain Firesong. At the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, Cain Firesong guides Forsaken mages in the arcane. He trains them in Tirisfal Glades, then sends advanced students to the Undercity for deeper study. Cain Firesong teaches the arcane arts in Brill, where Forsaken mages begin their studies. Many Forsaken spellcasters favor shadow or necromancy, but Cain keeps to the arcane. He mentors mages who set out from Deathknell. Deathguards direct visitors to the upstairs landing of the Gallows' End Tavern, where Cain can be found. They joke that he arrived too late to get a room. When students outgrow their first studies in Tirisfal Glades, Cain sends the capable onward. He directs them to Anastasia Hartwell, a master sorceress who lives in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity.

npc:calvin-montague.text: Calvin Montague. At Deathknell's gate, Calvin Montague catches newly awakened Forsaken on their way out and tricks passersby into running errands for him. Calvin Montague waits beyond Deathknell's gates, where the road leads into Tirisfal Glades. He tries to persuade wandering adventurers to carry his letters with false promises. He will neither handle his own correspondence nor pay a fair courier's fee. Other prominent undead named Montague manage banking interests in the Undercity. Calvin follows a less reputable path, relying on petty schemes and deception.

npc:captain-danuvin.text: Captain Danuvin. At Sentinel Hill, Captain Danuvin rallies Westfall’s defenders. He directs People's Militia volunteers and recruits to patrol the roads and drive back Gnolls and outlaws. Their orders guard supply lines and farmlands from hostile hands. Captain Danuvin directs patrols from Sentinel Hill's fortified tower. Stormwind's regular garrison has withdrawn, leaving Westfall's defenses weak. So he relies on travelers, farmhands, and volunteer fighters to keep some order across the plains. Captain Danuvin watches the roads and open lands around Sentinel Hill. Riverpaw Gnolls raid near the central outposts, so he sends patrols to thin their packs and secure the perimeter. His orders keep marauders and opportunists from surrounding the camp.

npc:captain-rugelfuss.text: Captain Rugelfuss. At Loch Modan’s southern gate, Captain Rugelfuss meets a sudden trogg uprising. The stern dwarf organizes the defense of the border. From the Valley of Kings, Captain Rugelfuss guards Loch Modan’s southern gateway. Ironforge’s forces are stretched thin across the world, so veteran officers like him defend its home territories. He sets military ceremony aside and turns to the danger at the border. Troggs surge into the highlands from ancient caverns. They have overwhelmed outlying dwarven patrols and built fortified footholds nearby. Rugelfuss calls on capable travelers to thin their ranks and drive them back from the roadway, defending the King’s lands.

npc:captain-shatterskull.text: Captain Shatterskull. At Mor'shan Base Camp, Captain Shatterskull directs the Horde's defense of its northern border. A seasoned orc commander, he organizes the fight against night elf forces near Warsong Gulch. At Mor'shan Base Camp, Captain Shatterskull guards the Horde's foothold on the edge of Ashenvale. He works with fellow officers such as Kadrak against night elf sentinels and Silverwing forces seeking to reclaim the borderlands. The struggle over Ashenvale's timber and ancient lands keeps the Barrens frontier under constant threat.

npc:captain-thalo-thas-brightsun.text: Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun. At Ratchet's docks, Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun keeps a cordial face toward Alliance travelers. He serves the Steamwheedle Cartel and resents the Theramore forces at Northwatch Hold for firing on his vessels. From Ratchet's docks, Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun leads the Thalo'dan Privateers under the Steamwheedle Cartel's banner. Ratchet welcomes merchants of every flag who bring coin, though trade along the Barrens coast carries danger. Northwatch Hold lies just south of the port, and its heavy cannons threaten neutral sea lanes. Brightsun remains cordial toward visiting travelers, but the garrison's attacks on his fleet have tried his patience. Brightsun cannot send his fleet against Northwatch Hold without endangering Ratchet's neutrality. Instead, he turns to capable Horde mercenaries to settle the score. Their strikes aim to silence the cannons and free his captured crew. By using Horde auxiliaries, Brightsun protects his shipping interests without provoking direct Alliance retaliation against the cartel or entering the conflict openly.

npc:captured-mountaineer.text: Captured Mountaineer. Beneath Brill, a captured Ironforge Mountaineer is held below the Gallows' End Tavern. The Forsaken keep him bound for the Royal Apothecary Society's experiments. An Ironforge Mountaineer is held beneath the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, far from Khaz Modan. Patrons drink above while the Royal Apothecary Society tests its concoctions on him. Apothecary Johaan and his peers measure their developing plague against living Alliance captives. They study how swiftly and painfully the toxins kill.

npc:captured-scarlet-zealot.text:
Captured Scarlet Zealot. Beneath Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, a Scarlet Zealot is held captive. Forsaken apothecaries use him to test concoctions for the Royal Apothecary Society. Beneath Gallows' End Tavern, a Scarlet Crusade zealot sits chained and defiant. He keeps his faith and calls the undead around him abominations. He calls on the Light to shield him from his captors.

The Forsaken hold him for Apothecary Johaan. As a living human, he is valuable to the apothecary, who tests the lethality of experimental plagues and toxins under development.

npc:caretaker-folsom.text: Caretaker Folsom. Along Stormwind’s Canals near the Park, Caretaker Folsom watches over a noble household’s remains. He once served the Flintridge estate, and now sells what survived its bloody end. Folsom followed his father into service at the Flintridge estate. The household was massacred, and the manor stood abandoned. Its remaining funds eventually ran out. Left to watch over what remained, Folsom now sends the family's surviving heirlooms and possessions to auction.

npc:carolai-anise.text: Carolai Anise. In Brill, Carolai Anise teaches alchemy as her experiments unsettle the guards. Carolai Anise teaches novice alchemists in Brill and pursues her own strange brews. Many Forsaken researchers work under the Royal Apothecary Society's grim mandate. Carolai's unpredictable experiments and smoking retorts are well known, and the Deathguards watching Brill openly grumble that she seems bent on blowing up her own house.

npc:cazul.text: Cazul. In the Cleft of Shadow, Cazul guides young warlocks toward command of demons. Though blind and ancient, he keeps old orc warlock traditions alive. Beneath Orgrimmar, Cazul waits in the Cleft of Shadow to counsel rising warlocks. Though blind, he senses the Twisting Nether's currents and hears demons whisper. Those who seek to master their craft and bind more dangerous servitors are often sent to him. His arcane power remains.

npc:cerellean-whiteclaw.text:
Cerellean Whiteclaw. Near Auberdine’s docks and inn, Cerellean Whiteclaw mourns the love he lost. The Sundering’s memory still haunts him, and he longs to bring Anaya’s restless spirit peace. Before the War of the Ancients, Cerellean Whiteclaw shared his life with Anaya Dawnrunner. Ten thousand years ago, the demonic invasion shattered ancient Kalimdor. Anaya died when her city, Ameth'Aran, fell in the destruction. Grief-stricken, Cerellean followed Malfurion Stormrage into the long druidic slumber.

The Emerald Dream brought little peace from his memories. Millennia later, Cerellean awoke and wandered Darkshore in grief. There he found Anaya's ghost still bound to the stones where she fell.

npc:chef-breanna.text: Chef Breanna. In Lakeshire, Chef Breanna keeps the Stormwind soldiers fed as they guard the Redridge Mountains. She leads the town's kitchen, using hearty local ingredients to help the defenders hold on. Chef Breanna runs a restaurant house in northwestern Lakeshire with her assistants, Crystal Boughman and Gretchen Vogel. She feeds the entire local battalion, whose strength matters as Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and murlocs besiege the town. Stormwind's garrison is understaffed, so every meal counts. Her signature Redridge Goulash draws on wild game and beasts from the surrounding ridges to feed the weary guards.

npc:chef-grual.text: Chef Grual. In Darkshire, Chef Grual keeps the Scarlet Raven Tavern's kitchen working. He feeds the Night Watch and weary travelers, though some ingredients raise eyebrows. Darkshire's cook works with scarce supplies. Highwaymen, wolves, and undead trouble the roads from Westfall and Stormwind, so fresh provisions are hard to find. Grual makes do with what the wilderness offers. He cooks wolf flank and meat scavenged by local adventurers, using whatever reaches his kitchen.

npc:chef-jessen.text:
Chef Jessen. In Southshore, Chef Jessen keeps the town fed while the borders remain tense. His turtle bisque is famous. Chef Jessen supplies meat and provisions in Southshore, in southern Hillsbrad Foothills. Locals and visiting Alliance soldiers rely on his provisions, and he is a skilled cook.

Before plague and war disrupted northern Lordaeron, Chef Jessen often traveled north past Dalaran to the shores of Lordamere Lake. There he gathered meat from native snapjaw turtles for his Soothing Turtle Bisque. Travelers who help gather its ingredients can learn the recipe from him.

npc:chief-archaeologist-greywhisker.text: Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker. Outside the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker gathers reports from the coast. The Ironforge dwarf coordinates the Explorers' League's research and keeps watch on colleagues in Darkshore. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker works far from his Ironforge home, outside the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. The Explorers' League sent him across the sea to Kalimdor for fieldwork. He speaks with night elf scholars such as Tarelvir and seeks knowledge of these ancient lands. In Ironforge, his lectures covered ancient lore and primordial beings, including the Wild God Agamaggan. Now he hopes to learn what the night elves' ancestral lands hold. Greywhisker oversees dwarven excavations in Kalimdor and follows expeditions searching ancient coastal ruins. To reach prospectors across the sea in Darkshore, he depends on travelers to carry messages. Field research in unexplored lands is perilous. He waits anxiously for word from the dig sites and hopes his colleagues are safe among the ruins.

npc:christoph-jeffcoat.text: Christoph Jeffcoat. At Tarren Mill, Christoph Jeffcoat supplies the Forsaken with goods for trade and travel. His wares serve crafters and travelers in Hillsbrad Foothills, where the Alliance and the Syndicate contest the land. At Tarren Mill, Christoph Jeffcoat supplies the Forsaken stronghold with what its people need. He sells reagents, tools, threads, and spices to soldiers and traveling artisans. Among his goods are spices for turtle bisque, rare schematics, and alchemical vials. Horde forces crossing southern Lordaeron rely on such supplies as they face Southshore and the region's dangers.

npc:chronormu.text: Chronormu. In the Western Plaguelands, Chronormu works to mend time's damaged threads. Mortals know her as Chromie, a bronze dragon who often works beside them. Mortals know Chronormu as Chromie, an eccentric and cheerful female gnome. She belongs to the bronze dragonflight and serves Nozdormu, the Timeless One. The titans charged bronze dragons to guard history and correct disruptions in the timeways. In her gnome form, Chronormu walks among mortals as an approachable and optimistic peer. Among Lordaeron's ruined remains, Chronormu watches over the devastated Western Plaguelands. The kingdom's fall and the Scourge's spread tore at the region's history, leaving temporal anomalies and trapped remnants. From places such as the ruins of Andorhal, she works quietly with mortal adventurers to mend tangled timelines and investigate disturbances. Only when necessary does she reveal the full majesty of the dragonflight.

npc:clarice-foster.text: Clarice Foster. In the Pools of Vision, Clarice Foster dwells among tauren seers and mystics. Far from Lordaeron, the Forsaken woman spends her days in contemplation beneath the bluffs of Mulgore. Most Forsaken remain in Lordaeron, rebuilding their kingdom beneath the Undercity. Clarice Foster has crossed to Kalimdor and the heart of tauren lands. She lives in the cavernous Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff's mesa. There she dwells among Forsaken apothecaries and tauren shamans who study the earth's spiritual and elemental mysteries.

npc:colonel-kurzen.text: Colonel Kurzen. In northern Stranglethorn Vale, Colonel Kurzen's former soldiers seek to end his rule. Once trusted by Stormwind, he now commands a rogue militia from an armed compound. Colonel Conrad Kurzen once served Stormwind as a capable and honorable officer. The kingdom's leaders trusted him with an expeditionary unit sent south into Stranglethorn Vale. Deep in the jungle, his behavior grew erratic and grandiose. He claimed the wilderness as his own and cast aside his loyalty to Stormwind. Kurzen's change divided his soldiers. Some followed him with blind loyalty or zeal, while others recoiled from his madness and brutality. When Emerine Junis rejected his advances, he threw her into the compound's prison. Lieutenant Doren led the soldiers who broke away and founded Rebel Camp along the northern road. Now they fight Kurzen's rampaging force to stop it.

npc:commander-mar-alith.text: Commander Mar'alith. At Cenarion Hold, Commander Mar'alith holds the line against the dangers of Silithus. He leads the fight against silithid swarms and Twilight's Hammer cultists, while grief over his missing wife weighs on him. At Cenarion Hold, Commander Mar'alith guards the Cenarion Circle's desert stronghold. The druids study Silithus's ancient ecological and cosmic anomalies, while he directs the work of war. His forces strike at the silithid hives of Hive'Ashi, Hive'Zora, and Hive'Regal. They keep the incursions from overwhelming the expedition's central foothold. Commander Mar'alith's stern bearing cannot hide his grief. His beloved wife, Natalia Mar'alith, went into the shifting sands on an assignment for the Circle and did not return. He holds to his duty to the Cenarion expedition, though he longs for news of what happened to her in the wastes.

npc:councilman-millstipe.text: Councilman Millstipe. In Darkshire, Councilman Millstipe wants justice for Duskwood's people. He lives in the town hall as the council grows bitter over Stormwind's rule. Undead and ferocious beasts threaten Darkshire, while its council wrestles with Stormwind City's bureaucracy. Councilman Millstipe shares the town's growing bitterness toward the crown. The grave robber Dextren Ward was caught selling freshly dug corpses to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Darkshire's leaders sentenced Ward to death, but Stormwind's House of Nobles commuted the execution and locked him away in the Stormwind Stockade.

npc:count-remington-ridgewell.text: Count Remington Ridgewell. In Stormwind Keep, Count Remington Ridgewell devotes his wealth to a noble’s collection. A human of the House of Nobles, he gathers rare artifacts, heirlooms, and fine art. Count Remington Ridgewell turns from military campaigns and local uprisings to the past. His family’s museum holds jewelry and artifacts, and he spends his wealth on relics from fallen civilizations and houses across Azeroth. To fill his gallery, he finances adventurers and sends field agents such as Mayara Brightwing into dangerous ruins. They search from Alterac’s mountain redoubts to the volcanic wastes of the Burning Steppes.

npc:crane-operator-bigglefuzz.text: Crane Operator Bigglefuzz. At Ratchet's docks, Crane Operator Bigglefuzz scrambles to recover cargo spilled from a crane. He searches for a stolen bottle before his superiors discover the loss. Crane Operator Bigglefuzz rushes to clear the wreckage across Ratchet's wharves. Like many goblin dockworkers, he chose speed over safety. While lifting an overloaded haul from a merchant vessel, his crane buckled and crates crashed across the docks. Scoundrels seized the confusion and swept up goods. Now he must recover the most precious cargo before Gazlowe or the local port masters dock his pay. The greatest loss was a crate of rare ninety-nine-year-old port. Before Bigglefuzz could secure the spilled cargo, Mad Magglish, an elusive vagrant, snatched a bottle and hid. Bigglefuzz may have to answer for losing something irreplaceable.

npc:craven-drok.text: Craven Drok. In the Cleft of Shadow, Craven Drok seeks travelers for a delicate matter. He wants them to consider how the Alliance sees the Horde. Craven Drok keeps to the winding paths beneath Orgrimmar, away from its sunlit avenues. The Cleft of Shadow draws warlocks, rogues, and folk in less honorable trades. Drok stays out of sight and hires passersby for discreet errands. One concerns the Horde's standing with the Alliance.

npc:cyrus-therepentous.text: Cyrus Therepentous. At Slither Rock, Cyrus Therepentous puts mortals who enter his lair to the test. He seeks survivors strong enough to serve the Black dragonflight. From his cavern at Slither Rock, Cyrus Therepentous watches the volcanic crags of the Burning Steppes. He scorns mortal travelers and calls anyone who disturbs his lair a fool. Yet he does not strike every trespasser down. Instead, he sends his minions against them in a deadly trial. Those who survive the flames may prove useful to the Black dragonflight.

npc:darcy-parker.text: Darcy. At the Lakeshire Inn, Darcy keeps the town's defenders fed and spirits high. She serves drinks and warm meals, with special care for Guard Parker. Darcy keeps the Lakeshire Inn's counter running through long days and nights. Lakeshire's militia come for food and drink while gnolls and Blackrock orcs keep the town under pressure. She also looks after guards posted around town. Travelers carry hot meals and friendly errands to defenders stationed along the borders. Near Three Corners, Guard Parker patrols the roads, and Darcy makes sure he has lunch. She thinks he works too hard on an empty stomach, so she often sends travelers with a meal for him. Darcy watches Martie Jainrose closely. She believes Martie is jealous and rivals her for Parker's favor, even as they all work to defend Lakeshire.

npc:dark-cleric-beryl.text: Dark Cleric Beryl. In Brill, Dark Cleric Beryl guides newly awakened undead priests through shadow magic. From the Gallows' End Tavern, he helps them face their unholy existence under the Dark Lady. Upstairs in Brill's Gallows' End Tavern, Dark Cleric Beryl trains new Forsaken priests. He teaches that a priest's power comes from darkness and shadow, but mastering darkness also calls for knowledge of the light. Under his guidance, newly risen priests turn to shadow and the dark arts. Their first trials include crafting their Garments of Darkness and proving their dedication to this path.

npc:darkmaster-gandling.text: Darkmaster Gandling. Beneath Caer Darrow, Darkmaster Gandling trains necromancers for the Scourge. From Scholomance, he serves the Cult of the Damned through experiments on the living and the dead. Darkmaster Gandling rules Scholomance beneath Caer Darrow. The academy trains aspiring necromancers for the Scourge. Gandling is a living human of the Cult of the Damned. With the lich Ras Frostwhisper, he committed atrocities against innocent captives taken from the surrounding lands. In the classrooms, students learn to brew plagues, reanimate the dead, and sculpt flesh. In the Headmaster's Study, Gandling commands Scholomance's dark relics and trapped spirits. He joins arcane and shadow magic with forbidden necromancy. With these arts, he curses intruders and hurls them through shadow portals into sealed chambers around the study. There, they face the risen dead alone while Gandling shields himself from harm.

npc:darn-talongrip.text: Darn Talongrip. At Malaka'jin, Darn Talongrip watches the Stonetalon frontier. The orc scout tracks threats in the crags and carries word between forward outposts and Horde commanders. Darn Talongrip watches the rugged climbs from the southern Barrens into Stonetalon. At Malaka'jin, he directs recruits toward the Horde's new fronts in Ashenvale. Travelers climbing into the contested peaks can reach the Horde through his post. From Malaka'jin, Darn sends messages and reports from the front to commanders such as Kadrak, at the watch tower in the northern Barrens. Encampments scattered through the mountains face constant pressure. As sentry and courier, Darn keeps the Horde vanguard informed.

npc:daryl-the-youngling.text: Daryl the Youngling. At Farstrider Lodge, Daryl the Youngling tests travelers' marksmanship against Loch Modan's beasts. The young human hunter hopes to earn his place among veteran dwarven trackers. Dwarven mountaineers, trackers, and seasoned outdoorsmen watch Loch Modan's wilderness from Farstrider Lodge. Daryl tests his hunting instincts against travelers there. He challenges them to hunt the tough wild boars and other beasts roaming the crags and lakeshore.

npc:dashel-stonefist.text: Dashel Stonefist. In Old Town, Dashel Stonefist draws notice for his quick temper, heavy hands, and dangerous connections. The dwarf called Fist keeps to Stormwind City's rougher alleys, where covert investigators are watching. Old Town knows Dashel Stonefist as Fist, a name earned in street fights. Locals and city guards see a drunken, combative dwarf, quick to throw a punch outside a tavern. His place in the district brings him close to Stormwind's underworld. Smugglers, cutpurses, and political agitators trade coin and rumors there, beyond the eyes of Cathedral Square.

npc:david-trias.text:
David Trias. In Deathknell, David Trias teaches the newly awakened Forsaken to move unseen and fight with a blade. He prepares them to serve Queen Sylvanas and the Forsaken. Among Deathknell’s tombstones and ruins, David Trias trains newly risen undead. He seeks those with a gift for killing unseen. For the fledgling Forsaken, survival takes more than strength at arms. It calls for a precise strike from the dark.

Trias deciphers their orders and teaches them to wield daggers and hide their movements. He shows them how to turn their reanimated reflexes against the living and the Scourge.

npc:dawnwatcher-selgorm.text: Dawnwatcher Selgorm. At the Craftsmen's Terrace in Darnassus, Dawnwatcher Selgorm watches for threats across northern Kalimdor. The human serves the Argent Dawn as an observer and liaison in the night elven capital, following reports of cult activity and dark powers stirring nearby. Dawnwatcher Selgorm keeps watch in Darnassus for the Argent Dawn. Though the order fights the undead Scourge in the Eastern Plaguelands, its vigilance reaches farther. From the Craftsmen's Terrace, Selgorm gathers reports of new threats in Kalimdor's wilds. The human links the night elves with the wider struggle against ancient evil and seeks Alliance travelers who can strike at cultists and dark powers before they spread.

npc:dawnwatcher-shaedlass.text: Dawnwatcher Shaedlass. From Darnassus, Dawnwatcher Shaedlass keeps watch for the Argent Dawn across Kalimdor. On the Craftsmen's Terrace, he seeks word of order members sent to scout hostile lands. The Argent Dawn fights the Scourge in the Eastern Plaguelands, yet keeps watch beyond Lordaeron. From Darnassus, Dawnwatcher Shaedlass follows the order's interests across Kalimdor. At his post on the Craftsmen's Terrace, he tracks covert expeditions against dark cults and corrupting powers that threaten the wider world.

npc:dazalar.text: Dazalar. In Dolanaar, Dazalar prepares young night elf hunters for Teldrassil's wilds. He teaches steady aim and bonds with the beasts of the great boughs. After leaving Shadowglen, young hunters train with Dazalar in Dolanaar. Night elf rangers and sentinels patrol the wilderness, so he teaches the patience and discipline needed to protect Teldrassil's fragile ecosystem. Dazalar teaches hunters to tame and care for beasts. The Kaldorei seek a pact with forest predators such as nightsabers, owls, and strigid hunters. Their companions learn to fight beside them through respect, not force.

npc:deathguard-bartholomew.text: Deathguard Bartholomew. In Brill, Deathguard Bartholomew watches over the town and helps travelers find their way. He helps keep order among the Forsaken defenders of Tirisfal Glades. Deathguard Bartholomew stands watch in Brill among the Forsaken guards defending Tirisfal Glades. They protect reclaimed land from the lingering Scourge, fanatical Scarlet Crusaders, and other threats to Lady Sylvanas's domain. Bartholomew also guides travelers around town and helps keep order among the newly risen.

npc:deathguard-burgess.text: Deathguard Burgess. In Brill, Deathguard Burgess watches over the town for the Forsaken. He guards the settlement and guides travelers to the services they need. North of the Undercity, Deathguard Burgess guards Brill from the Scourge and Scarlet Crusade. Like the other Deathguards in Tirisfal Glades, he guides arriving Forsaken to tradesfolk, class trainers, and civic services. His watch helps keep the vulnerable outpost running.

npc:deathguard-humbert.text: Deathguard Humbert. At Tarren Mill, Deathguard Humbert watches the Alliance across Hillsbrad. Dwarves from Dun Garok have taken his military gear. From a hidden camp, Deathguard Humbert watches Dun Garok for High Executor Darthalia. One morning, he left to gather firewood. While he was away, dwarven scouts from Dun Garok took his prized sword and other equipment. Now he must recover his arms and save his pride before high command learns what happened.

npc:deathguard-linnea.text: Deathguard Linnea. At a roadside post in southeastern Tirisfal, Deathguard Linnea watches the roads between Brill and the eastern borders. Her unit guards against the Scarlet Crusade and the Scourge still in the wilds. Travelers sometimes join them on patrol. Southeast of Brill, Deathguard Linnea guards a fortified post. The Forsaken defend their young realm from Scarlet Crusade infiltrators and Scourge still prowling the wilderness. Linnea and her fellow guards patrol the road and share reports with Magistrate Sevren in Brill. Their watch keeps the eastern road toward the Bulwark secure.

npc:deathguard-samsa.text: Deathguard Samsa. In Tarren Mill, Deathguard Samsa watches the frontier and sends travelers against nearby threats. Deathguard Samsa guards Tarren Mill, where the Forsaken hold their ground in the contested Hillsbrad Foothills. Horde sentries face pressure from Alliance outposts such as Southshore and from savage local wildlife. Samsa watches the perimeter and directs capable adventurers against dangers before they reach the settlement.

npc:deathguard-simmer.text:
Deathguard Simmer. At Deathknell’s edge, Deathguard Simmer tests newly risen Forsaken. He sends them west to raid a human pumpkin farm patrolled by the Scarlet Crusade for reagents needed by Brill’s apothecaries. Deathguard Simmer guards the ground outside Deathknell, where the Forsaken hold the line between their haven and Tirisfal Glades. Living humans still roam the region. Among them are the fanatical Scarlet Crusade, who see all undead as abominations to purge with fire and blade.

Simmer tests newly risen Forsaken by sending them west to Solliden Farmstead. Scarlet Crusade soldiers patrol from a nearby tower. The recruits must steal ten pumpkins and carry them to Apothecary Johaan in Brill.

npc:deathstalker-faerleia.text: Deathstalker Faerleia. In Pyrewood Village, Deathstalker Faerleia works against the leaders who rule it. From the town hall, she directs covert strikes against the Pyrewood Council, the puppets Arugal uses to govern the village.

npc:deathstalker-lesh.text:
Deathstalker Lesh. At Southpoint Tower, Deathstalker Lesh studies the human farms in Hillsbrad Foothills. She serves High Executor Darthalia and judges when the Forsaken should strike. From Southpoint Tower, Deathstalker Lesh watches the human farmers and town militia in nearby Hillsbrad Fields. The tower stands on the southern road through the Hillsbrad Foothills. Lesh belongs to the Deathstalkers, the Forsaken's covert network of scouts, spies, and assassins.

She tracks enemy movements and numbers for High Executor Darthalia in Tarren Mill. When the moment is right, Lesh sends Darthalia a coded message: “The raven's cry from the west doth beckon.” Those words signal that Hillsbrad is ripe for the Forsaken's attack.

npc:deathstalker-rane-yorick.text: Rane Yorick. At a farmhouse in Silverpine, Rane Yorick and her brother Quinn cannot reach the Sepulcher. Sent to scout the northern farms, they must get their report to High Executor Hadrec. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner relies on the Deathstalkers to watch across Lordaeron. They serve as her eyes and ears, and strike when Forsaken rule is threatened. Rane Yorick and her brother Quinn were sent to scout northern Silverpine Forest. Feral dangers closed around them, and their covert work became a fight to survive.

npc:deathstalker-vincent.text: Deathstalker Vincent. Inside Shadowfang Keep, Arugal has slain Deathstalker Vincent. The Forsaken scout entered with Deathstalker Adamant to learn the keep’s defenses before the Forsaken could attack. The Deathstalkers needed to learn Shadowfang Keep’s layout before the Forsaken could assault it. Vincent and Adamant slipped past the barricades and entered the fortress. Their mission failed. Adamant was captured and locked in a dungeon cell, while Vincent was brought before the keep’s master. Vincent refused to serve Arugal or yield to him. The mage executed him, leaving his body on the stone floor.

npc:deathwing.text: Deathwing. Deathwing's shadow still reaches Azeroth's deepest places. Once Neltharion the Earth-Warder, he was the black dragonflight's Dragon Aspect until the Old Gods drove him mad. He turned against the other Aspects and brought fire and turmoil to the world. Defeated near grim batol after the Second War, he is believed slain or hidden away. The titans gave Neltharion dominion over the earth and Azeroth's subterranean vaults. In those depths, the imprisoned Old Gods whispered to him. During the ancient War of the Ancients, their madness took hold. Neltharion tricked the other Dragon Aspects into placing part of their essence in a golden disc called the Dragon Soul. He said it would stop the Burning Legion, then turned the weapon on his allies and unleashed devastation. Most mortal kingdoms believe Deathwing was destroyed or driven from the world for good. The black dragonflight remains a scourge across Azeroth, led by his cunning brood, including his daughter Onyxia and son nefarian. Black drakes manipulate mortal politics and terrorize the land from mountain lairs. The scars of the black Aspect's ancient treachery run deep. Travelers crossing craggy wastelands or descending into deep tunnels still fear the Great Dragon may stir.

npc:deino.text: Deino. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, Deino guides Horde mages in their studies. She teaches them to master arcane and elemental forces, then sends seasoned spellcasters across Kalimdor to study ancient magic and seek distant tutors. Deino trains Horde mages on raised platforms in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits. Totems, huts, and quiet waters surround her place of teaching. Troll spellcasters honor spiritual traditions as they master the arcane. Deino follows this path alongside fellow instructors Enyo and Pephredo. Deino sends promising mages beyond Durotar to study arcane mysteries. In Ashenvale's corrupted wilds, they gather tainted Waters of Xavian and enchanted hair from the Laughing Sisters. When a student's skill outgrows Orgrimmar's teaching, Deino sends them to remote masters. One is Tabetha, a hermit sorceress in Dustwallow's swamplands.

npc:demisette-cloyce.text: Demisette Cloyce. Beneath Stormwind's Slaughtered Lamb, Demisette Cloyce teaches warlocks in secret. She guides students in fel magic and sends the ready to learn from other summoners. Warlocks gather in the cellar beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. The city's authorities uphold order and the Holy Light, while Demisette Cloyce lives in the catacombs below. There, she teaches those willing to study forbidden arts. She warns that dark energies corrupt only those who lack the discipline to master them. When warlocks have gained enough mastery, Demisette guides them beyond Stormwind. She connects them with summoners such as Menara Voidrender in the Barrens. There, they can seek potent artifacts and learn to bind formidable fel steeds.

npc:deputy-feldon.text: Deputy Feldon. At the road south of the Great Lakeshire Bridge, Deputy Feldon keeps a nervous watch as gnolls creep toward Lakeshire. Deputy Feldon guards the road south of the Lakeshire bridge, a route needed for trade and travel. Blackrock orcs press from the north as gnoll packs overrun the southern hills, leaving the town guard stretched thin. Feldon cannot abandon his post without weakening Lakeshire's perimeter. He relies on passing adventurers to drive the gnolls back before they cut the town off.

npc:deputy-rainer.text:
Deputy Rainer. At Westbrook Garrison, Deputy Rainer holds Elwynn's western border against threats from Westfall. The Stormwind Army officer coordinates the local defense, though reinforcements have not arrived. Westbrook Garrison guards Elwynn Forest's western edge, where the road crosses into Westfall. Political paralysis in Stormwind City leaves much of the army abroad or caught in bureaucracy, and border posts like this one lack troops. Deputy Rainer organizes the defense outside the tower with the few forces at hand.

Riverpaw gnolls and wandering thieves threaten the local roads. Rainer depends on passing travelers and mercenary adventurers to keep the forest trails secure. Deputy Rainer watches for the Riverpaw pack and warns travelers about Hogger, the infamous gnoll chieftain. He also carries word of the troubled lands beyond the river. The chaos at Elwynn's border begins in Westfall's lawless farmlands, so he sends capable volunteers across the border to Gryan Stoutmantle and the struggling People's Militia.

npc:dirge-quikcleave.text: Dirge Quikcleave. Inside Gadgetzan's inn, Dirge Quikcleave welcomes travelers with food and drink. This goblin calls himself Azeroth's greatest living culinary artist, and chefs come to him when they are ready for artisan cooking. In dusty Gadgetzan, Dirge Quikcleave serves food and drink to travelers crossing the Tanaris sands. He claims to be Azeroth's greatest living culinary artist, though his kitchen stands in a frontier tavern. When city cooking lessons are spent, trainers send their most promising students to him. His demanding recipes call for rare ingredients, from giant clam meat and eggs for his Clamlette creations to beasts from distant shores. Dirge Quikcleave brings a gourmand's bravado and a goblin's eye for business to his work. Across Kalimdor, he keeps company with eccentric figures and pursues dangerous culinary ventures. Those who bring him fierce beast cuts can receive hearty recipes for champions facing perilous journeys. The monstrous chimaeroks of Feralas's Isle of Dread provide one such ingredient. Dirge's private dealings are best left unquestioned.

npc:doan-karhan.text: Doan Karhan. In the southern Barrens, Doan Karhan pursues dangerous studies far from Alliance lands. The human scholar lives alone, studying the Burning Legion’s demonic artifacts and seeking knowledge of the Orb of Soran'ruk. Doan Karhan keeps a solitary camp in the southern Barrens, far from the Alliance’s settled lands. He withdrew into the wilderness so he could study dangerous demonic relics without disturbance. He knows much about powerful fel vessels and possesses the Orb of Zargain. Yet his thoughts are fixed on the legendary Orb of Soran'ruk. Warlocks come to him for knowledge of artifact crafting and dark rituals.

npc:doctor-gregory-victor.text: Doctor Gregory Victor. At Hammerfall, Doctor Gregory Victor tends the Horde’s wounded and trains medics for the fighting in the Arathi Highlands. Renowned as its premier trauma physician, he teaches advanced triage and battlefield first aid. Doctor Gregory Victor treats the Horde’s wounded at Hammerfall, in the contested Arathi Highlands. Though many distrust Forsaken apothecaries, he uses surgery instead of blighted alchemy on soldiers hurt by Syndicate brigands, Boulderfist ogres, and Alliance forces. Hammerfall is the Horde’s main proving ground for field medics, and Victor demands speed and care when the most critical patients are under pressure.

npc:doctor-gustaf-vanhowzen.text: Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen. At Foothold Citadel, Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen directs Theramore’s medical care. He trains healers and tests seasoned medics in field triage and bandage work. On Foothold Citadel’s ground floor, Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen tends the forces of Lady Jaina Proudmoore and trains Theramore’s frontline healers. Dustwallow Marsh makes their work harsh, so VanHowzen demands skill under pressure. Experienced medics face his demanding triage test and must judge which wounds need care first.

npc:donova-snowden.text: Donova Snowden. Beside Frostfire Hot Springs, Donova Snowden studies Winterspring’s strange warmth and the Winterfall furbolgs’ growing corruption. She camps in the bitter cold, far from most travelers in Everlook. Donova Snowden camps in the frozen wilds near Frostfire Hot Springs, while most travelers stay in Everlook. She studies heat rising through the permafrost and dark influences spreading among Winterspring’s native wildlife. Practical and determined, she calls on passing adventurers from both the Alliance and the Horde to gather samples and help curb local threats.

npc:donyal-tovald.text: Donyal Tovald. In Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald tends the Royal Library’s historical works. Young King Anduin Wrynn sponsors his work to preserve and copy books for wider public use. Donyal Tovald tends the Royal Library in Stormwind Keep. Its historical accounts, scrolls, and scholarly volumes chiefly serve the nobility and royal court. Young King Anduin Wrynn has sponsored an effort to share that knowledge with ordinary citizens. So Tovald preserves and copies the texts, keeping the Alliance’s lessons and triumphs recorded amid the kingdom’s political troubles.

npc:doomsayer-wiserunner.text: Seer Wiserunner. At his cave northwest of Bloodhoof Village, Seer Wiserunner guides young tauren through sacred rites. The respected elder helps them seek spiritual wisdom in Mulgore. Seer Wiserunner guides young tauren through their ancestral rites. After their first trials of strength and vision, they seek his counsel. He interprets visions of the Earth Mother and teaches them to honor their forebears. His wisdom helps bind Mulgore’s scattered nomadic tribes into one community.

npc:doras.text: Doras. Above Orgrimmar, Doras sends wind riders across Kalimdor. He oversees the capital's wyverns, carrying couriers, scouts, and travelers to distant places. Doras tends the wind riders on a wooden platform above the Valley of Strength. Since the Horde settled in Durotar, these clever, leathery-winged beasts have carried messages and travelers across Kalimdor. Doras pairs resting mounts with riders and sees that important messages and reinforcements reach distant outposts. Their routes lead to the Crossroads and Thunder Bluff, and to settlements deep in Ashenvale or Dustwallow Marsh.

npc:doren.text: Doren. At the Rebel Camp, Doren leads soldiers who have turned against Colonel Kurzen. They once served on Stormwind's expedition and now seek the cause of his madness. Lieutenant Doren leads the Rebel Camp beside the road in Stranglethorn Vale. He came south under Stormwind's banner with Colonel Kurzen on an expedition to establish a foothold in the jungle. But Kurzen and his inner circle grew erratic and violent. Doren would not follow them into madness, so he and loyal soldiers broke ranks and fled north.
