They chose defection over service to a mad commander.

npc:drum-fel.text: Drum Fel. At Hammerfall, Drum Fel directs the Horde’s fight to hold Arathi against trolls, ogres, and human remnants. With his wife Korin, he seeks a lasting foothold for the Horde in the region. Drum Fel commands Hammerfall’s defenses and leads the Horde’s push into Arathi. From this fortified refuge, he faces rival factions on every side. The Witherbark forest trolls and Boulderfist ogres hold Boulder'gor and Boulderfist Hall. Drum knows Hammerfall cannot thrive in isolation, so their strength must be broken. He sends veteran champions into hostile territory to disrupt these threats before they can strike the encampment.

npc:drusilla-la-salle.text: Drusilla La Salle. Outside Northshire Abbey, Drusilla La Salle teaches warlocks in the graveyard. The human trainer guides new spellcasters in shadow and summoning, beyond the Holy Order’s reach. When forbidden knowledge leaves the abbey, she moves to claim it. Drusilla La Salle teaches novice warlocks among the headstones outside Northshire Abbey. Within, paladins and priests practice beneath stained glass. Warlocks keep to society’s edges because Stormwind forbids demonology and fel magic. Recruits receive tainted correspondence, then Drusilla teaches them to wield shadow without drawing the abbey authorities’ immediate anger.

npc:duke-hydraxis.text:
Duke Hydraxis. On a wave-battered islet off Azshara, Duke Hydraxis calls mortals to battle ancient elemental rivals. He leads the Hydraxian Waterlords in service to Neptulon the Tidehunter, with Ragnaros the Firelord his chief foe. Duke Hydraxis watches elemental turmoil from a rock northeast of the Ravencrest Monument in Azshara. As emissary of the Hydraxian Waterlords, he acts with purpose amid Azeroth’s hostile and chaotic elementals. He serves Neptulon the Tidehunter and holds water to be the purest and most essential primal force. Now he seeks champions to shift the balance of elemental warfare. Duke Hydraxis wages his chief campaign against the blazing hosts of Ragnaros the Firelord. He sees the advance of fiery elementals as a blight that must be extinguished.

Before he trusts mortals with the means to challenge Ragnaros’s stronghold in the Molten Core, they must prove their strength, resilience, and loyalty by slaying hostile elementals across the continents. Those who prove worthy receive the sea’s blessings and the means to douse the sacred flames guarding the Firelord’s domain.

npc:durnan-furcutter.text: Durnan Furcutter. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Durnan Furcutter outfits young dwarves and gnomes for the mountain cold. He sells light clothing and leather goods from inside the settlement. Inside Anvilmar, young dwarves and exiled gnomes prove themselves. Some need more freedom of movement than heavy iron allows. Durnan Furcutter sells light, pliable layers to scouts, rogues, and spellcasters who want to stay agile in Dun Morogh's bitter winds. Near the hearth, he offers everyday tailoring and stitched leather. He claims his stock is the finest in the valley. Durnan likes a strong drink as much as an honest trade. To warm himself against the freezing draft, he orders steaming mugs of Scalding Mornbrew from Nori Pridedrift, who sells the brew piping hot across Coldridge Valley. Adventurers hurrying through the valley with errands often bring Durnan a hot mug before it cools. Then they carry the empty back to Nori.

npc:ebru.text:
Ebru. Above the Wailing Caverns, Ebru watches Naralex's dream turn to nightmare. A night elf druid and one of his few uncorrupted disciples, she calls on travelers to enter the depths and cull the mutated horrors born of the Nightmare. Ebru keeps watch from a camp inside the cavernous skull above the Wailing Caverns' entrance. Most of Naralex's followers have fallen to the emerald corruption spreading through the caverns, but she escaped it.

Naralex hoped to draw on underground springs and make the arid Barrens a woodland. His plan has gone horribly wrong, and Ebru sees that dream become a nightmare. She urges willing travelers into the depths to kill the growing number of deviate beasts threatening the surrounding plains.

npc:einar-stonegrip.text:
Einar Stonegrip. Along the Wetlands crossroads, Einar Stonegrip stays by the road and sends his goods to town with travelers. He avoids Menethil Harbor, where his estranged wife lives. Einar Stonegrip hunts crocolisks where the Wetlands roads meet. From there, the roads lead to Dun Algaz, Dun Modr, and Menethil Harbor. He sells the sturdy hides to leatherworkers and merchants along the coast.

Einar is rugged enough to wrestle reptiles from the mire, but he and his wife, Sida, have fallen bitterly out. He stays on the road and asks travelers to carry his bundles of skins to his trading partner, James Halloran. He will not enter Menethil Harbor himself.

npc:elanaria.text: Elanaria. On the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, Elanaria prepares fighters for danger across Kalimdor. She tests their strength against foes such as Vorlus Vilehoof and the Shade of Elura. Elanaria trains warriors on Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace. Since the night elves joined the Grand Alliance, she has guided Sentinels and fighters from other peoples through the dangers facing their lands. Elanaria demands discipline, endurance, and strength proven in battle. She sends seasoned fighters after threats in Teldrassil and Darkshore, including the satyr Vorlus Vilehoof and the Shade of Elura. She also works with Smith Mathiel so proven warriors can be armed for war.

npc:elder-bloodhoof.text: Elder Bloodhoof. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Bloodhoof rests just north of Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. The Bloodhoof tribe honors him as a guardian spirit of its ancestors. Near Bloodhoof Village, Elder Bloodhoof watches over his people. The tauren honor him as a spirit bound to their lineage and the plains of Mulgore. During the Lunar Festival, respectful travelers seek his wisdom and receive his blessings. Through him, the guidance of dead chieftains and tribal forebears remains close to the Bloodhoof tribe.

npc:elder-bronzebeard.text:
Elder Bronzebeard. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Bronzebeard appears in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. His name is the name of the clan that rules the city, and his earthen form recalls the dwarves' stone-born ancestors. Near the pool in Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Elder Bronzebeard appears in the shape of an earthen. The Titans forged the ancient earthen from living stone before they became creatures of flesh. Dwarven scholars and explorers are only beginning to uncover their origins through excavations across Khaz Modan and beyond.

Elder Bronzebeard bears the name of the ruling clan, and his form suggests he is a direct ancestor of the Bronzebeards. His spirit shows how far his stone-born descendants have changed.

npc:elder-darkcore.text: Elder Darkcore. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Darkcore keeps watch in the throne room above the Undercity. He honors the world's ancestors and blesses travelers who come to pay their respects. Elder Darkcore is one of the ancient elders who appear across Azeroth during the Lunar Festival, sharing their wisdom with travelers. The throne room’s blood-stained floor marks the place where King Terenas Menethil II fell. Visitors who pay their respects there receive a Coin of Ancestry.

npc:elder-goldwell.text: Elder Goldwell. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Goldwell appears near Kharanos. The ancient earthen spirit recalls the beginnings of modern dwarven civilization. Near Kharanos, Elder Goldwell watches over the snowy slopes as a translucent earthen spirit. His stony form recalls the Titan-forged ancestors of the Bronzebeard clan. During the ancestor celebrations, travelers can honor that heritage in his presence.

npc:elder-graveborn.text: Elder Graveborn. Near Brill, Elder Graveborn welcomes travelers for the Lunar Festival. This ancestral spirit honors them and directs pilgrims to other elders across northern Lordaeron. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Graveborn greets travelers just southeast of Brill. The spectral elder stands in the haunted woods of Tirisfal Glades, with the Forsaken town nearby. Though the kingdom is troubled, Graveborn offers pilgrims peaceful greetings and ancestral wisdom. He also directs them to spirits in the Undercity, the Sepulcher, and across the Plaguelands.

npc:elder-morningdew.text: Elder Morningdew. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Morningdew greets travelers in Thousand Needles. She offers ancestral wisdom and blessings to those who honor her. In Thousand Needles, Elder Morningdew greets pilgrims during the Lunar Festival as an honored ancestor. Across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, revered spirits gather to celebrate wisdom, legacy, and peace. She belongs to neither faction and takes no part in mortal conflicts. Travelers who seek her counsel and show respect receive her blessing and a Coin of Ancestry.

npc:elder-obsidian.text: Elder Obsidian. At the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Elder Obsidian greets travelers during the Lunar Festival. The ancient earthen spirit offers wisdom and blessings among graves claimed by the Forsaken. Elder Obsidian welcomes travelers to the Sepulcher during the Lunar Festival. His earthen spirit brings Azeroth's ancient heritage to Silverpine Forest. The Forsaken hold the nearby crypts, and feral worgen menace the forest. Yet he greets wayfarers of every allegiance in peace, offering a Coin of Ancestry and ancient blessings to those who seek his wisdom.

npc:elder-runetotem.text: Elder Runetotem. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Runetotem appears outside Razor Hill in Durotar. The tauren spirit offers travelers wisdom and a blessing. Elder Runetotem appears beside Razor Hill, far from Mulgore's grassy plains and sacred burial grounds. Her presence brings the ancient traditions of the Shu'halo to the Horde's home along the Great Sea. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of great leaders, shamans, and heroes appear throughout the world to commune with the living. Elder Runetotem bears a name from a line that reveres the Earth Mother and seeks spiritual communion. Travelers who honor her receive ancestral tokens and her blessing.

npc:elder-skyseer.text: Elder Skyseer. At Freewind Post, Elder Skyseer watches over travelers as an ancestor beyond the mortal world. His spirit remains tied to the resting grounds of his people. High above Thousand Needles, Elder Skyseer watches over Freewind Post from its mesa. Tauren cross perilous bridges and wooden platforms there, while he keeps watch beyond the mortal veil. Travelers who honor old traditions may receive his blessings and seek the wisdom of past generations. Elder Skyseer’s spirit often appears among the wind-carved needles. He belongs to the line of tauren ancestors honored on Mulgore’s sacred soil, where the ancestral spirits of Red Rocks watch over the tribes. Through remembrance and ritual, those ancestors guide future generations. His presence shows how thin the veil remains between the living and the dead.

npc:elder-starweave.text:
Elder Starweave. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Starweave rests in Auberdine as a night elf ancestral spirit. Along Darkshore’s coast, she shares ancient wisdom with pilgrims. In Auberdine, Elder Starweave appears as an ethereal shade among the coastal dwellings. The Cenarion Circle and the peoples of Kalimdor honor her as an ancestor. Travelers pass through the port on their way inland or across the sea, yet those who pause before her receive an ancestral blessing.

Elder Starweave speaks of the stars. Their paths in this age differ from those of old, yet she sees them as beacons of hope and fortitude for generations to come.

npc:eleanor-shackleton.text: Eleanor Shackleton. In the woods southwest of Brill, Eleanor Shackleton teaches travelers to live off Tirisfal's blighted land. This Forsaken outdoorswoman camps away from town and the Undercity. Pierce Shackleton and Samantha Shackleton share her surname, though their kinship is unknown. Eleanor Shackleton camps in the haunted woods southwest of Brill, away from the Undercity. Newly awakened Forsaken often go to those settlements, but Eleanor teaches travelers to live off Tirisfal's blighted land. She shows them how to make camps, gather firewood, and keep up their trade crafts while roaming far from civilization's fires and kitchens. Eleanor Shackleton shares her surname with Pierce Shackleton and Samantha Shackleton, who live in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. For an undead person, a family name may be the only tether to mortal life in the shattered remnants of Lordaeron. Whether the three are close kin or share only common ancestry, each serves the Forsaken in a different way across the blighted kingdom.

npc:elu.text: Elu. At Freewind Post, Elu tends the mounts and waits to begin wind rider training. He hopes to fly and asks Horde travelers to bring back wild wyvern eggs from nearby roosts. At Freewind Post, Elu cares for the aerial mounts and dreams of flying. The young tauren hopes to join the master wind riders who patrol Kalimdor’s mesas. Before training begins, he must prove himself by bringing fresh wyvern stock to the roost. So he sends capable travelers to Highperch for intact eggs from the fierce wild wyverns nesting there.

npc:eva-sarkhoff.text:
Eva Sarkhoff. Outside Scholomance, Eva Sarkhoff lingers with Lucien, her husband, and seeks vengeance for their deaths. Once head maid to House Barov, she asks mortals to destroy their cursed remains. For decades, Eva served as head maid to the wealthy Barov family at Caer Darrow. Her husband Lucien was the family butler. As the Barovs feared age and the loss of their vast wealth, they made a disastrous pact with Kel'Thuzad. They gradually gave their manor to the young Cult of the Damned, which turned it into Scholomance, a hidden school of necromancy.

Eva and Lucien hid in the keep's corridors for six months. They scavenged food as cultists and monstrosities took over their home.

npc:falfindel-waywarder.text: Falfindel Waywarder. At Thalanaar, Falfindel Waywarder keeps watch over the border between Feralas and Thousand Needles. The night elf druid works to heal corrupted lands and guard Kalimdor’s southern wilderness. Travelers from Stonetalon or the Barrens often seek his aid to restore balance to the wild. Falfindel Waywarder stands at Thalanaar, the night elf outpost on the edge of Feralas. The outpost marks the passage from forest to mesas and salt plains. Travelers who have crossed far across the continent greet him there. From this post, he watches for local threats and dangers to lands across Kalimdor. Falfindel Waywarder watches from the south, but the ruin of the Charred Vale in Stonetalon Mountains weighs on him. Dark sorcery and fire scarred that wilderness. When adventurers bring aid for its recovery, he calls on the forest spirits. Falfindel summons swarms of wisps and sends them north to mend the scorched earth. Falfindel Waywarder also watches the region around Thalanaar, including the quilboar dens of Razorfen Kraul. He studies recovered journals and gathers word of quilboar leaders. His watch helps the Alliance understand the dangers threatening the passes between Feralas and the central deserts.

npc:falla-sagewind.text: Falla Sagewind. On a crag above the Barrens, Falla Sagewind watches for signs of trouble. Her camp lies between the Crossroads and the Lushwater Oasis, where she studies changes in nature and magic. Southwest of the Crossroads, Falla Sagewind keeps camp on a secluded summit above the Barrens trails. From there, she watches the savanna and its changing wildlife. She also studies corruption rising from fissures beneath the Wailing Caverns. Her vigil keeps her apart from daily trade at the Crossroads, yet her attention stays on the land's spirits and wounds.

npc:fallen-hero-of-the-horde.text:
Fallen Hero of the Horde. At the southern road from the Swamp of Sorrows, the Fallen Hero of the Horde keeps watch. Regret and dishonor bind him there. He warns travelers of the Blasted Lands and seeks champions to free his tortured soldiers from demonic bondage. In life, the orc warrior was a celebrated champion. He led a handpicked regiment sent to investigate the Blasted Lands and report on the Burning Legion. But his dispatch never arrived. The courier bound for Stonard was ambushed and slain by the Swamp Talker and his murlocs.

Without orders or reinforcements, the commander marched south into the shattered wastes to face the growing darkness. It was a fatal choice. Demonic forces overwhelmed his army, scattering and capturing his soldiers. Razelikh the Defiler then subjected them to horrific torment.

npc:farmer-furlbrow.text:
Farmer Furlbrow. Near the Jansen Stead, Farmer Furlbrow and his wife, Verna, are stranded beside their broken wagon. Driven from their northern Westfall farm by the Defias Brotherhood, they hope to reach Elwynn Forest. The Furlbrows salvaged what they could and set out for Elwynn Forest. Theodore urged neighbors like Farmer Saldean to leave as well. Now bandits and wild beasts threaten them on the road.

Verna tends their horse, Old Blanchy, while Theodore keeps watch. He hopes to recover the pocket watch Verna's father gave him on their wedding day. He also wants to warn Sentinel Hill about the approaching bandits.

npc:farmer-saldean.text:
Farmer Saldean. At Saldean's Farm in central Westfall, Farmer Saldean and his wife, Salma, keep working troubled fields. Other farmers flee or give up, but he faces rogue harvest golems and growing banditry. Farmer Saldean remembers Westfall before its prosperity crumbled. Overgrown fields, rampaging mechanical harvest watchers, and predatory bandits now surround his farm. Yet he refuses to yield his land.

Other homesteaders have abandoned their acres or turned to thievery. Saldean and his wife, Salma, stay to harvest what little grain they can. He asks wandering adventurers to destroy the rogue Harvest Watchers in his fields and his neighbors' fields, so he can clear the soil for planting. Between Sentinel Hill and the northern bridge, Saldean's defense of his homestead helps keep civilian life going. He remains tied to the People's Militia despite the hard times. Once his immediate troubles are settled, he sends able-bodied travelers to Gryan Stoutmantle.

Clearing the wild harvest reapers can give his farm only a temporary reprieve. The lawlessness strangling the countryside still has to be dealt with.

npc:feegly-the-exiled.text: Feegly the Exiled. In the southern Barrens, Feegly the Exiled keeps to himself near the Bael Modan excavation. Once praised as one of its finest diggers, he was driven away by General Twinbraid after claiming an uncovered relic’s power.

npc:feero-ironhand.text: Feero Ironhand. At Maestra's Post, Feero Ironhand keeps watch over the road from Darkshore into Ashenvale. He works with Delgren the Purifier against the Cult of the Dark Strand. Maestra's Post guards the road south from Darkshore into Ashenvale. Feero Ironhand keeps communication and trade with Auberdine moving while he watches the surrounding woods. He and Delgren the Purifier oppose the Cult of the Dark Strand. Cultists and forest predators threaten the route between Darnassus's supply lines and Ashenvale's front lines.

npc:fel-zerul.text: Fel'zerul. At Stonard, Fel'zerul watches the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar for danger. Thrall has sent him to learn what stirs there. From Stonard, Fel'zerul watches the corruption around the Pool of Tears and the submerged Temple of Atal'Hakkar. Thrall's Horde is wary of dark arts, yet the Warchief knows their students can help uncover the dangers they hold. So Fel'zerul directs adventurers to recover artifacts and investigate the exiled Atal'ai trolls. He seeks to learn what evil stirs beneath the waters before it threatens the Horde's southern outpost.

npc:felgur-twocuts.text: Felgur Twocuts. At Ghost Walker Post, Felgur Twocuts watches the Horde’s struggle with Desolace’s centaur clans. At Ghost Walker Post in central Desolace, Felgur Twocuts keeps watch and spares little for pleasantries. As a forward scout for the Horde, he weighs the dangers facing travelers and settlers heading west through the mountains. The Kolkar centaur are foremost among them. Felgur directs Horde champions against the local centaur chieftains. He also sends them to claim bounties on tribes that threaten to overrun the region. Those seeking to secure the Horde’s foothold in Desolace can turn to him.

npc:felix-whindlebolt.text:
Felix Whindlebolt. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Felix Whindlebolt seeks shelter after fleeing Gnomeregan's radiation. Frostmane trolls have taken his belongings. Felix Whindlebolt fled Gnomeregan when radiation flooded the city. In the rush, he left his belongings and tools behind.

Frostmane ice trolls carried his chest, box and bucket of bolts to their camps southwest of Anvilmar. Without his gear, Felix depends on travelers to retrieve it.

npc:field-marshal-snowfall.text: Field Marshal Snowfall. In Ironforge's Military Ward, Field Marshal Snowfall directs the Alliance's preparations against the silithid threat in Silithus. The dwarven officer oversees the supplies gathered for the coming war and rewards those who aid the realm. From Ironforge's Military Ward, Field Marshal Snowfall directs the Alliance's war preparations. He sees the coming conflict as more than a border skirmish. It is a fight against an ancient enemy hostile to all creations of the Titans. Volunteers gather bandages, metal bars, leathers, herbs, and rations in great numbers. Snowfall oversees these stores so Alliance forces can be armed, armored, and fed when the march south to Silithus begins. Blacksmiths, gatherers, cooks, and soldiers across Alliance lands all have a part in preparing for war. Snowfall tracks their effort, accepts commendation signets, and offers supply requisitions to volunteers. Once both factions have gathered the required supplies, the stores are packed and hauled south to Cenarion Hold. From there, the grand assault will target the qiraji swarms and the Old God behind the Scarab Wall.

npc:field-marshal-stonebridge.text: Field Marshal Stonebridge. At Stormwind's gates, Field Marshal Stonebridge helps guard the capital with General Marcus Jonathan. She also receives reports and trophies after great victories. At Stormwind's main gates, Field Marshal Stonebridge watches the eastern archway into the Valley of Heroes. A senior Grand Alliance officer, she works closely with General Marcus Jonathan. Defenders, travelers, and returning champions pass beneath her post. If danger breaks through the outer defenses, she is ready to organize the garrison. Field Marshal Stonebridge receives reports and spoils from campaigns against great threats to the kingdom. Senior commanders rely on officers like her to confirm important intelligence and mark victories in the field. Among them are victories over warlords and monsters in the crags of Blackrock Mountain.

npc:fizzle-brassbolts.text: Fizzle Brassbolts. At the Mirage Raceway, Fizzle Brassbolts works on the salt flats of Thousand Needles. He and Pozzik founded the raceway to pit gnomish precision against goblin ingenuity in rocket car races. Fizzle seeks parts, fuel, and desert reagents for his team. Fizzle Brassbolts came to the Shimmering Flats to prove gnomish craftsmanship superior to goblin tinkering. With the goblin engineer Pozzik, he laid out the Mirage Raceway. Race cars, pit crews, and spectators soon filled the basin. The dry salt beds keep Fizzle improvising. He tests mixtures made with local creature venom and contracts travelers to find replacement mechanical parts. His aim is to keep his driver's wheels turning faster than any goblin contraption.

npc:fleet-master-seahorn.text: Fleet Master Seahorn. From Booty Bay, Fleet Master Seahorn guards the harbor against the Bloodsail Buccaneers. The seasoned tauren commands the Blackwater Raiders from the Salty Sailor Tavern, beside Baron Revilgaz. Fleet Master Seahorn commands the Blackwater Raiders from the Salty Sailor Tavern. Though many tauren across Kalimdor live on the plains, Seahorn chose the sea and wears pirate regalia. The Raiders serve as the Steamwheedle Cartel's private navy in Stranglethorn Vale. From his post above Booty Bay, Seahorn works with Baron Revilgaz to direct shipping routes, crew deployments, and coastal defenses for a port both lawless and tightly managed. Seahorn oversees trade and salvage ventures across the Eastern Kingdoms. Near Faldir's Cove on the Arathi coast, he coordinates the recovery of sunken treasures and works with salvage divers to secure elven relics. He also keeps Revilgaz informed of profitable opportunities in town, including competitive angling and local trade. These ventures help fund the Blackwater fleet and keep it ahead of rivals.

npc:foggy-mackreel.text: Foggy MacKreel. On the broken Thandol Span, Foggy MacKreel is stranded above a dizzying drop with a moonshine delivery bound for Southshore on his mind. Foggy MacKreel waits on broken pylons beneath the Thandol Span, calm on his dangerous perch. Dark Iron sabotage and war damage shattered the bridge between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands. Rescue can wait; MacKreel wants his potent moonshine delivered to the patrons of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. So he hires passing travelers nimble enough to reach his ledge and finish the delivery.

npc:foreman-stonebrow.text: Foreman Stonebrow. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, Foreman Stonebrow faces a trogg attack that has driven miners from the pits. He speaks for the Miners' League and needs help defending the excavation. Foreman Stonebrow directs the Miners' League's work at Gol'Bolar Quarry, east of Kharanos. Deep digging broke into trogg burrows beneath the quarry. The creatures swarmed the pits and drove miners from their tools. Stonebrow remains at the quarry rim, seeking travelers willing to push the troggs back.

npc:foreman-thazz-ril.text: Foreman Thazz'ril. In the Valley of Trials, Foreman Thazz'ril keeps the peons at work. Crews gather what the encampment and young warriors need, but sleepers and nearby cultists test his patience. In the Valley of Trials, Foreman Thazz'ril directs peons as they chop lumber and gather materials for the encampment and young warriors. Durotar's harsh red rock demands steady labor, but the peons often nap beneath the desert sun. So Thazz'ril sends newly arrived recruits to rouse them with his blackjack and keep construction moving. Thazz'ril was scouting the Burning Blade Coven for mineral resources when dark cultists drove him to flee. In his haste, he left behind his treasured enchanted pick. Warlocks and their demonic minions now gather in the cave. Too cautious to retrieve it himself, Thazz'ril depends on young Horde aspirants to venture into the depths and bring it back.

npc:foreman-thistlenettle.text: Foreman Thistlenettle. Below the Deadmines, Foreman Thistlenettle's crew lies trapped beneath Moonbrook. He served both the Miners' League and the Explorers' League, and died with his miners when the tunnels fell in. Now he walks again as a ghoul, his guild badge still with him.

npc:frahun-shadewhisper.text: Frahun Shadewhisper. At Aldrassil in Shadowglen, Frahun Shadewhisper trains new scouts and rogues. He teaches stealth, agility, and covert strikes. Erion Shadewhisper trains rogues in Darnassus, and shares his family name. At Aldrassil in Teldrassil, Frahun Shadewhisper teaches new rogues concealment and bladecraft. Night elf society honors priests, sentinels, and druids, yet scouts and infiltrators also help guard the World Tree's boughs. Recruits bring Frahun an encrypted sigil. He weighs their promise and guides their first steps in the craft.

npc:furl-scornbrow.text: Furl Scornbrow. Northwest of Razor Hill, Furl Scornbrow keeps watch over Durotar. Too old for the front lines, he makes sturdy packs for young travelers. From a wooden tower northwest of Razor Hill, Furl Scornbrow watches Durotar’s central plains. In the tense days after Orgrimmar was founded, sentries like him sounded their horns against hostile quilboar, centaur, and Kul Tiras interlopers. Since then, Durotar has grown more stable, and Razor Hill has secured its borders. Emergencies come less often, leaving Furl long, quiet hours at his post. Furl says his old bones and fading strength keep him from fighting. Yet an orc does not easily surrender their purpose. He puts his hands to work making canvas sacks and packs for fresh recruits who carry supplies. In exchange for coarse thread and practical materials, he equips green adventurers setting out to prove their worth to the Horde.

npc:gaerolas-talvethren.text: Gaerolas Talvethren. At Starbreeze Village, Gaerolas Talvethren keeps watch over the Sleeping druids as corruption spreads through Teldrassil. He seeks aid against aggressive furbolgs. At Starbreeze Village, Gaerolas Talvethren watches over the Sleeping druids. They slumber in communion with the Emerald Dream. Now unnatural corruption spreads through the forest, and his watch grows uneasy as Teldrassil is unsettled. Gaerolas calls on travelers to drive back the Gnarlpine furbolgs. Their minds have turned to madness and savagery. He hopes to uncover the taint spreading from their shamans and the roots of their distress. What sanctity remains in eastern Teldrassil is at stake.

npc:galgar.text: Galgar. Near the Den in the Valley of Trials, Galgar feeds young Horde recruits. He asks newcomers to gather wild cactus apples for his Cactus Apple Surprise. Galgar cooks by the Den's fire in the Valley of Trials. He feeds young orcs and trolls through their first rites of passage. Durotar is a dry, harsh red wasteland, so food must be found across the land. Galgar sends novice warriors to gather ripe cactus fruit, testing their attention and resilience while stocking his kitchen. Galgar calls his specialty Cactus Apple Surprise. He says gathering spiny desert fruit is a simple way to ease fresh recruits into adventuring. The dish still feeds hungry trainees. Every Horde warrior begins somewhere, and Galgar starts them by foraging in the desert.

npc:gar-thok.text:
Gar'Thok. At Razor Hill, Gar'Thok directs recruits from the Valley of Trials as they help secure Durotar. The veteran orc warrior survived the Kul Tiras landings on Durotar's coast. Now he coordinates the defense against human encroachers and native threats. After the Third War, Gar'Thok marched to Durotar under Warchief Thrall. In the first days of building the new homeland, he served as a lieutenant under Nazgrel.

When Rexxar, the half-ogre wanderer, arrived in Durotar, Gar'Thok warned him that quilboar were raiding the settlement's perimeter. He enlisted the beastmaster to protect the fragile new settlement. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's Kul Tiras fleet landed on Durotar's eastern shores, and Gar'Thok's resolve was tested. At an outlying watch post, he saw naval marines overwhelm and slaughter his garrison. His forces were decimated, but Gar'Thok survived.

The surprise assault left him vigilant. Surviving marines still occupy Tiragarde Keep and the coastal shipwrecks. From Razor Hill's barracks, Gar'Thok oversees the defense of central Durotar. He sends emerging Horde warriors, shamans, and scouts to drive out hostile Kul Tiran remnants, reclaim salvaged supplies, and recover military orders left in the coastal ruins.

Durotar's safety is far from assured. Gar'Thok keeps pressure on those who challenge the Horde's right to this soil.

npc:gart-mistrunner.text: Gart Mistrunner. At Camp Narache, Gart Mistrunner teaches new tauren their first rites of nature magic on the Red Cloud Mesa. At Camp Narache, Gart Mistrunner guides the Shu'halo as they return to their ancient druidic path. New tauren druids come to him when they take their first steps on the Red Cloud Mesa, often carrying a note that commends them to his care. Gart teaches them to commune with the natural world. Through that bond, they draw on nature's healing power and Mu'sha's lunar light to mend allies and strike at threats to the land.

npc:gath-ilzogg.text: Gath'Ilzogg. In the Redridge Mountains, Gath'Ilzogg commands Stonewatch Keep and sends raids toward Lakeshire. Magistrate Solomon has set a bounty on the Blackrock warlord. Gath'Ilzogg came north from the Burning Steppes to claim Redridge for the Blackrock clan. With the foul sorcery of Morganth, a renegade human warlock, his warband battered Stonewatch Keep's defenders and took the heights above the region. From the fortress, he directs raids through the valleys and toward Lakeshire's bridge, pressing the human settlement. Elite Blackrock guards and Singe, a vicious black dragon whelp, remain close at his side.

npc:gazin-tenorm.text: Gazin Tenorm. Near the altar in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Gazin Tenorm has returned from a dangerous scouting mission in Elwynn Forest. Gazin Tenorm remains in the Cathedral of Light, but his thoughts are in Elwynn Forest. He and his close friend Henze Faulk went into the woods to gather proof of the Defias Brotherhood's movements for the royal court. Defias forces ambushed them. Gazin escaped to Stormwind, while Henze was left in mortal danger. Now Gazin seeks a hero of the Light to help his companion.

npc:gelkak-gyromast.text:
Gelkak Gyromast. Along Mist's Edge in northern Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast waits for his mechanical first mate to work again. Threshadons sank his ship, leaving him stranded on the coast. West of the Ruins of Mathystra, Gelkak Gyromast is stranded on Darkshore's northern coast. The gnome calls himself captain and talks like an old sea dog. Threshadons sank his ship just offshore, and he washed up on the misty shore.

The key to his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, broke on the rocks. Crawlers, foreststriders and murlocs rummaging through the wreckage carried off its pieces.

npc:general-marcus-jonathan.text: General Marcus Jonathan. At Stormwind's gates, General Marcus Jonathan guards the capital and weighs pleas for aid from frontier settlements. He is a veteran of the Second War, commands Stormwind Defense, and oversees the garrison. General Marcus Jonathan commands Stormwind's defense from horseback in the Valley of Heroes. As the highest-ranking officer at the city gates, he is the capital's first line of defense. During the Second War, he fought beside soldiers such as Reginald Windsor under General Turalyon. Now he must guard the capital as frontier towns, including Lakeshire, make ever more desperate appeals for help.

npc:gerard-tiller.text: Gerard Tiller. At the Maclure Vineyards, Gerard Tiller tends the grounds and longs for spring water. Bring him a skin of it, and he offers shiny red apples. Gerard Tiller works outside the barn at the Maclure Vineyards, south of Goldshire. The vineyard is known for its grapes, and keeping the harvest going takes hard labor. His chores leave him thirsty, so he welcomes travelers who bring a skin of fresh spring water. In return, he gives them shiny red apples gathered from local orchards.

npc:gerrig-bonegrip.text: Gerrig Bonegrip. In Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern, Gerrig Bonegrip trades in strange texts and writings on dark rituals and ancient powers.

npc:gershala-nightwhisper.text: Gershala Nightwhisper. In Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper studies the harm magical corruption brings to elves. He fears the path taken by the high elves of Quel'Thalas, and examines cursed aquatic naga and demonic satyr for signs of what corruption does to mind and body. From Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper looks beyond Darkshore's coastal troubles to the danger he sees in Quel'Thalas. The high elves embrace perilous arcane practices and call themselves blood elves. Their example troubles him, so he seeks to learn what unchecked magic does to body and spirit. He sends seasoned Alliance adventurers into the submerged halls of Blackfathom Deeps to gather corrupted brain stems from the naga and satyr who dwell there. The naga and satyr brain stems interest Gershala because both races were once night elves. They yielded to Queen Azshara and demonic bargains, and became what they are now. Gershala studies the marks that millennia of demonic and abyssal energies left on their nervous systems. He hopes to find warnings or safeguards that could spare other elven kin a similar monstrous deformity.

npc:gilshalan-windwalker.text: Gilshalan Windwalker. At Aldrassil's roots in Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker studies the corruption spreading through Teldrassil. He begins with the Webwood spiders and their growing aggression. From the stone steps at Aldrassil's entrance, Gilshalan Windwalker watches over Shadowglen. Teldrassil was planted to restore the night elves' lost sanctuary and their harmony with nature. Yet signs of spiritual malaise appeared almost at once. Gilshalan studies how the corruption affects local beasts, beginning with the venomous spiders weaving webs nearby. North of Shadowglen, Gilshalan studies the Webwood spiders in Shadowthread Cave. Once part of the forest's balance, they have grown hostile and tainted. He sends young novices to gather venom sacs and intact eggs. Through these, he hopes to learn how the venom has changed and whether the corruption passes through generations or spreads from Teldrassil's soil.

npc:gilthares-firebough.text:
Gilthares Firebough. At Northwatch Hold, Gilthares Firebough waits in a tower as Theramore's captive. Once a deckhand on a moonshine run between Ratchet and Booty Bay, he looks for a chance to escape. Gilthares Firebough is held in a tower at Northwatch Hold. His ship carried illicit cargo between Ratchet and Booty Bay when Theramore's naval forces blasted it apart. Gilthares alone survived. Dragged ashore in chains, he was locked away.

He wears vivid red and has little love for the Alliance zealots who slaughtered his crew. Still, he cares little who helps him break free, so long as they can fight their way down from the ramparts.

npc:gnoarn.text: Gnoarn. In Ironforge, Gnoarn helps his scattered people find aid. After Gnomeregan fell, the exiled gnome made his home in Tinker Town and began directing travelers to fellow engineers and survivors. Troggs invaded Gnomeregan, and catastrophic radiation drove its people from the great underground city. The Bronzebeard dwarves gave Gnoarn refuge in Tinker Town. From there, he sends travelers to gnomes in need across Alliance lands, including the stranded pilot Bingles Blastenheimer in Loch Modan and the ambitious engineer Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind.

npc:godrick-farsan.text:
Godrick Farsan. In the Undercity’s Magic Quarter, Godrick Farsan aids Forsaken warlocks beside Carendin Halgar. Though blind, he says he sees in a different way. In the Magic Quarter, Godrick Farsan helps Master Carendin Halgar guide aspiring Forsaken warlocks. Godrick is blind, yet says he sees in a different way. He does not explain how.

Those seeking to bind greater demons face Godrick’s tests. He sends them to gather pure hearts and essences for intricate summoning rites.

npc:golnir-bouldertoe.text: Golnir Bouldertoe. At Ironforge's Great Forge, Golnir Bouldertoe supplies miners and prospectors and receives dispatches from outposts. Golnir Bouldertoe outfits prospectors and craftsmen at Ironforge's Great Forge. He sells mining picks, flux, and coal for the smelting fires and smithies of the dwarven capital. Kin to Geofram Bouldertoe, Golnir is a trusted contact for workers arriving in the city. He guides fresh hands and receives supply messages from nearby outposts.

npc:gorbold-steelhand.text: Gorbold Steelhand. In Auberdine, Gorbold Steelhand keeps trade moving along Darkshore’s coast. The dwarven merchant brings goods across the Great Sea for travelers, crafters, and night elves. Gorbold Steelhand carries Ironforge trade to Auberdine. Night elves live across much of northern Kalimdor, and Alliance outposts rely on merchants who cross the Great Sea. Gorbold works alongside the kaldorei, selling trade goods, reagents, crafting supplies, and tools. Travelers visit him before exploring Darkshore’s dangerous shores and forests. Gorbold Steelhand keeps watch on the perilous waters off Auberdine as well as his stock. Reefs along Darkshore have swallowed Alliance vessels, and their lost cargo interests the merchant. Travelers who dive into the deep ocean may find him eager to hear of salvage and lost logs from sunken wrecks.

npc:gordon-wendham.text: Gordon Wendham. In the Undercity's Trade Quarter, Gordon Wendham sells weapons and guides couriers from the surface. Gordon Wendham sells weapons to those who take up arms for the Forsaken. His stall offers daggers, hand axes, broadswords, and maces. Fledgling fighters can find dependable iron here before venturing into Lordaeron's contested reaches. Travelers sent by flight masters and couriers are often directed to Gordon Wendham's stall. Some arrive from the bat handlers atop the ruins. In the Trade Quarter, his stall is easy to find for travelers seeking supplies or carrying dispatches through the underground city.

npc:gramma-stonefield.text: Gramma Stonefield. At the Stonefield farm in Elwynn, Gramma Stonefield works quietly to ease a family feud. For decades, the Stonefields and Maclures have bickered across the road. Gramma Stonefield, the oldest living member of her clan, sees their rivalry as senseless and harmful. So when her grandson Tommy Joe Stonefield falls in love with Maybell Maclure, she chooses compassion over clan loyalty. She turns to her old friend William Pestle in Goldshire and quietly plans ways for the sweethearts to meet in secret despite the hostility between their farms.

npc:grand-mason-marblesten.text: Grand Mason Marblesten. In Ironforge's Commons, Marblesten prepares a tribute to Sully Balloo. King Magni Bronzebeard commissioned the memorial for the dwarven soldier, who died in the Thandol Span tragedy. Marblesten seeks stone worthy of the work. Grand Mason Marblesten oversees civic projects and memorials in Ironforge's Commons. Dwarven stonemasons carve halls, pillars, and great effigies from the mountain, carrying on a centuries-old tradition. Marblesten is among the city's foremost masters of the chisel. Through his work, he preserves the history of the Bronzebeard line. King Magni commissioned Marblesten to build a memorial to Sully Balloo, a soldier who died in the Thandol Span tragedy. The memorial honors Balloo and his grieving widow. For a tribute meant to last, Marblesten seeks Alterac Granite, one of the finest stones available. He asks travelers to bring it from Darrow Hill in Hillsbrad.

npc:granis-swiftaxe.text: Granis Swiftaxe. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Granis Swiftaxe trains young Alliance fighters from Coldridge Pass. He prepares them for the road across Dun Morogh, then sends seasoned warriors to Ironforge. Granis Swiftaxe trains young warriors in the Thunderbrew Distillery as they cross Dun Morogh seeking instruction. Proud of the warrior’s path, he takes amusement in those from other callings who try to win his attention. Once a student proves their skill in combat, Granis sends them up the mountain path to Muren Stormpike, master trainer in Ironforge’s Military Ward.

npc:great-father-winter.text: Great-father Winter. In Orgrimmar, Great-father Winter hears children's wishes during the Feast of Winter Veil. Smokywood Pastures hires him to bring cheer near Grommash Hold, though the long work wears on him. In the Valley of Strength, an orc hired by Smokywood Pastures performs as Greatfather Winter. Ancient lore tells of a majestic elemental spirit who wanders the land, bringing snow and seasonal renewal. But this figure promotes company wares and entertains Horde children. Some say the commercial show cheapens genuine seasonal traditions. Still, few deny the festive excitement he brings to Orgrimmar's streets. Outside Grommash Hold, beneath decorated evergreens, Greatfather Winter hears children's wishes. They climb onto his lap and tell him what gifts they want. He promotes Smokywood Pastures discounts and offers holiday greetings, but the long shift wears him down. He says he keeps festive spirits in his pack to quiet the noise when work ends. Visiting adventurers bring him snacks to help him endure.

npc:greatfather-winter.text:
Greatfather Winter. As winter turns, Greatfather Winter is part of old legend and city festivities. Some say he lays snow across Azeroth so the land may rest and renew. In the cities, goblins of Smokywood Pastures shape how people know him. Ancient tales say Greatfather Winter wanders the world late in the year. He spreads his snowy cloak, and nature sleeps before it is born anew. Dwarves call him an aspect or herald of the titans. They point to Dun Morogh's frosted crags as proof of his favor. Tauren honor his place in winter's turning, while crediting the Sun and Moon with the cold and storms that let the Earth Mother rest.

Across the lands, people gather and feast against the cold. They hold to the promise that life will return. In Ironforge and Orgrimmar, goblins of Smokywood Pastures have reshaped the old spirit for city celebrations. The trading company made popular the image of Greatfather Winter as a cheerful elder in red, with a white beard, flying sleigh, holiday treats, and toys.

Smokywood Pastures hires a dwarf in Ironforge and an orc in Orgrimmar to hear children's wishlists and accept milk and gingerbread cookies. Beneath lavishly decorated trees, the company also promotes its seasonal wares.

npc:greatmother-hawkwind.text: Greatmother Hawkwind. Beside the well on Red Cloud Mesa, Greatmother Hawkwind guides young tauren. As mother of Chief Hawkwind, she upholds the tribe’s shared duty despite her age. Greatmother Hawkwind spends her days beside Camp Narache’s fresh water well, guiding young tauren through the start of their rites of passage. Age has slowed her stride, yet she still takes part in village life. She believes every member of the tribe, young or old, must help sustain the community. So she often asks young tauren to fetch water and help with simple chores. Greatmother Hawkwind is mother to Chief Hawkwind, who leads Camp Narache. She offers counsel as threats face Red Cloud Mesa. Her son organizes hunters and warriors against Bristleback quilboar and local predators. She tends the settlement’s moral heart, reminding the newly awakened that strength begins with humility and service to kin.

npc:greta-mosshoof.text: Greta Mosshoof. At the Emerald Sanctuary, Greta Mosshoof works to stop the corruption spreading through Felwood. She stands with the Emerald Circle and other guardians of nature, studying the taint and sending scouts into Jaedenar. At Felwood’s southern edge, Greta Mosshoof works from the Emerald Sanctuary with the Emerald Circle. Corruption is consuming the ancient woods. Greta and her allies seek to understand the spreading rot and push it back. Her investigations follow Felwood’s poisoned waters and the foul cultists hidden within Jaedenar.

npc:grimbooze-thunderbrew.text: Grimbooze Thunderbrew. In Westfall's Dagger Hills, Grimbooze Thunderbrew keeps his casks and brews potent spirits. The eccentric dwarf speaks in verse and belongs to the Thunderbrew clan. Grimbooze Thunderbrew keeps camp in the Dagger Hills, where he tends his private casks. He left the snowy peaks of Dun Morogh, home of the Thunderbrew brewing family in Kharanos, for Westfall's windswept hills. Jovial and devoted to potent spirits, he speaks only in rhymes. A traveler must complete a simple task before he answers questions, and he is ready to test a thirsty palate.

npc:grish-longrunner.text: Grish Longrunner. At the Great Lift, Grish Longrunner watches the road between the southern Barrens and Thousand Needles. The tauren scout carries Horde messages and tracks movement across the crossing. Grish Longrunner keeps watch beside the Great Lift in the southern Barrens. Its platform links the dry southern Barrens with the canyons of Thousand Needles. Quilboar packs roam nearby, and rival groups threaten the crossing. Grish watches travelers and keeps the Horde informed, so reinforcements can be sent where they are needed.

npc:grub.text: Grub. East of the Crossroads, Grub feeds travelers from a hut shared with a cook and a baker. He teaches them to make stew from the Barrens' dig rats. East of the Crossroads, Grub shares a hut with Duhng, his cook, and Tarban Hearthgrain, a baker. He puts the Barrens' dig rats to use instead of letting them go to waste. Travelers can learn his recipe for simmering the rodents into stew.

npc:grull-hawkwind.text: Grull Hawkwind. At Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa, Grull Hawkwind guides young tauren through their first trials. As Chief Hawkwind’s son, he prepares hunters and warriors to test their resolve and honor their ancestors. At Camp Narache, Grull Hawkwind prepares the tribe’s youth. The son of Chief Hawkwind, he guides new arrivals on Red Cloud Mesa and judges whether they are ready to serve the Shu'halo. His trials test stamina, tracking, and survival against plainstriders and mountain cougars. Through them, young tauren learn that balance and respect for nature are foundations of life in Mulgore.

npc:grunt-dogran.text: Grunt Dogran. Deep in the southern Barrens, Grunt Dogran waits in captivity. Once sent to the Crossroads and then Camp Taurajo, he was taken during a patrol into Agama'gor. Grunt Dogran was sent from the Crossroads to reinforce Camp Taurajo after rising through the Horde military. He led a detachment of grunts into Agama'gor, where they clashed fiercely with the Bristleback quilboar. Dogran was badly wounded and crippled. His comrades retreated without him, and the quilboar dragged him away captive.

npc:grunt-logmar.text: Grunt Logmar. At Camp Taurajo, Grunt Logmar watches the Horde's southern Barrens frontier. He tracks nearby threats and seeks aid for scouts who have gone missing. At Camp Taurajo, Grunt Logmar guards the Horde's southern frontier in the Barrens. The camp lies among the tauren, near hostile quilboar grounds and mountain passes into Stonetalon and Mulgore. Logmar watches these dangers and gathers reports from scouts. When local hostiles ambush or capture his comrades, he calls on capable Horde travelers to find and aid them.

npc:grunth.text: Grunth. In Orgrimmar, Grunth eagerly seeks the company of Horde champions. He lives in the Drag orphanage and, during Children's Week, travels across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to learn what makes a hero. Grunth is a young orc orphan in Orgrimmar's Drag, cared for by Orphan Matron Battlewail. Raised in Durotar's harsh red wastes, he watches armored adventurers with awe and asks them question after question. Are armored warriors truly terrifying? Why doesn't lightning on water kill every fish? Will he ever see someone fight a real dragon? During Children's Week, an Orcish Orphan Whistle calls Grunth to travel with adventurers across the world. He hopes to meet High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof in Mulgore and see Lordaeron's ruined throne room. He also wants to visit the rugged frontiers where his people fight for their future.

npc:guard-berton.text:
Guard Berton. Outside the Lakeshire Inn, Guard Berton presses for swift justice against Targorr the Dread. Redridge faces the Blackrock orc invasion, and Stormwind's delays have worn thin. Guard Berton keeps watch outside the Lakeshire Inn as the Blackrock orc invasion threatens Redridge Mountains. Targorr the Dread, an enemy captured for crimes against the kingdom, is locked deep in the Stormwind Stockade and sentenced to death. Yet Stormwind has postponed his execution indefinitely.

With Lakeshire bleeding, Berton will not let the brutal raider linger in a cell. He hires willing adventurers to bypass the delays and kill the orc.

npc:guard-howe.text: Guard Howe. On the bridge south of Lakeshire, Guard Howe watches the road and calls for fighters against the Blackrock orcs. A bitter grudge drives him to offer bounties for proof of their defeat. Guard Howe keeps watch just south of the stone bridge over Lake Everstill, near the heart of Lakeshire. Blackrock orcs press into the Redridge Mountains, and Howe sees them as a threat to the valley. He bears a bitter grudge against the clan and recruits passing fighters to hunt orcs in the eastern hills. For proof that they have been defeated, he offers pay.

npc:gubber-blump.text: Gubber Blump. Along Auberdine’s shore, Gubber Blump fishes, teaches angling, and seeks fresh crab meat. Gubber Blump fishes on the Darkshore coast between Auberdine’s flight master and ferry pier. Most dwarves favor stone halls or forges, but Gubber chooses the shore. He teaches fishing and sells simple angling gear to travelers. Crab meat is a favorite, so he often depends on travelers to bring catches from the dangerous coast or recover his family fishing tackle. Gubber Blump speaks freely about his family, especially his cousin Graun Blump. Graun has a beard and an unusual odor. Travelers may help with coastal work by gathering crawler legs or finding Gubber’s family pole. For their help, they may receive a handwritten thank-you letter and a shiny fishing lure for their next cast.

npc:gurda-ragescar.text: Gurda Ragescar. At a Horde camp southwest of Splintertree Post, Gurda Ragescar fell defending against dangers in Ashenvale's shadowed forest. She and Feran Strongwind died there. Gurda Ragescar and her guards fell at a small Horde camp southwest of Splintertree Post. Dense canopy covered the outpost, deep in Ashenvale, where night elven defenders and wild beasts contested the territory. The camp was overrun, and Gurda and Feran Strongwind were killed. Only remnants of their last stand remain for passing allies to find. Travelers near the trail may come upon the scene of Gurda's defeat. The camp's possessions and unfinished work show the Horde's efforts across the woods. Missing documents and orders speak of work disrupted by the ambush.

npc:hagar-lightninghoof.text: Hagar Lightninghoof. At Freewind Post, Hagar Lightninghoof investigates rumors of an unusual egg hidden deep in the canyon. Wind serpents guard it fiercely, and he wants to learn what lies within. Hagar Lightninghoof hears reports of an unnatural egg in a cavern below Freewind Post. Wind serpents guard the nest with unusual ferocity, keeping curious scouts away. So Hagar seeks an adventurer bold enough to brave their den and bring back the egg. He hopes to study it firsthand and learn what creature inspires such fierce protection from the canyon’s natural predators.

npc:halaan-hawk-eye.text: Halaan Hawk-Eye. From Thendal Village, Halaan Hawk-Eye watches Zephras Isle’s anchor pylons. Though he lacks many Skyborne gifts, his keen natural vision helps him warn visitors as the pylons’ magic falters. From the tower above Thendal Village, Halaan Hawk-Eye keeps watch. Many Skyborne can draw on the ley lines beneath Zephras Isle or see between worlds with mystical skysight. Halaan has neither gift. So he trusts his sharp natural senses, scanning the horizon for the island’s anchor pylons and calling attention to their increasingly volatile, inconsistent arcane energies.

npc:hana-zua.text: Hana'zua. In the Valley of Trials, Hana'zua waits wounded on the canyon ridges for help from young Horde initiates. Above the Valley of Trials, Hana'zua lies wounded on the ridges. The Darkspear scout met Sarkoth, a vicious scorpid that stalks the cliffs. Its venomous sting nearly killed him. Unable to move or return to camp, he waits in the dust for passing recruits. He needs them to kill Sarkoth and carry word of his plight to the Den.

npc:hands-springsprocket.text: Hands Springsprocket. At Coldridge Pass, Hands Springsprocket struggles to keep supplies moving between the valley and Kharanos. Rockjaw troggs have blocked the route. At the mouth of Coldridge Pass, Hands Springsprocket finds his supply runs stopped by Rockjaw troggs. He usually carries provisions to the Thunderbrew distillery and the inn in Kharanos. The troggs have overrun the underground tunnel out of Coldridge Valley, halting trade and foot traffic. Now Hands depends on travelers who can carry essential crates through the dangerous mountain passage.

npc:hansel-heavyhands.text: Hansel Heavyhands. At Thorium Point, Hansel Heavyhands is given dangerous work below the outpost. The huge Dark Iron dwarf passes those jobs to travelers and offers a string of complaints. At Thorium Point, Hansel Heavyhands towers over the other Dark Iron dwarves. His broad frame is nearly as tall and wide as an orc's. He seems made for the front line, yet avoids needless exertion. Instead, he stays in the Thorium Brotherhood's camp above the volcanic ash. Taskmaster Scrange and Master Smith Burninate send Hansel after dangerous beasts in the slag pits. When told to clear Incendosaurs from the Cauldron, he pleads sore feet. Ordered to kill Greater Lava Spiders in the searing wastes, he claims the volcanic ridge is so cold that he has caught a miserable chill. Travelers willing to brave the magma flows can take the work instead.

npc:harb-clawhoof.text: Harb Clawhoof. Near Bloodhoof Village, Harb Clawhoof cares for the kodos that carry tauren across the plains. He entrusts them to worthy tauren riders and champions trusted by Thunder Bluff. Near Bloodhoof Village, Harb Clawhoof tends the kodos. Great beasts, they carry heavy loads over long distances and serve tauren travel and work across the plains. Harb cares for each one and trains it. Then he pairs it with a rider respected by the tauren people. Tauren earn the trust needed to ride Harb’s kodos, while outsiders face closer scrutiny. Their size and temperament make kodos hard for the unfamiliar to guide. So non-tauren allies must prove their loyalty and earn exalted standing with Thunder Bluff before riding one of Harb’s mounts.

npc:harken-windtotem.text: Harken Windtotem. In Bloodhoof Village, Harken Windtotem guides young hunters across Mulgore’s plains. He teaches tauren hunting traditions and asks hunters and travelers to prove their tracking and foraging skills. Harken Windtotem guides those learning the tauren hunting ways in Bloodhoof Village. Life on Mulgore’s plains calls for respect for the natural world and the skills that sustain a tribe. He tests young hunters by sending them after swoops that circle the mesas. They gather the birds’ quills, showing patience, aim, and care in taking only what they need.

npc:harlan-bagley.text: Harlan Bagley. In Stormwind's Trade District, Harlan Bagley keeps the Lionheart Armory stocked for customers. His shop stands on the district's northern side, serving citizens and visiting adventurers. Harlan Bagley keeps the Lionheart Armory on the northern side of Stormwind's Trade District. He tends the stock and sells defensive gear from behind the counter. Trade and regional couriers bring supplies to the shop. The capital faces distant border conflicts and shortages.

npc:harlo-barnaby.text:
Harlo Barnaby. In Menethil Harbor, Harlo Barnaby bears the wounds of Dun Modr's fall. The dwarven refugee escaped the Dark Iron assault and warns travelers of the tragedy in the northern marshes. Harlo Barnaby fled Dun Modr when Dark Iron dwarves struck the northern stronghold without warning. In the chaos, a stray axe hit him square in the back. The blow knocked him unconscious, yet he survived the trek across the marshland.

Harlo awoke bandaged in Menethil Harbor, alive but marked by his wounds and memories of the massacre. Unable to return to Dun Modr, he urges Alliance adventurers to investigate the smoking ruins of his former home.

npc:hegnar-rumbleshot.text: Hegnar Rumbleshot. On the snowy road from Coldridge Pass to Kharanos, Hegnar Rumbleshot supplies hunters and mountaineers with firearms and ammunition. Between Coldridge Pass and Kharanos, Hegnar's small camp serves dwarven marksmen, travelers, and the local militia. Mountain folk use its popular range to practice against Dun Morogh's wild beasts. The steady stream of shooters keeps Hegnar reliant on fresh ammunition from Loslor Rudge, a dwarf engineer.

npc:henze-faulk.text: Henze Faulk. Near Heroes' Vigil in Elwynn Forest, Henze Faulk lies gravely wounded. He shielded Gazin Tenorm from the Defias Brotherhood and now waits for a paladin's aid. At Heroes' Vigil, east of Stormwind, Henze Faulk lies near the stone ring. Defias marauders ambushed him and his friend Gazin Tenorm there. Henze took the attack so Gazin could survive, then fell to the bandits' blades. Gazin reached the Cathedral of Light to seek help. Henze remains between life and death, awaiting a paladin carrying a Symbol of Life.

npc:heralath-fallowbrook.text:
Heralath Fallowbrook. Deep in Razorfen Kraul, Heralath Fallowbrook lies dying in quilboar hands. His people sent him to investigate the briars around Ancient Agamaggan's remains, but the quilboar captured and brutalized him. Now he hopes word of his fate and his cherished pendant will reach his wife in Darnassus. Heralath Fallowbrook came to the southern Barrens to study Ancient Agamaggan and the briars spreading around his remains. His people sent the night elf druid to seek the source of Razorfen Kraul's corruption. Instead, the quilboar captured him and shut him in a pen. Beatings and fever left him mortally wounded.

Before his strength failed, Heralath told Henrig Lonebrow, a dwarf captive, what he had learned. He urged Henrig to warn the sentinel outpost at Thalanaar about the aggression stirred by Charlga Razorflank, the quilboar crone.

npc:high-executor-derrington.text: High Executor Derrington. At the Bulwark, High Executor Derrington directs the Forsaken vanguard against threats from the Western Plaguelands. He sends seasoned champions toward contested ruins such as Andorhal and Scholomance. High Executor Derrington commands the Bulwark’s barricades, where soldiers cross from Tirisfal Glades into the Western Plaguelands. He has little patience for political maneuvering in the Undercity. To him, the front lines are a test of survival. So he orders Horde soldiers and sellswords to scout plague-ridden territory and blunt enemy incursions before they reach Tirisfal. The Bulwark faces the Scourge in Andorhal and the Scarlet Crusade farther north. Scourge forces spread corruption through cauldrons in the countryside. The Crusade’s zealous fanatics contest northern fortifications and skirmish relentlessly with Forsaken patrols. Derrington coordinates sharp counterattacks, sabotage against Scarlet lines, and the systematic disruption of Scourge cauldron fields to protect the eastern border.

npc:high-priest-rohan.text: High Priest Rohan. In Ironforge, High Priest Rohan guides the Church of the Holy Light from the Hall of Mysteries. He teaches young priests, helps them deepen their mastery of the Light, and keeps spiritual ties between Ironforge, Stormwind, and distant allies. In Ironforge’s Mystic Ward, High Priest Rohan paces the Hall of Mysteries as the Church of the Holy Light’s highest-ranking representative in the city. Dwarves once honored the titans, yet their priests have embraced the Light’s wisdom, compassion, and justice. Rohan patiently teaches young acolytes to wield holy magic and steel their minds against despair. Once the priests in his care master the fundamentals, Rohan sends them abroad to learn from other traditions. Human and dwarven students go to High Priestess Laurena in Stormwind City. Night elf disciples travel to Priestess Alathea at Darnassus’s Temple of the Moon, where they study mysteries such as Elune’s Grace. Rohan also sends healers to aid the Cenarion Circle’s druids in distant Azshara, wherever hardship calls. Rohan keeps sacred relics for the Alliance priesthood and paladin brotherhoods. Among them is a blessed exorcism censer used for years to cleanse vile spirits. When the Order of the Silver Hand and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker need it for their knights’ holy calling, Rohan lends it freely. He asks only for charitable alms to replenish Ironforge’s dwindling food reserves for the needy.

npc:highlord-demitrian.text: Highlord Demitrian. Among the strange crystals of northwestern Silithus, Highlord Demitrian waits alone. He calls himself a loyal servant of Prince Thunderaan and knows how to wake the sleeping elemental lord. Those who bring him ancient elemental bindings seek the Windseeker's power. In the Crystal Vale, Demitrian lingers at an abandoned encampment in Silithus's desolate wastes. The ruined camp belongs to the Twilight's Hammer, and the solitary human seems out of place there. Yet Demitrian's chief purpose is to herald Prince Thunderaan, the Windseeker. He gives visitors little notice unless they carry proof of the Windseeker's shattered essence.

npc:hogger.text: Hogger. In southwestern Elwynn Forest, Hogger leads the Riverpaw gnolls in raids on farms and travelers. The Stormwind Marshals have put a bounty on him for his violent attacks. Hogger commands the Riverpaw pack from Hogger Hill in southwestern Elwynn Forest. Since the Third War, the gnolls have grown bolder and more orderly in their raids on nearby homesteads. Now they fight beside the Defias Brotherhood, trading raw ferocity for arms, tactical direction, and magical support. To guard Elwynn's borders and trade routes from further bloodshed, Marshal Dughan has put a bounty on Hogger's head.

npc:holt-thunderhorn.text: Holt Thunderhorn. On Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff, Holt Thunderhorn trains hunters to serve the Horde. He teaches tracking and survival, and sends hunters toward specialized trials across Mulgore and beyond. On Hunter Rise, Holt Thunderhorn trains hunters for the Horde. From the rise above Mulgore's plains, he teaches ranged combat, tracking, and survival. Like other elders of his craft, he guides young tauren from roaming hunters toward disciplined defenders of their new capital.

npc:huldar.text: Huldar. Huldar is stranded on Loch Modan’s southern road after his blast powder delivery is stopped. The dwarven teamster needs help getting the cargo to the southern excavation site, where archaeologists and prospectors need supplies. Huldar’s damaged wagon leaves him stranded near the lake’s southern bend. Local wildlife and troggs threaten the road, and Dark Iron infiltrators lurk nearby. He needs passing travelers to guard the remaining powder kegs and carry the shipment to the dig.

npc:illiyana-moonblaze.text: Illiyana Moonblaze. At Silverwing Grove, Illiyana Moonblaze supplies Alliance champions bound for the fight against the Warsong Outriders. She works beside the Silverwing Sentinels in Ashenvale. At Silverwing Grove, Illiyana Moonblaze keeps the Silverwing Sentinels supplied. Her post lies near the path into Warsong Gulch. From there, she outfits defenders holding Ashenvale's southern woods against the Warsong clan. Illiyana equips Alliance volunteers preparing to fight the Warsong clan in Warsong Gulch. As champions earn favor with the Silverwing Sentinels, she provides custom rations, specialized draughts, and fine weapons for woodland skirmishes. Weary fighters return from the front for repairs to their weapons and armor, keeping the Sentinels ready for war.

npc:ilthalaine.text: Ilthalaine. In Shadowglen, Ilthalaine keeps watch over the sacred glade and guides young night elves as they begin life in Teldrassil. He teaches them to defend their home and tend its balance. Just beyond Shadowglen's heart, Ilthalaine watches the woodland paths. He notices changes in the forest that ordinary eyes miss. When young night elves awaken to their duties, he welcomes them and teaches Kaldorei traditions. His guidance prepares them to care for Teldrassil and take up the work of its defenders. Heavy spring rains have brought more nightsabers and thistle boars to Shadowglen than the glade can feed. Ilthalaine asks young defenders to thin their numbers. With fewer beasts, the woodland's other creatures can flourish and nature's balance can be restored. Ilthalaine tests young elves against local wildlife and points each toward a chosen calling. He gives each traveler a class sigil, then sends them to their mentors in the Aldrassil sanctuary. Warriors, druids, rogues, priests, and hunters each find where their service to the Kaldorei begins.

npc:innkeeper-allison.text:
Innkeeper Allison. At the Gilded Rose, Innkeeper Allison welcomes travelers and merchants in Stormwind's Trade District. The inn stands between the bank and auction house, offering hearthstone bindings, drinks, and shelter. Innkeeper Allison welcomes travelers at the Gilded Rose in Stormwind. Between the Trade District auction house and the city's main vaults, its ground floor draws peddlers, mercenaries, and visiting diplomats. She keeps order behind the counter and offers lodging and hearthstone services.

Allison also joins local holiday festivities. At times, she coordinates small errands for traveling heroes who seek rest in the capital.

npc:innkeeper-farley.text: Innkeeper Farley. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Innkeeper Farley offers travelers meals, beds, and hearthstones. Well liked and watchful, he keeps misplaced mail and listens to the troubles of the road. Travelers bound for Stormwind, Westfall, and Duskwood find Innkeeper Farley at the Lion's Pride Inn counter in Goldshire. He offers meals, ale, cheese, and a bed, and sets hearthstones for those who need one. Farley welcomes all who pass through this busy waystation and keeps order at the inn.

npc:innkeeper-firebrew.text:
Innkeeper Firebrew. At the Stonefire Tavern in Ironforge’s Commons, Innkeeper Firebrew gives travelers food and rest. His hearty dwarven fare welcomes mountaineers and visiting dignitaries beneath the mountain. Innkeeper Firebrew welcomes travelers at the Stonefire Tavern in the Commons. The tavern stands in the Commons’ central ring, and many arriving through the Great Gates find it first. Behind a counter of ale, stout, and roasted meat, Firebrew serves those bound for Dun Morogh’s snowy passes or deeper into the mountain kingdom.

Miners, riflemen, and emissaries gather there to leave the drafty tunnels behind and trade tales around the hearth. The Stonefire remains a lively crossroads in the heart of Ironforge.

npc:innkeeper-grosk.text: Innkeeper Grosk. At Razor Hill, Innkeeper Grosk welcomes travelers on the road between the Valley of Trials and Orgrimmar. His inn offers food, drink, and a place to rest in central Durotar. Razor Hill joins Durotar’s southern training grounds to Orgrimmar’s high walls. Innkeeper Grosk gives warriors, scouts, and peons shelter at his inn. Beneath its sturdy timbers, travelers can find basic provisions, hearty meats, and cool water. Innkeeper Grosk also helps the laborers who keep Durotar running. Ukor, a timid peon, carried food to the Valley of Trials, only to learn it was not needed. He asks travelers to bring the load back to Grosk’s inn in Razor Hill.

npc:innkeeper-gryshka.text: Innkeeper Gryshka. At the Broken Tusk in Orgrimmar, Innkeeper Gryshka welcomes travelers with food, drink, and a hearthstone binding. Hunters across Durotar and the Barrens keep her supplied with meat. At the Broken Tusk, Innkeeper Gryshka welcomes travelers in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. The inn stands just beyond the city's main gates, where warriors, messengers, and newcomers to Thrall's Horde can find shelter. Gryshka keeps the Broken Tusk's kitchen supplied with fresh meat. Trusted hunters across Horde lands send her game, including Zargh at the Crossroads and Grimtak in Durotar. They ship their finest cuts to the inn.

npc:innkeeper-keldamyr.text: Innkeeper Keldamyr. At Dolanaar's inn, Innkeeper Keldamyr gives young night elves leaving Shadowglen food, drink, and a place to rest. His inn offers shelter beneath the boughs of the World Tree. Many newcomers reach Dolanaar first after leaving Aldrassil's sheltered glade. At the village's central inn, Innkeeper Keldamyr offers bread, spring water, and soft beds beneath Teldrassil's canopy. Travelers, sentinels, and young novices bound for Darnassus pause at his counter. They rest, bind their Hearthstones, and gather rations for the journey through the boughs. An inn high among the branches needs steady supplies from nearby settlements and tradesfolk. Couriers bringing goods are often sent to Keldamyr's desk. His inn is tied to the daily trade that keeps Dolanaar running.

npc:innkeeper-norman.text: Innkeeper Norman. In the Undercity's Trade Quarter, Innkeeper Norman keeps a tavern ready for travelers. The quiet, diligent Forsaken offers Horde travelers rooms, hearthstone bindings, and food for the living and the dead. Beneath Lordaeron's ruined capital, Innkeeper Norman tends the main tavern in the Undercity's Trade Quarter. Emissaries, mercenaries, and adventurers passing through the Forsaken stronghold find lodging there. Travelers bind their hearthstones, share news from across Azeroth, or prepare for journeys into the Plaguelands. Innkeeper Norman sells provisions and manages rooms through most of the year. During Hallow's End, he joins the revelry and asks adventurous patrons for peculiar displays, such as clucking like a chicken. Those who oblige can earn holiday treats like Undercity mints.

npc:innkeeper-pala.text: Innkeeper Pala. On Thunder Bluff’s lower rise, Innkeeper Pala welcomes travelers to the Cat and the Shaman. She offers a place to rest, cold drinks, and a hearthstone binding for journeys across Mulgore and beyond. At the Cat and the Shaman on Thunder Bluff’s lower rise, Innkeeper Pala keeps the hearth. Travelers come from the central lifts or the plains of Mulgore. In the common room, weary warriors, wandering druids, and the Horde’s visiting allies find shelter, a warm drink, and a familiar place to rest.

npc:jahan-hawkwing.text: Jahan Hawkwing. At the Crossroads in the Barrens, Jahan Hawkwing keeps Horde travelers supplied with armor. The tauren armorer works from the outpost while predators roam the plains. Jahan Hawkwing supplies armor to Horde travelers and defenders at the Crossroads. In the Barrens, good gear can mean survival against centaur, quilboar, and wild beasts. He works with local leatherworkers, sending cured hides for delivery. Their work keeps his shop stocked with tanned leather and sturdy chainmail.

npc:james-halloran.text: James Halloran. In Menethil Harbor, James Halloran tans crocolisk hides for a living. Passing travelers and nearby trade carry raw skins to him and finished leather to buyers across the eastern continents. James Halloran earns his living from the marsh just outside Menethil Harbor. Its dangerous bogs supply crocolisk skins, which he turns into fine leather with rare skill. Nearby trade carries his finished goods to buyers across Azeroth. Near the marsh, Halloran tends his curing vats and trade arrangements while danger remains close. He hires hardy travelers to skin young marsh beasts and make routine deliveries between his work site and nearby settlements. Their help supplies his craft while he manages the tanning and trade.

npc:jannok-breezesong.text: Jannok Breezesong. In Dolanaar, Jannok Breezesong guides young night elf rogues beneath the World Tree’s boughs. He teaches stealth, cunning, and bladecraft to those setting out on their path. Beneath Dolanaar’s boughs, Jannok Breezesong trains novice night elf rogues. They work quietly beyond the ranks of Teldrassil’s sentinels and druids. His lessons teach them to stalk through shadows, strike from behind, and survive unseen among the boughs. When their first lessons are done, Jannok sends them to more experienced trainers in Darnassus.

npc:jasper-fel.text: Jasper Fel. At SI:7 headquarters in Old Town, Jasper Fel keeps watch on visitors and warns them to mind their speech. Jasper Fel supplies the agents inside SI:7 headquarters in Old Town. His wares include simple daggers and empty vials for brewing and applying poisons. He serves Mathias Shaw's intelligence division and warns visitors to mind their speech. Here, careless words can put people in danger.

npc:jen-shan.text: Jen'shan. In the Valley of Trials, Jen'shan prepares young hunters for the wild. The Darkspear jungle troll teaches orc and troll marksmen to track, fight at range, and survive. Jen'shan trains new hunters in the Valley of Trials. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls find her by following inscribed tablets and parchments. She teaches archery, marksmanship, and wilderness survival, readying them for the scorpids and boars on the canyon floor.

npc:jennea-cannon.text: Jennea Cannon. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Jennea Cannon teaches new mages from the Wizard's Sanctum. She urges caution and self-control, investigates disturbances in local arcane energies, and sends promising apprentices beyond the city to test their studies. At the top of the Wizard's Sanctum's spiral walkway, Jennea Cannon teaches those who come to Stormwind to study the arcane. She teaches more than spells. Caution and self-control matter just as much. Even those who do not study magic hear her warning: without training, magic can burn its wielder. Jennea sends promising apprentices beyond the city walls to test what they have learned. At Mirror Lake in Elwynn Forest, they study how natural water sources meet arcane resonance. As their studies advance, she sends them to investigate disturbances at the Blue Recluse or gather volatile reagents for their first true wizard's implements. When an apprentice has outgrown Jennea's lessons, she points the way to greater masters. Those who show true potential may continue up the Sanctum's hierarchy with High Sorcerer Andromath. Others may travel beyond the kingdom to practitioners such as Tabetha, deep in the Dustwallow Marsh.

npc:jocaste.text: Jocaste. In Darnassus, Jocaste teaches hunters who have come in from Teldrassil's wilds. Jocaste trains night elf hunters in the Cenarion Enclave of Darnassus. Young trackers arrive after their first lessons in Shadowglen, ready to hunt in the capital. She teaches marksmanship and survival in the wild, and the bond between a hunter and the beasts of Kalimdor.

npc:john-j-keeshan.text: John J. Keeshan. In the Redridge fighting, Corporal John J. Keeshan was taken prisoner by the Blackrock orcs. After the battle around Stonewatch, they dragged him deep into Render's Rock. Corporal John J. Keeshan serves Stormwind in the Redridge Mountains. He was posted there as Blackrock orcs pressed against Lakeshire and its defenders. When fighting flared around Stonewatch Keep, Keeshan stood with the soldiers holding the line for the kingdom.

npc:jorah-annison.text: Jorah Annison. In the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Jorah Annison guides warlocks seeking ancient knowledge. The Forsaken cartographer knows both the land and the old texts they seek. Jorah Annison makes maps in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, though the work does little to hold his interest. He would trade every map in the shop for one good book. Few know more about ancient texts, and warlocks share his taste for a scholar's work. Warlocks seeking the elusive Tome of the Cabal are often sent to Jorah Annison. His knowledge reaches beyond the ruins of Lordaeron, and he can point them toward places where ancient texts and remnants of dark sects may be found. He joins the study of old lore to the geography of distant lands.

npc:jorgen.text: Jorgen. At Stormwind’s Valley of Heroes entrance, Jorgen keeps watch beside the water. His quiet perch draws people with matters they cannot discuss openly.
