Jorgen keeps to the water just right of Stormwind’s great entrance. Above him, statues of heroes look over the bridge as he watches those who pass below. People seeking information they want kept off the record can find a quiet contact there.

npc:josef-gregorian.text: Josef Gregorian. In the Undercity’s Magic Quarter, Josef Gregorian trains tailors for the Horde. His craft leads them toward enchanted fabrics and specialized garments. Josef Gregorian teaches tailoring in the Undercity’s Magic Quarter, where Forsaken and their Horde allies learn the craft. Tailoring matters to warlocks, mages, and priests who channel raw energies through woven fibers. Gregorian teaches the first patterns and stitches robes for young mages who bring him the right materials.

npc:kaal-soulreaper.text:
Kaal Soulreaper. In the Undercity, Kaal Soulreaper trains orc warlocks and keeps ties with dark practitioners across the Horde. Among the Forsaken, he guides students to mentors in distant lands. Kaal Soulreaper teaches in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, where Horde warlocks seek his knowledge of demons and curses. Thrall's Horde keeps close watch on fel magic in Orgrimmar, so Lordaeron's underground sanctums give practitioners like Kaal room to work.

He also connects those who seek greater power with mentors across the sea. One of them is Menara Voidrender in the Barrens.

npc:kali-remik.text: Kali Remik. In Sen'jin Village, Kali Remik sends young hunters on toward further training. She is a Darkspear troll hunter who knows Durotar's tracking and survival ways. Kali Remik guides young scouts in Sen'jin Village, where they begin life beyond the Valley of Trials. A Darkspear troll tracker, she knows Durotar's dry lands and the Horde's settlements. When novices are ready to leave the local training grounds, she sends promising hunters to Thotar in Razor Hill. There they learn to tame beasts and strengthen the Horde's frontier ranks.

npc:kaltunk.text: Kaltunk. In Durotar's Valley of Trials, Kaltunk welcomes young orcs and points them toward their first duties for the Horde. Kaltunk watches over new arrivals in the Valley of Trials. He directs them to Gornek and the path of discipline. Trainers and elders set trials and hunting rites, while Kaltunk gives recruits clear orders so they know where to go. The Valley of Trials was chosen to test the strength and resilience of youths walking its canyon floors. Kaltunk brings the same rugged practicality to his work. He offers no grand speeches or coddling. Each orc must find a place in the world and serve the warchief.

npc:kanati-greycloud.text: Kanati Greycloud. At Whitereach Post, Kanati Greycloud and his companions stand against the Galak centaur. The tauren hunters watch western Thousand Needles as the centaur threat continues. Kanati Greycloud keeps camp at Whitereach Post, high on the sandstone spires of western Thousand Needles. Game is plentiful there, and the view stretches across the canyon. Below, Galak warbands contest the arid flats. Kanati and the other tauren hunters watch the canyon floor and defend the post from nearby marauders.

npc:kaplak.text:
Kaplak. In Razor Hill, Kaplak prepares young rogues for the Horde's quieter work. He teaches orc and troll students before sending them north to Orgrimmar. Kaplak trains new Horde rogues in Razor Hill. Though orcish custom favors open combat and roaring charges, he teaches skills that call for patience. His students learn to stalk unseen, pick locks, and strike from behind.

When they outgrow his lessons in Durotar's red ravines, Kaplak sends them north to Orgrimmar. There, senior guild operatives can deepen their craft.

npc:karang-amakkar.text: Karang Amakkar. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Karang Amakkar watches the rocky coast as threats close in around the Horde. At Zoram'gar Outpost on the Zoram Strand, Karang Amakkar guards one of the Horde's most exposed borders. The camp faces danger from the sea, the night elves, and wild beasts inland. Along the road east, Karang watches hostile peoples and guards Horde couriers and scouts from ambush by tribes defending their territory. Karang Amakkar gives much of his attention to the furbolgs of the ancient woods, especially the Foulweald tribe. Corruption and primal hostility drive these bear-folk into frenzies. So Karang sends capable warriors to bring down their leader and clear their dens before the tribes can gather for an organized assault on Zoram'gar.

npc:kargal-battlescar.text:
Kargal Battlescar. At the Far Watch Post, Kargal Battlescar watches the eastern edge of the Barrens. He guards the crossing from Durotar, judges incoming recruits, and sends capable fighters west to strengthen Horde defenses. From the Far Watch Post, Kargal Battlescar watches the road into the Barrens. Travelers and new adventurers cross the bridge over the Southfury River, leaving the Valley of Trials behind. The Barrens is dangerous and contested.

Aggressive wildlife, centaur raiders, and quilboar tribes threaten the frontier. Kargal inspects those who pass and gathers willing recruits for the Horde. He sends them west to the Crossroads, where they can aid local commanders in securing the frontier.

npc:karos-razok.text: Karos Razok. At the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Karos Razok keeps the Forsaken bat roost ready. Karos Razok tends skeletal bats from a wooden platform above the Sepulcher's crypts. The northern road through Silverpine Forest is treacherous, with Moonrage worgen, rogue Dalaran magi, and the human remnants of Ambermill. Razok keeps messengers, fresh recruits, and vital supplies moving above the haunted canopy. His bats link the frontier outpost to the capital in Tirisfal Glades.

npc:katie-hunter.text: Katie Hunter. At the Eastvale Logging Camp stables, Katie Hunter tends horses for Stormwind and trusted Alliance champions. With Randal Hunter, she keeps travelers and soldiers mounted on the kingdom’s roads. In eastern Elwynn Forest, Katie Hunter tends the horses at the Eastvale Logging Camp. As lumberjacks cut timber for Stormwind’s reconstruction, she raises dependable pintos, mares, and swift steeds for riders. Her horses carry people along the kingdom’s roads and the dangerous routes of southern Azeroth.

npc:kaymard-copperpinch.text: Kaymard Copperpinch. In Orgrimmar, Kaymard Copperpinch brings Smokywood Pastures' Winter Veil trade to the Valley of Strength. Travelers find festive wares there and can help with holiday troubles. Each Feast of Winter Veil, Kaymard Copperpinch brings Smokywood Pastures to the Valley of Strength. Great-father Winter receives visitors nearby while Kaymard sells fine treats, festive wrapping paper, and other holiday goods. For a goblin, no grand festival is complete without a lively exchange of coin. During the festival, Kaymard also handles troubles that threaten Smokywood Pastures. Holiday confections go missing, and Metzen the Reindeer disappears. Kaymard calls on Horde adventurers to solve these problems and keep Winter Veil running smoothly.

npc:keeper-albagorm.text: Keeper Albagorm. At Stonetalon Peak, Keeper Albagorm seeks aid as the Charred Vale burns and the wilds suffer. Keeper Albagorm guards the night elven refuge at Stonetalon Peak. As a son of Cenarius, he feels the pain of the natural world. South of the peak, the Charred Vale lies scorched by a greedy mechanized army of industrialists. Bloodfury harpies now hold the ruins and prevent new growth. From his sanctuary, Albagorm works to halt the corruption and restore balance to the wounded forest.

npc:keeper-bel-dugur.text: Keeper Bel'dugur. In the Undercity's Apothecarium, Keeper Bel'dugur sends travelers to recover dark tomes and magical artifacts for his people. The scholarly Forsaken works among its researchers. Keeper Bel'dugur works among the Apothecarium's vats and researchers. He sends travelers across Azeroth to recover dangerous arcane and occult relics. The Book of Ur, a legendary treatise on beings from other dimensions, lies locked inside Shadowfang Keep. It has drawn his keen interest. Many in the Undercity seek magical knowledge to cure undeath or wield it as a weapon. Bel'dugur's chosen acquisitions seem aimed at uncovering ancient, forbidden powers.

npc:keeper-bel-varil.text: Keeper Bel'varil. At Tarren Mill, Keeper Bel'varil studies magic and alchemy for the Forsaken. With Wordeen Voidglare, he searches Hillsbrad Foothills for relics and binding materials. Tarren Mill is besieged, and Keeper Bel'varil supports the Forsaken there with magic and alchemy. The royal apothecaries and soldiers focus on the Alliance garrison at Southshore, down the road. So Bel'varil turns to practical sorcery, sending travelers to recover stone tokens and binding bracers from nearby elemental and enchanted threats.

npc:keldran.text:
Keldran. North of the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar, Keldran works to open a path to peace with the Alliance. He directs secret strikes against demonic remnants, hoping to show that the modern Horde has left the Burning Legion behind. Keldran works from Orgrimmar’s red rock terraces while Thrall governs from the Valley of Wisdom. The Alliance still sees orcs as bloodthirsty puppets of demonic masters, a reputation forged in the first wars. Keldran believes Thrall has grown weary of endless conflict.

Yet peace talks cannot begin while demon-worshiping cults endure in Kalimdor. Without the Warchief’s formal sanction, Keldran takes the initiative and directs trusted agents toward distant threats. He hopes to erase the demonic stain and clear the way for diplomacy.

npc:kelm-hargunth.text: Kelm Hargunth. At Mor'shan Base Camp, Kelm Hargunth keeps the Warsong Outriders supplied. He sends provisions and care packages to Horde champions fighting night elves in Warsong Gulch. Kelm Hargunth manages supplies for the Warsong Outriders at Mor'shan Base Camp. The camp sits on the northern edge of the Barrens, beside Ashenvale. Beyond its stockade, scouts and raiders skirmish. Kelm sends weapons, armor, and rations to the fighters. The Warsong Outriders face the Silverwing Sentinels, so steady provisions matter as much as fury in battle. Kelm gives special supplies to warriors who have proven themselves in Warsong Gulch. His stores hold care packages with field dressings and iron rations. He also offers weapons marked with the Warsong clan's crimson insignia. These supplies support fighters serving the Horde's campaign in the forests to the north.

npc:kerlonian-evershade.text: Kerlonian Evershade. At the Grove of the Ancients in Darkshore, Kerlonian Evershade has just awakened from a long sleep in the Emerald Dream. The night elf Druid of the Claw needs help through the troubled wilds on his way to Maestra's Post. For centuries, Druids of the Claw slept in barrows and communed with the Emerald Dream. They were called from their slumber during the Third War. Now Kerlonian Evershade rests beneath the ancient trees of the Grove of the Ancients, still shaking off the supernatural grogginess of his long sleep. He must cross Darkshore's troubled forests to reach Maestra's Post on the Ashenvale border. The road from the Grove of the Ancients is dangerous. Blackwood furbolgs prowl the Twilight Vale, and Dark Strand cultists lurk along the road into Ashenvale. Sleep has weakened Kerlonian, and sudden bouts of exhaustion still trouble him. So he depends on sympathetic Alliance travelers for protection as he journeys south to rejoin his fellow night elves.

npc:kernobee.text: Kernobee. In Gnomeregan, Kernobee lies trapped among the ruins. The goblin engineer found Dark Iron dwarves working on the great super rig, then was captured, beaten unconscious, and left among the troggs in the dormitory quarters. While doing business or scavenging in Gnomeregan, Kernobee learned that Dark Iron dwarves had helped build and operate the great super rig burrowing beneath the city. He knew the danger of that discovery and tried to flee to Ratchet. There he meant to warn his associate, Tinkerwiz. The Dark Irons caught him before he could escape. Kernobee's captors beat him unconscious and left him alive. They threw him into a small room along the dormitory corridor, opposite the Clean Zone. Feral troggs and radiation surround him. He needs help to wake, reach safety, and escape the ruins.

npc:keryn-sylvius.text:
Keryn Sylvius. On the second floor of Goldshire’s Lion’s Pride Inn, Keryn Sylvius trains young rogues. In the reading room, she teaches stealth and bladecraft and quietly guides promising operatives toward Stormwind’s intelligence service. Keryn Sylvius keeps to the reading room above the Lion’s Pride Inn. Below, travelers and town guards fill the common room. Upstairs, she listens to the steady flow of gossip from the road. She mentors rogues learning their trade in Elwynn Forest.

When promising operatives outgrow petty theft and roadside skulduggery, Sylvius quietly sends them to Stormwind City. There, they can seek out SI:7.

npc:khelden-bremen.text: Khelden Bremen. On Northshire Abbey's upper floor, Khelden Bremen teaches human mages their first spells. He prepares novices to serve Stormwind through the arcane arts. In his study, Khelden Bremen teaches novices the discipline and focus to shape raw magical energy safely. Below, clergy and defenders carry on their work. His pupils prepare to travel through Elwynn Forest and continue their studies in Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

npc:kil-hala.text: Kil'hala. At the Crossroads in the Barrens, Kil'hala teaches Horde tailors the work of cloth. Young Horde mages also bring him locks of hair from Ashenvale's laughing sisters, and he weaves them into nether-lace robes. At the Crossroads, Kil'hala teaches tailors from among the Horde recruits and travelers. He shows them how to work common spun bolts and make garments for life on the dry plains. At Deino's request, he also weaves nether-lace robes for young mages who bring him hair from the laughing sisters, the dryads of Ashenvale's forests.

npc:kin-weelay.text: Kin'weelay. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Kin'weelay brings Darkspear witchcraft to the Horde's effort to free young Yenniku. His knowledge of spirits guides the work in Stranglethorn Vale. Kin'weelay is a powerful Darkspear witch doctor who knows spirits, hexes, and soul magic. Horde scouts seek his counsel in Stranglethorn Vale when ancestral spirits stir or hostile troll enchantments block their way.

npc:kindal-moonweaver.text:
Kindal Moonweaver. From a hidden perch in Feralas, Kindal Moonweaver watches the Grimtotem Compound and its captured beasts. Troubled by their mistreatment, she seeks help to free them and protect young animals. She is kin to Jer'kai Moonweaver, and both defend the forest's creatures. East of Dire Maul, Kindal Moonweaver watches the valley from a hidden perch along a narrow, winding mountain path. The path lies behind timber, north of the Grimtotem Compound. Feralas is contested by the Horde, the night elves of Feathermoon, and the ancient ruins of Eldre'Thalas.

Kindal's concern is the nearby hollow, where the Grimtotem tribe keeps a fortified compound. They capture and pen local wildlife for cruel ends. From her concealed overlook, Kindal watches for anyone willing to brave the enemy camp and free the beasts. Kindal seeks to preserve Feralas's sacred balance and protect its gentle creatures from their brutish captors. With her kin, Jer'kai Moonweaver, she works to free caged beasts and find help for young animals left stranded by poaching.

Her concern is close at hand: freeing caged sprites and finding a home for an orphaned sprite darter.

npc:kirge-sternhorn.text: Kirge Sternhorn. In the Barrens, Kirge Sternhorn guides travelers across central Kalimdor. He watches the southern trails and sends new Horde adventurers north to the Crossroads. For new wanderers, the sun-baked Barrens can feel daunting. Kirge Sternhorn watches over travelers south of the central trails, between the southern camps and the heart of Kalimdor. Quilboar and fierce predators roam the savanna, so Kirge helps young adventurers find their footing. He sends them toward the greater Horde presence gathering in the north.

npc:klannoc-macleod.text: Klannoc Macleod. On Fray Island, Klannoc Macleod tests warriors seeking mastery of combat and its stances. The human welcomes fighters from both the Alliance and the Horde. Those who earn his respect face greater trials inland. On Fray Island, off the Merchant Coast in the Barrens, Klannoc Macleod tests seasoned fighters. Though human, he sets Alliance and Horde quarrels aside. He judges each contender by grit, skill with a blade, and resolve under fire. Klannoc Macleod calls his Fray Island trial the affray. Contenders climb onto raised iron grating and face wave after wave of eager brawlers as he watches. Those who endure and defeat his chosen champion earn his approval. They prove they have the temperament for berserker stance training.

npc:kor-ghan.text: Kor'ghan. In Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow, Kor'ghan tends remedies and toxins. The Darkspear troll stands outside Rekkul's Poisons and asks for help making antidotes against Durotar’s venomous predators. Outside Rekkul's Poisons in Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow, Kor'ghan tends remedies and toxins. He sends travelers from the capital into Durotar’s red canyons to gather venom from scorpids. Those venomous creatures provide what he needs to prepare antidotes for the dangers of the wild.

npc:korran.text: Korran. At the Crossroads, Korran watches the Barrens for dangers to the Horde. The Darkspear troll reports to Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar and studies silithid spreading across the scrublands. At the Crossroads, Korran watches beyond the quilboar and centaur clans for threats to the Horde. Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar stationed the troll scout here to observe changes in the land. Korran gathers intelligence for the Horde's leaders. Korran now focuses on the Field of Giants in the southern Barrens. Strange, aggressive insectoid creatures called silithid have begun burrowing into the earth. To learn where the swarm came from and what danger it poses to the young Horde, Korran asks passing adventurers to dig up intact eggs with his claw tool.

npc:kravel-koalbeard.text: Kravel Koalbeard. At the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats, Kravel Koalbeard sees profit in the rivalry between gnome and goblin racers. He seeks coin through scavenged machine parts, blackmail, and schemes to sway race results. At the Mirage Raceway, Kravel Koalbeard watches the crowds and crews for a chance to profit. He works among the raceway encampment, offering contracts and favors for motives rarely clean. The rivalry between gnome and goblin engineers gives him openings for extortion, sabotage, and theft.

npc:kreldig-ungor.text: Kreldig Ungor. At Nijel's Point, Kreldig Ungor directs Reclaimers Inc.'s work in dangerous Desolace. He hires Alliance adventurers to recover lost cargo and gather local reagents. Kreldig works from Nijel's Point, an Alliance refuge among Desolace's blighted canyons. He represents Reclaimers Inc., far from Khaz Modan, where centaur clans, demons, and the Horde contest the wilderness. Others see ruin and ash. Kreldig sees lost goods and assets that can still be reclaimed for profit. Kreldig seeks the lost vessel of Karnitol, wrecked along Desolace's treacherous western coast. Its shipment held prized goods. He directs the search for the wreck and the scattered cargo, before scavengers or coastal sea giants claim it. Kreldig also oversees the gathering of Desolace's unusual biological and mineral resources for Reclaimers Inc. The harsh land breeds distinctive fauna and flora, whose parts bring high prices from alchemists and engineers in the Eastern Kingdoms. Adventurers who face the wasteland's predators can earn steady pay through his contracts.

npc:krolg.text: Krolg. In a hut south of Mystral Lake, Krolg keeps his mind while his kin fall to madness. Cast out from the Foulweald tribe, he speaks only with those who appear to be furbolgs. South of Mystral Lake, Krolg watches the forest from his secluded shelter. He remains lucid while most Foulweald furbolgs in Ashenvale succumb to the demonic taint left by the Burning Legion. He saw his brethren descend into senseless violence. Now he speaks only with those who appear to be kin.

npc:krom-stoutarm.text: Krom Stoutarm. In Ironforge, Krom Stoutarm turns to the darker arts in the Hall of Explorers. A dwarven scholar and warlock, he studies arcane texts and demonic rites in the library. He guides Alliance warlocks seeking esoteric knowledge across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Krom Stoutarm pursues occult lore in the Hall of Explorers. While dwarven archaeologists there study titan artifacts with picks and shovels, Krom turns to massive tomes and the rites for binding demons. His work gives a warlock’s craft a place in Ironforge’s mountain halls, though many distrust those arts. Alliance warlocks seeking to bind powerful demons such as the felhunter turn to Krom Stoutarm. He knows of occult volumes scattered across distant lands. He sends summoners to recover torn pages and fragments of the infamous Tome of the Cabal, including from the centaur of Thousand Needles.

npc:krusk.text:
Krusk. At Tarren Mill, Krusk seeks his captured scouts and the Syndicate's relics. Warchief Thrall sent him to investigate Durnholde Keep, but an ambush scattered his team. Krusk leads the effort from Tarren Mill after a failed strike at Durnholde Keep. Warchief Thrall sent him and a small team to scout Syndicate activity and recover relics tied to the fortress's grim past. The human outlaws were better entrenched and more coordinated than expected. An ambush inside the crumbling walls overwhelmed the orcish scouts.

Krusk fought his way out. Drull and Tog'thar were captured and locked within the ruins. Gol'dir, the expedition's leader, was taken to another Syndicate hold. Now Krusk directs Horde forces to breach Durnholde, recover the lost items, and free his comrades. From Tarren Mill, Krusk tracks Syndicate movements in Hillsbrad. The fallen nobles of Alterac operate from Durnholde Keep, plotting against Horde outposts and their former Alliance brethren. Krusk watches leaders such as Lord Aliden Perenolde. He hopes to break their command before they threaten the Horde's tenuous foothold in Lordaeron.

npc:kuray-bin.text: Kuray'bin. Outside Splintertree Post, Kuray'bin keeps watch over Ashenvale's forest trails. The Darkspear scout guards the Horde encampment from night elf scouts. Kuray'bin watches the forest outside Splintertree Post for Alliance scouts. Silverwing Sentinels patrol the canopy and send swift outrunners across the border. They gather intelligence on Horde lumber operations and defenses. Kuray'bin sends Horde fighters after the outrunners before they can report to Silverwing Outpost. Left unchecked, the scouts can become an ambushing force.

npc:kzan-thornslash.text: Kzan Thornslash. In the Valley of Trials, Kzan Thornslash equips new Horde recruits for their first trials. The orc merchant supplies weapons in Durotar. Kzan Thornslash supplies weapons to young orcs and Darkspear trolls in the Valley of Trials. They are taking their first steps as Horde warriors. He offers basic hand axes, shortswords, clubs, and staves for recruits facing local wildlife and hazards.

npc:laird.text: Laird. At Auberdine's inn, Laird sells fish and cooking supplies to travelers along Darkshore's coast. Inside Auberdine's inn, Laird sells fish and supplies. Sailors, locals, and travelers come to him as Darkshore's waters churn with dangers greater than those along Teldrassil's sheltered shores. Yet anglers willing to cast from the misty beaches can earn a handsome profit from the local catch. Laird keeps in touch with fishing operations across the channel in Teldrassil. His fellow fisher Nessa Shadowsong sends shipments from Rut'theran Village, linking it with the mainland port and keeping coastal trade moving.

npc:lakota-windsong.text: Lakota Windsong. At Darkcloud Pinnacle, Lakota Windsong waits under Grimtotem guard. Arnak Grimtotem took her after she refused his proposal. Not long after the Third War, Arnak Grimtotem began courting Lakota Windsong. She refused him and would not join his clan, but Arnak would not accept her answer. Under cover of night, he returned and killed Lakota's brother when he tried to stop him. Then Arnak carried Lakota into the jagged heights of Thousand Needles. Now she is held high above the canyon floor at Darkcloud Pinnacle, under heavy guard. Arnak still insists she will be his bride.

npc:lanka-farshot.text: Lanka Farshot. At Camp Narache, Lanka Farshot guides young tauren into the hunter’s path. He teaches tracking, marksmanship, and survival on Mulgore’s plains. At Camp Narache, Lanka Farshot welcomes new tauren called to the hunter’s path. Fresh recruits arrive with an etched note that sends them to seek his counsel. He teaches ranged combat and how to track prey. He also teaches respect for the wild beasts roaming Mulgore’s grassy plains, preparing each young hunter to scout and provide for the tribe.

npc:lar-prowltusk.text:
Lar Prowltusk. Southwest of Sen'jin Village, Lar Prowltusk keeps watch over Durotar's frontier. He guards the young troll settlement and sends travelers against nearby threats. Lar Prowltusk watches the coast southwest of Sen'jin Village. As a Darkspear sentinel, he helps guard the tribe's new home after its people fled their sunken island chain. Hostile neighbors still harass Sen'jin Village as the trolls work to secure a permanent home.

So Lar directs scouts and warriors to watch the coast and curb these attacks. He pays special attention to the Kolkar centaur, giving the settlement room to breathe.

npc:laris-geardawdle.text:
Laris Geardawdle. In Ironforge's Hall of Explorers, Laris Geardawdle welcomes travelers with samples of noxious slime. The gnome researcher gives his academic life to studying oozes across Azeroth and their strange nature and origins. In the Hall of Explorers Library, Laris Geardawdle studies how oozes begin. His dwarven colleagues pore over Titan tablets and ancient stone carvings. Laris searches Azeroth's vile, gelatinous horrors for alchemical and biological secrets.

He asks roving explorers to gather caustic samples from remote corners of the world. With those samples, he tests his unusual ideas about how these mindless puddles of malice come to life.

npc:lars.text: Lars. At a small camp on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank, Lars and Sven Yorgen struggle to survive Duskwood. Beasts, undead, and worgen roam the surrounding woods. Lars keeps to a small camp on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank, far from the uncertain safety of Darkshire. Duskwood is dangerous, with ferocious beasts, undead, and worgen in the woods. He stays close to Sven Yorgen and tries to endure the forest. Starving dire wolves prowl near Lars and Sven's camp. Lars cannot keep watch or drive them off alone, so he relies on travelers to thin their packs before the predators overrun the camp.

npc:lelanai.text: Lelanai. In Darnassus, Lelanai tends the saber mounts kept in the Cenarion Enclave. Night elves and trusted allies may earn a mount from her. Lelanai tends Kalimdor’s great cats in the Cenarion Enclave, beside Jartsam, the riding instructor. Night elves have long bonded with the fierce predators of northern forests. They train nightsabers and frostsabers to carry sentinels and scouts across rugged ground with a predator’s grace. In Darnassus, Lelanai provides these mounts to riders. Lelanai offers saber mounts to skilled night elves, while outsiders must meet a higher bar. The kaldorei hold the cats sacred and keep their distance from strangers. She entrusts a mount to a non-night elf only after they earn the highest respect and renown with Darnassus.

npc:lieutenant-haggerdin.text: Lieutenant Haggerdin. At the Headland gate, Lieutenant Haggerdin gathers recruits for the Stormpike Guard. He watches the entrance to Alterac Valley and honors Alliance champions who prove their valor against the Frostwolf Clan. At the snowy Headland above the Hillsbrad Foothills, Lieutenant Haggerdin oversees the Alliance muster for its campaign in Alterac Valley. Dwarven banners mark the massive wooden gate. Recruits and veterans gather under his watch before entering the frigid warzone. Lieutenant Haggerdin serves the Stormpike Expedition, testing warriors who would represent Ironforge and the Grand Alliance in the valley. In trials such as the Proving Grounds, recruits recover banners and relics. As soldiers rise through the Stormpike Guard, Haggerdin grants official commendations, insignias, and rank recognitions.

npc:lieutenant-lisande.text: Lieutenant Lisande. On Thunder Bluff’s high mesas, Lieutenant Lisande watches for signs of the Scourge. Lieutenant Lisande serves the Argent Dawn from Thunder Bluff, where human faces are rare. The order watches for the Lich King's taint, even in remote Kalimdor. When undead forces stir on the plains below, Lisande calls on Horde champions to ride out and investigate before the Scourge can defile the sacred earth.

npc:lieutenant-nevell.text: Lieutenant Nevell. Outside Ironforge in Dun Morogh, Lieutenant Nevell keeps watch for the Scourge. This Argent Dawn officer coordinates local defenders and warns newcomers of undead threats near the dwarven kingdom. Lieutenant Nevell watches Ironforge's snowy approaches for the Scourge. Though the Argent Dawn is best known for holding the line in Lordaeron's shattered Plaguelands, its watch reaches farther south. From outside Ironforge, Nevell directs recruits and capable adventurers toward the front when Scourge activity stirs in Dun Morogh's mountain passes. So the dwarven city's borders remain under watch.

npc:lieutenant-orrin.text: Lieutenant Orrin. At Stormwind's gates, Lieutenant Orrin calls for scouts as the Scourge stirs beyond the city. From the Valley of Heroes, he directs recruits to investigate undead threats before they reach the capital. Lieutenant Orrin watches the road from the Valley of Heroes. The Argent Dawn holds the front lines in the ruined north, yet it also guards strongholds farther south, including Stormwind City. When necromantic magic stirs beyond the capital, Orrin raises the alarm and rallies adventurers before the undead can threaten the people within. Lieutenant Orrin links the Argent Dawn with volunteers in the southern kingdom. When signs of the Scourge appear beyond Stormwind's gates, he sends scouts to gather intelligence and secure hazardous artifacts. Among the objects they recover are cracked necrotic crystals, which help the order understand and repel the undead threat.

npc:loganaar.text:
Loganaar. In Nighthaven, Loganaar guides druids from both factions in the ways of their calling. He teaches them to heed nature and prepares them for the Emerald Dream. Loganaar welcomes newly initiated druids who come to Moonglade from Darnassus or Thunder Bluff. In Nighthaven, he teaches balance, shape-shifting, and reverence for nature. Even in cold stone or unfamiliar lands, he says, tranquility must come from within. He also leads promising students toward deeper Cenarion Circle concerns.

Some druids he sends to wanderers such as Torwa Pathfinder in Un'Goro Crater. Others he guides into ancient woodland rites. Loganaar teaches that Kalimdor's traditional protectors share a deeper calling: the Emerald Dream. He speaks of the sacred bond between Azeroth's primal spirit realm and the waking world. To master their path, druids must hibernate for centuries and walk among nature's purest forms, guided by the demigods.

npc:lomac-gearstrip.text: Lomac Gearstrip. In Ironforge's Tinker Town, Lomac Gearstrip pursues gnomish inventions. He formulated the NG-5 explosive and stays in contact with fellow researchers in Kalimdor. Lomac Gearstrip works on gnomish ordnance in Ironforge's Tinker Town. Like many gnomes who fled Gnomeregan's tragedy, he brought his tinkering operations to the dwarven capital. His workshop centers on volatile chemical mixtures and specialized munitions meant to overcome heavily defended enemy strongholds. Lomac's proudest contribution to combat engineering is the NG-5 explosive. The compound is made for great destructive force and demands precise handling and rare chemical reagents. To refine and use such hazardous inventions in the field, Lomac stays in touch with former colleagues in distant theaters. They exchange technical orders and dangerous supplies across the Great Sea.

npc:longbraid-the-grim.text: Longbraid the Grim. Outside fallen Dun Modr, Longbraid the Grim keeps watch over the northern Wetlands. He mourns his brother and the loss of the Thandol Span as he leads surviving dwarves against the Dark Iron clan. Longbraid the Grim rallies the dwarven garrison near the bridge to the Arathi Highlands. The Dark Iron clan seized Dun Modr in a sudden assault and devastated its defenders. During the siege of the Thandol Span, Longbraid's brother died. Grief and hatred keep Longbraid at the northern boundary, where he directs travelers and surviving mountaineers in strikes against the Dark Iron advance. Longbraid directs dwarven operations across the Wetlands. He sent soldiers to escort Prospector Whelgar into the marshlands and works to reclaim Dun Modr's lost fortifications. He vows retribution against the Dark Iron saboteurs.

npc:loramus-thalipedes.text: Loramus Thalipedes. On a remote isle off Azshara's coast, Loramus Thalipedes keeps three felhounds close. His hunt leads to Razelikh the Defiler in the Blasted Lands. Southeast of Hetaera's Clutch, Loramus Thalipedes watches from a solitary island. An exile among his kin, he is a demon hunter who endured the agonizing ritual of blinding himself for spectral sight. Raytaf, Shahiar, and Zaman, three towering felhounds, stand around him. From the island, Loramus watches demonic corruption stir across Azeroth and keeps vigil over Azshara's shattered ruins.

npc:lord-arkkoroc.text: Lord Arkkoroc. Along Azshara’s ragged coast, Lord Arkkoroc commands the waters around his ruined temple. Loramus Thalipedes calls him a lesser deity, and the sea giants he calls his sons patrol the shore. Lord Arkkoroc holds the ruined Temple of Arkkoran above Azshara’s coast. Loramus Thalipedes, a hermit, regards the colossal sea giant as a lesser deity. His will shapes the waters around the temple. His sons patrol the crags and shallows, keeping his dominion over the shore.

npc:lord-baurles-k-wishock.text: Lord Baurles K. Wishock. In Stormwind Keep, Lord Baurles K. Wishock moves among petitioners and dignitaries. His unpaid tavern tabs and taste for strong drink have brought him close to darker dealings in the city. Lord Baurles K. Wishock belongs to the influential House of Nobles and moves among petitioners and dignitaries in Stormwind Keep. Yet he often drinks in Mage Quarter dive bars, especially the Slaughtered Lamb, and leaves large bills unpaid. There he hears of a warlock coven practicing dark arts in cellars beneath the floorboards. Wishock seeks to close the tavern and asks fellow nobles for a formal inquiry. Uncovering demonic cabals in Stormwind rarely goes unpunished.

npc:lord-grayson-shadowbreaker.text: Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker trains champions of the Light and guides promising knights. A veteran paladin commander of the Knights of the Silver Hand, he also oversees the sacred trials senior paladins must complete to claim their holy chargers. In Stormwind City, Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker leads the Silver Hand's work and stands among the Alliance's foremost defenders. A veteran of the order, he trains recruits in arms and tests their faith in the Light. When promising knights are ready, he sends them north to the contested front lines of the Western Plaguelands. There, they aid Commander Ashlam Valorfist at Chillwind Camp.

npc:lord-jorach-ravenholdt.text:
Lord Jorach Ravenholdt. At Ravenholdt Manor, Lord Jorach Ravenholdt trains rogues and directs a war against the Syndicate. His estate lies in the Alterac Mountains. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt commands the Assassin's League from a manor hidden among the crags between Alterac and Hillsbrad. A nobleman of mysterious heritage, he welcomes outlaws, cutpurses, and assassins of any allegiance, provided they show great skill and respect his authority. The league joins master thieves in espionage and killings for hire.

Ravenholdt despises the Syndicate, whose members are disgraced Alterac nobles turned outlaws. He sends his followers and visiting rogues to sabotage their camps and plunder their goods.

npc:lord-maxwell-tyrosus.text: Lord Maxwell Tyrosus. At Light's Hope Chapel, Lord Maxwell Tyrosus directs the Argent Dawn's defense against the Scourge. A veteran paladin of the Silver Hand, he also sends forces against blighted strongholds such as Stratholme. In the Third War, Maxwell Tyrosus rode with Uther the Lightbringer. He guarded Andorhal's exits as the Scourge tore through the kingdom. After Lordaeron fell, Tyrosus joined the Argent Dawn. The order welcomes anyone willing to fight the Scourge, unlike the Scarlet Crusade and its human-only zealotry. Tyrosus leads the Argent Dawn and directs the defenses of Light's Hope Chapel. From his command post inside the chapel, he oversees military operations across the Plaguelands. Among them are tactical assaults led by Duke Nicholas Zverenhoff against Baron Rivendare in the ruins of Stratholme.

npc:lord-shalzaru.text: Lord Shalzaru. On the Isle of Dread, Lord Shalzaru rules the Hatecrest naga by cruelty. His followers dig through ruined elven settlements, and the ancient relic he uncovered now draws mainland investigators. Along Feralas’s southern coast, Lord Shalzaru commands the Hatecrest naga. From his cavern lair on the Isle of Dread, he rules by force and cruelty. His followers search Kalimdor’s ancient ruins for forgotten treasures and powerful relics left by the Sundering. South of the main ruins on the Isle of Dread, Lord Shalzaru uncovered a strange ancient relic. Its purpose and power remain unknown, yet it is now held by a powerful naga warlord. Mainland operatives seek champions to enter his lair, end his command, and secure the relic before the Hatecrest turn it to darker ends.

npc:lorekeeper-raintotem.text: Lorekeeper Raintotem. South of Red Rocks, Lorekeeper Raintotem tends Mulgore’s sacred burial grounds. He asks travelers to drive off Bristleback quilboar disturbing them. Near Red Rocks in Mulgore, Lorekeeper Raintotem tends his people’s sacred burial grounds. Bristleback Interlopers disturb the resting place. He asks travelers to drive them away so the ancestors may rest in peace. At Red Rocks, Lorekeeper Raintotem watches over the burial sites. Bristleback quilboar disturb the resting places of tauren chieftains and shamans. Raintotem calls on travelers to restore quiet and dignity to the grounds and their dead.

npc:loslor-rudge.text:
Loslor Rudge. At Steelgrill's Depot, Loslor Rudge keeps Dun Morogh's tinkerers supplied. His goods travel across the snowy ridges to craftsmen such as gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot. Loslor Rudge supplies engineering goods from Steelgrill's Depot, just down the road from Kharanos. His stock holds copper modulators, bronze tubing, blasting powder, and spanners. Harsh weather and scattered tinker operations keep these parts in demand, so Loslor works to supply local gearheads.

Deliveries through the wilderness between outposts can be perilous. Near the Grizzled Den, wendigos drove off a courier taking a shortcut. The courier left behind an ammunition shipment meant for Loslor's valued client, gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot.

npc:lotwil-veriatus.text:
Lotwil Veriatus. East of Kargath, Lotwil Veriatus pursues dangerous experiments with the Badlands' elementals. The gnomish scholar works with his sarcastic apprentice Lucien Tosselwrench and mechanical attendant Servo, hoping to unite arcane theory, alchemy, and engineering. From Kharanos in Dun Morogh, Lotwil dreams of founding a grand University for his Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy, and Engineering Sciences. He believes arcane study, alchemy, and engineering belong together, not in separate pursuits. So he came to the harsh Badlands to study its native rock elementals and make shackles that bind elemental forces.

Lotwil has studied elemental machines and defeated dark iron constructs. Yet his mind stays so fixed on the work that he often misses the explosive danger of his experiments.

npc:lucius.text: Lucius. At the Lakeshire docks, Lucius watches the Redridge waterfront for Stormwind’s SI:7. The dwarf works undercover, helping agents with reconnaissance and trade skills. Lucius watches the Lakeshire docks for SI:7, Stormwind’s intelligence service. He tracks trade, unusual traffic, and threats moving into the Redridge Mountains. Agents sent east from Stormwind come to him to coordinate covert work and practice field skills such as lockpicking. Through Lucius, Stormwind reaches beyond Elwynn Forest in secret.

npc:lyria-du-lac.text: Lyria Du Lac. In Goldshire, Lyria Du Lac trains young warriors behind the village smithy. She guides them as they master their stances and arms. Behind Goldshire's forge, Lyria Du Lac trains warriors fresh from Northshire Abbey. She judges when they are ready and teaches them specialized combat techniques. Those who take up shield and blade for Stormwind must face the dangers of Elwynn Forest.

npc:ma-stonefield.text: Ma Stonefield. At Stonefield Farm in western Elwynn, Ma Stonefield tends to troubles close to home. With Auntie Bernice beside her, she faces farm hardships, rivalries with neighbors, and pests. Ma Stonefield watches over the farm beside her family's cottage in southwestern Elwynn Forest. Auntie Bernice Stonefield stays at her side. The neighboring Maclure homestead and nearby pumpkin patches bring little peace. Wild boars threaten the Stonefield crops, and Princess causes the greatest trouble. The enormous prize sow tramples fields and devours the harvest the family worked hard to grow.

npc:mad-magus-tirth.text:
Magus Tirth. At the Mirage Raceway, Magus Tirth tends chickens, serves drinks, and stakes books on the races. The human wizard lives on the Shimmering Flats, where he torments his apprentice and has wagered away valuable works. Magus Tirth makes his home beside the roaring Shimmering Flats. Mages of his skill often study in Dalaran or Stormwind, but he sells chickens and drinks to passersby. He gambles and watches the rocket cars race.

His apprentice, 'Plucky' Johnson, lives under a curse that has turned him into a chicken. Beneath Tirth’s odd habits lies true arcane mastery. He wrote esoteric books on magical power, then lost them in reckless wagers at the speedway.

npc:magga.text: Magga. Near the Den in the Valley of Trials, Magga welcomes new arrivals. She greets Horde travelers beginning their journey through the valley in Durotar. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls first meet the wider world in the Valley of Trials. Near the Den, Magga welcomes those arriving there. Trainers and recruits keep busy nearby, while she helps bring the small camp together.

npc:magis-sparkmantle.text: Magis Sparkmantle. In Kharanos, Magis Sparkmantle teaches gnome mages inside the Thunderbrew Distillery. He guides new spellcasters who come from Coldridge Valley into Dun Morogh. Dwarves come to the Thunderbrew Distillery for ale, and Magis Sparkmantle teaches among its casks and kegs. Across Dun Morogh, gnome mages work closely with their dwarven allies. Magis helps new spellcasters deepen their knowledge of the arcane and put it to practice. Magis teaches beginners their first incantations, then points promising students toward broader studies of magic. When they outgrow his early lessons or need special guidance, he sends them to other practitioners, including Bink, or to mentors in the Alliance’s main hubs.

npc:magistrate-henry-maleb.text: Magistrate Henry Maleb. In Southshore, Magistrate Henry Maleb keeps order as threats gather around the Alliance's chief coastal stronghold in Hillsbrad Foothills. The Forsaken and the Syndicate menace the port town. Magistrate Henry Maleb governs from Southshore's town hall, one of the last true Alliance settlements in Lordaeron. Forsaken forces threaten the town from the north and west, while highwaymen prowl the foothills. Maleb took office after the previous magistrate was mysteriously assassinated, and he blames the Syndicate. He means to avoid the same fate. His inquiries seek hidden assassins, Syndicate supply networks, and the nobles directing them from the ruins of Alterac.

npc:magus-rimtori.text:
Magus Rimtori. In Azshara, Magus Rimtori leads a blood elf expedition among the ancient ruins. She won passage across Kalimdor by deceiving the Horde, then slaughtered her orcish escort. Magus Rimtori brought high-borne blood elves across the sea to Azshara's ancient shores. To carry them safely through Kalimdor, she charmed and manipulated the orc Belgrom until he agreed to provide an armed escort. Once his soldiers brought her to Azshara, Rimtori turned on her protectors and slaughtered the entire garrison.

Her forces now hold the Thalassian Base Camp. Rimtori ventures into the coastal wilds with elite bodyguards, seeking forgotten magical artifacts.

npc:mai-ah.text: Mai'ah. In the Valley of Trials, Mai'ah guides young Darkspear trolls as they begin their study of magic. She prepares new spellcasters for their path among the Horde. Young Darkspear trolls come to Mai'ah in the Valley of Trials to learn magic. Orcs favor the elements or the warrior's path, while trolls have a rare gift for arcane study. Candidates bring glyphic inscriptions, and Mai'ah teaches them to shape raw power into controlled incantations. That control matters in Durotar, where danger waits beyond the den.

npc:major-mattingly.text: Major Mattingly. At Stormwind's main gates, Major Mattingly helps guard the capital and advises crafters on protection from dragons. Major Mattingly oversees Stormwind City's landward defense. In the Valley of Heroes, he stands watch under General Marcus Jonathan with the city's garrison. He oversees the gate patrols and the travelers entering the city. Dragons are deadly, and Mattingly guides skilled crafters who seek to make dragonscale gear for dangerous lairs.

npc:major-samuelson.text:
Major Samuelson. In Stormwind Keep, Major Samuelson directs the city guard and its officers. He serves in the throne room and once mentored Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Major Samuelson leads the Stormwind City Guard before the royal court. From the capital, he oversees officer postings and military orders across the realm. He once mentored Lieutenant Farren Orinelle, now stationed at Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills.

Junior commanders at distant frontier garrisons send their reports and requests for transfer to Samuelson. When they struggle, their appeals reach his desk in Stormwind.

npc:mankrik.text:
Mankrik. At the Crossroads, Mankrik searches the Barrens for his wife, Olgra. A quilboar ambush tore them apart, and grief now drives him to hunt the bristled beasts. Mankrik and his wife Olgra crossed the Barrens when quilboar swarmed them at a small tauren settlement. The fighting tore them apart, and Mankrik saw Olgra vanish beneath tusks and thorn-woven weapons. Fury drove him to fight without care. Then a blow left him unconscious.

Along the Gold Road, a passing tauren druid found Mankrik bleeding out and bound his injuries. He survived the ambush, but Olgra was gone. At the Crossroads, Mankrik recovers, paralyzed by grief and consumed by bloodlust. Thork and other local leaders warn that hatred has clouded his judgment, so they refuse to send official war parties. Mankrik will not move on.

Unsure of Olgra's fate, he calls on willing Horde travelers to search the Barrens for signs of his lost mate. He asks them to slaughter any quilboar they meet.

npc:marcus-redpath.text:
Marcus Redpath. In Southshore, Marshal Marcus Redpath rallies patrols and bounty hunters to hold Lordaeron’s last southern coastal bastion. Ogres, murlocs, and naga press against the town. Marshal Marcus Redpath commands Southshore’s defense on the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills. The Alliance port endured the fall of Lordaeron’s capital and the Scourge invasion. Redpath now protects the survivors who remain in town. Southshore stands nearly alone as hostile forces press in from every side. Marshal Redpath coordinates the defense across the Hillsbrad Foothills and calls on seasoned adventurers to drive back the Crushridge ogres advancing from Alterac. He also sends them against dangerous naga and murloc camps along the coast.

The Forsaken hold the north, and nearby Tarren Mill is heavily fortified. Redpath’s vigilance keeps the Alliance presence in the region from collapsing.

npc:mardant-strongoak.text:
Mardant Strongoak. In Aldrassil, Mardant Strongoak guides young night elves who take up the druid’s path. He teaches them to commune with nature and learn of the Emerald Dream. Young night elves in Aldrassil who feel the call of the wild turn to Mardant Strongoak. He teaches new druids to open their senses to nature spirits, hear their murmurs, and channel healing magic.

Those beginning their work as protectors of the wild learn from him first. He introduces them to the mysteries and ancient perils of the Emerald Dream.

npc:marek-ironheart.text: Marek Ironheart. At the Farstrider Lodge in south-eastern Loch Modan, Marek Ironheart tests hunters who seek the lodge’s respect. The veteran dwarf follows the traditions of the wild. The Farstrider Lodge gathers marksmen and trackers from across the dwarven lands on a ridge above the lake. Marek cares little for titles or boasts. Visitors earn the hunters’ respect through skill against Loch Modan’s beasts, and by showing a true hunter’s patience and nerve.

npc:marisa-du-paige.text: Marisa du'Paige. In the caves outside the Deadmines, Marisa du'Paige fights beside Moonbrook's outlaws. Few of their laborers and highwaymen wield arcane magic in southwestern Westfall. Beneath Moonbrook, caves lead toward the Deadmines. Cutpurses, renegade miners, and thugs guard those tunnels. Among them is Marisa du'Paige, a skilled human mage. Many spellcasters train in Stormwind's Mage Quarter or serve the Kirin Tor, but Marisa has joined Westfall's outlaws and brigands in their underground passages.

npc:marleth-barleybrew.text: Marleth Barleybrew. At Brewnall Village, Marleth Barleybrew works to prove her family’s ale can rival Thunder Ale. The Thunderbrew clan’s hold on local beer trade frustrates her, and she seeks to put Barleybrew brew before drinkers. In Dun Morogh, beer matters as much as steel, and the Barleybrew and Thunderbrew rivalry is legendary. Ragnar Thunderbrew and his kin control nearly all the beer trade from their Kharanos distillery. Marleth Barleybrew believes her family’s brew is just as strong, but she will not challenge the Thunderbrews openly. Instead, she recruits travelers to secretly replace Kharanos tavern casks with Barleybrew kegs.

npc:marryk-nurribit.text: Marryk Nurribit. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Marryk Nurribit teaches young gnomes the first steps in arcane magic. Local brews often draw his attention from lessons, and he asks pupils for spare coins to buy a drink. Every newly arrived gnome mage in Coldridge Valley starts out as Marryk's pupil. Yet a flagon of dwarven ale can win more of his attention than a lesson. He asks new pupils for spare pocket change, and warns aspiring spellcasters about Gnomeregan's radioactive, trogg-infested ruins beyond Coldridge Valley.

npc:marshal-maxwell.text:
Marshal Maxwell. At Morgan's Vigil, Marshal Maxwell holds the northern ridge against the Blackrock clan and Dark Iron dwarves. The Stormwind officer directs scouts through the hostile crags and searches for his captured comrade, Marshal Reginald Windsor. Marshal Maxwell commands Stormwind's detachment at Morgan's Vigil on the southern rim of the Burning Steppes. The outpost overlooks ash, dragonkin, and Blackrock orcs. Travelers crossing the fiery crags find a rare friendly post here.

From the rocky ridge, Maxwell directs the defense against mountain threats before they can move south into Redridge and Elwynn.

npc:martie-jainrose.text:
Martie Jainrose. In Lakeshire, Martie Jainrose tends her garden beside Lake Everstill. She gathers herbs and flowers for the town, though wild beasts threaten her plots. She seems fond of Guard Parker. Lakeshire's herbalist, Martie Jainrose, gathers herbs and flowers for the town. Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and local brigands threaten the Redridge Mountains, yet she keeps Lakeshire supplied with fresh herbs and floral arrangements. Wild animals trouble her work, especially Bellygrub, a monstrous boar that often ravages her garden beds.

Martie also seems fond of Guard Parker. Parker is courting Darcy, who calls Martie a jealous rival.

npc:marukai.text: Marukai. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Marukai holds the Horde's beachhead against the Wrathtail naga. The Darkspear troll directs the fight along Ashenvale's foggy northwest coast. Marukai works to keep Zoram'gar Outpost from being overwhelmed. The encampment lies on the northern edge of the Zoram Strand, amid ancient ruins, hostile night elf territory and the restless sea. Wrathtail naga rise in force from the waters and elven ruins to claim the shoreline. Marukai sends Horde champions to drive them back into the tide and take their heads, so the outpost can hold the coast.

npc:master-apothecary-lydon.text: Apothecary Lydon. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon studies poisons for the Royal Apothecary Society. Bored and sunk in gloom, he takes pleasure in lethal brews and the suffering they cause. His research seeks to secure Hillsbrad for the Forsaken and advance Sylvanas's New Plague. In Tarren Mill's chapel, now a laboratory, Apothecary Lydon does the cold work of the Royal Apothecary Society. The flowers and crisp air of Hillsbrad Foothills deepen his melancholy. Deathcraft alone lifts his gloom. Left to himself, he poisons, dissects, and reanimates his pet frog, Umpi, again and again as he waits for new reagents.

npc:master-vornal.text: Master Vornal. In Sen'jin Village, Master Vornal brews for the Darkspear and guards the craft he has mastered. Though age has touched him, the elderly jungle troll refuses to teach an apprentice. Master Vornal makes draughts and spirits for his fellow Darkspear trolls in Sen'jin Village. Age is catching up with him, yet he will not give up his independence. He refuses to train an apprentice and mixes every remedy and volatile brew himself. At times, Master Vornal sends young adventurers into the surrounding lands for harsh or unusual ingredients. He uses them in solvents and other mixtures, and rewards those who bring them back. Yet he keeps his methods and recipes to himself, doing all the brewing by his own hand.

npc:mastok-wrilehiss.text: Mastok Wrilehiss. At Splintertree Post, Mastok Wrilehiss works to hold the Horde’s ground in Ashenvale. He directs scouts and warriors to watch nearby borders and face corrupting elemental forces amid the night elves’ hostility. Splintertree Post lies beneath Ashenvale’s canopy, surrounded by hostile night elf territory. Mastok Wrilehiss helps defend the outpost and watches its supply routes and the forest beyond. The Sentinels see the settlement as an intrusion on their lands. They strike quickly when they sense weakness. From inside the stockade, Mastok Wrilehiss gives passing adventurers duties in the Horde’s defense. He watches the borders toward the Stonetalon Mountains and sends scouts to speak with shamans such as Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring at Zoram'gar Strand. He also follows the strange corruption afflicting local elementals.

npc:mathredis-firestar.text:
Mathredis Firestar. At Flame Crest, Mathredis Firestar binds Lesser Arcanums in the Burning Steppes. He relies on his dead mentor’s research and the energy released by each binding. At Flame Crest in the Burning Steppes, Mathredis Firestar crafts Lesser Arcanums from his mentor Telmius Dreamseeker’s work. Telmius died in Dire Maul’s ancient ruins while seeking magical secrets from the Shen'dralar. He invented the bindings, but Mathredis cannot yet make the greatest arcanums. So he turns to lesser ones.

His craft is more than study. Like other blood elves since the Sunwell fell, Mathredis hungers for arcane power. Binding materials to ancient librams releases violent magical discharges. He draws on that energy to sustain himself. Mathredis accepts the proper tomes, including the Librams of Constitution, Resilience, Rumination, Tenacity, or Voracity, along with rare reagents. He binds the volatile reagents to the text and concentrates their essence into an arcanum. The finished arcanum permanently enchants headwear or leg armor.

When adventurers bring the components, Mathredis trades his craft for payment and the arcane sustenance he craves.

npc:maur-grimtotem.text: Maur Grimtotem. Beneath Orgrimmar, Maur Grimtotem lies dead in Ragefire Chasm. Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem sent him to seek peace with the troggs, and his body and satchel remain in the caverns. Maur Grimtotem entered Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar as an envoy to the troggs. Most of the Horde saw them as savage brutes beyond negotiation. Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem believed peace might be possible, or at least said so. Maur carried her offer into the winding caverns. The troggs killed him, and his body remains under the watch of their chieftain, Oggleflint.

npc:maur-raincaller.text: Maur Raincaller. In Bloodhoof Village, Maur Raincaller tends to Mulgore’s herds and wild beasts. He answers concerns tied to the plains’ natural and spiritual life. Maur Raincaller lives near the heart of Bloodhoof Village, on Lake Stonebull’s shore. He watches over Mulgore’s wildlife and the balance of the elements. Then the strider Mazzranache bites him and infects his wound. Maur asks young travelers to gather animal parts for a remedy.

npc:maurin-bonesplitter.text: Maurin Bonesplitter. At Ghost Walker Post, Maurin Bonesplitter watches the Burning Blade in Desolace. Keldran sent the Forsaken scholar to watch the cult's demonic activity. Maurin draws on ancient lore to undermine the cult and scorns its members as fools blind to the dark powers directing them. At Ghost Walker Post, Maurin Bonesplitter is one of the few undead among the tauren and Horde residents. He is a learned spellcaster rather than a soldier, with deep knowledge of forbidden histories and occult forces. His learning and sharp mind caught Keldran's attention. So Keldran sent Maurin to Desolace to watch the growing demonic presence and direct focused attacks against it. Across Desolace, Maurin reserves much of his scorn for the Burning Blade. He despises their reckless ambition and mocks them for mistaking borrowed power for their own. To him, they are thralls blind to the demonic masters who bind them. Maurin uses scrying spells and ritual knowledge to enlist Horde adventurers in disrupting the cult's summonings and weakening its operations across the barren landscape.

npc:maxan-anvol.text: Maxan Anvol. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Maxan Anvol teaches dwarven priests the ways of the Holy Light. Before acolytes earn the Church’s vestments, he puts their faith to the test. Beyond his teaching, Maxan Anvol looks after the spiritual needs of Kharanos. Travelers, mountaineers, and acolytes gather there, for the hamlet lies between Coldridge Valley and Ironforge. Its inn draws those passing through. Maxan offers prayer and counsel to all who enter, with stout close at hand. Before novice priests venture into the wider world, Maxan Anvol tests their faith and skill. He sends initiates to use simple healing prayers on Dun Morogh’s wounded defenders. Those who prove devoted and skilled receive their first priestly vestments, a mark of their place in the Church of the Holy Light.

npc:maybell-maclure.text: Maybell Maclure. At the Maclure Vineyards, Maybell Maclure loves a Stonefield, though the families’ feud keeps her apart from Tommy Joe Stonefield. Maybell Maclure tends her family’s vineyards beside the Stonefield farm. She loves Tommy Joe Stonefield, heir to the neighboring farm. Their families’ long feud keeps them apart, and Maybell seeks a way to speak with him beyond her family’s watchful eyes.

npc:melithar-staghelm.text: Melithar Staghelm. Outside Aldrassil in Shadowglen, Melithar Staghelm guides young night elves. He sends them to learn why Tarindrella has returned to the glade. His name recalls Archdruid Fandral Staghelm, though their connection remains unknown. Outside Aldrassil, Melithar Staghelm guides night elves taking their first steps into the world. A druid who listens to the forest spirits, he has learned that Tarindrella, a woodland protector, has returned to Shadowglen after years away. Sensing trouble, Melithar sends newcomers southwest of Aldrassil to find her and learn why she has come back to the grove. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus after Malfurion Stormrage disappeared into the Emerald Dream. That makes Melithar's shared name draw notice. Yet Melithar says nothing of his lineage and claims no grand heritage. Whether he belongs to the Archdruid's family or shares an ancient Kaldorei name remains unknown. For now, he tends to his humble duties at Aldrassil's roots.

npc:merissa-stilwell.text: Merissa Stilwell. At Northshire Abbey, Merissa Stilwell greets newcomers to Northshire Valley. The young human offers a cheerful welcome and a helping hand to those training nearby. From Northshire Abbey, Merissa Stilwell welcomes fresh recruits arriving in Northshire Valley. She offers simple hospitality and practical advice on resting and finding the way. Her surname is shared by craftsmen and homesteaders across the kingdom, including the blacksmith Jordan Stilwell and the Westfall defender Daphne Stilwell. Amid the kingdom's rising tensions, Merissa remains a peaceful local presence.

npc:merrin-rockweaver.text: Merrin Rockweaver. On a ridge above Whelgar's Excavation Site, Merrin Rockweaver waits with the survivors. Raptors drove them from the dig, where she represented the Explorers' League. Merrin Rockweaver came to the Wetlands for the Ironforge Explorers' League. Beneath the muck, the expedition sought ancient Titan secrets. Then the crew unearthed large bones, and raptors came to the dig. The beasts swarmed the trenches, forcing Merrin and the surviving crew to flee. They left their equipment, notes, and progress behind. Now Merrin and a few survivors are trapped on a bluff above the overrun ruins. The survivors on the bluff still hope to save what they can of the expedition. Ormer Ironbraid plans to take vengeance on the beasts, while Prospector Whelgar searches the raptor-infested trenches for tablet fragments. Merrin fears for her husband Tarrel, who has heard nothing from her in weeks. Longbraid sent a scout to find the team, and that scout can carry word of their plight back to Tarrel.

npc:miles-welsh.text: Miles Welsh. Beneath Thunder Bluff, Miles Welsh teaches priests in the Pools of Vision. The Forsaken trainer offers spiritual instruction and shadow discipline in the tauren capital. In the Pools of Vision, Miles Welsh teaches priests beneath Thunder Bluff. Far from Lordaeron's plague-scarred ruins, the Forsaken priest makes his home in the grotto beneath the city. He instructs travelers in divine and shadowy energies. His place in the heart of Mulgore reflects the tenuous ties between the Forsaken and the Horde. There, he shares sanctuary with tauren mystics and shamans while guiding acolytes in shadow and faith.

npc:milli-featherwhistle.text: Milli Featherwhistle. At Steelgrill's Depot, Milli Featherwhistle builds and maintains mechanostriders for Gnomeregan's displaced people. She sells these clockwork mounts to her kin and to trusted allies among the exiles. Just east of Kharanos, Milli works outdoors in Dun Morogh's biting chill. She tunes each mount's gears, pistons, and balancing gyros to carry riders across the snowy crags. Dwarves and night elves favor living mounts. For Gnomeregan's displaced people, Milli's clockwork steeds meet a different need. Milli follows the blueprints first drawn by High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque. She has improved each mechanostrider's performance by lightening its chassis and refining its exhaust vents. Yet she keeps to the High Tinker's original designs. Her work carries gnomish ambition forward, even in exile.

npc:milton-sheaf.text: Milton Sheaf. In Stormwind Keep, Milton Sheaf tends the Royal Library and calls on Alliance travelers to recover lost books and records. Milton Sheaf tends the Royal Library inside Stormwind Keep. While the court weighs politics, noble disputes, and military concerns, he preserves the written record. To him, accurate histories of the Alliance and the Eastern Kingdoms are a duty, especially amid war, loss, and instability. Milton Sheaf sends travelers across the realm to recover scattered books. Volumes wear with use, while records rest in monastic archives, distant outposts, and forgotten ruins. From Northshire Abbey to Southshore in the north, he sends Alliance adventurers to retrieve misplaced books, examine ancient texts, and return rare manuscripts safely to the keep.

npc:minor-manifestation-of-earth.text:
Minor Manifestation of Earth. At sacred stones in Mulgore and Durotar, Minor Manifestation of Earth waits beyond ordinary sight. Fledgling shamans who drink Earth Sapta can meet the spirit and receive rough quartz for carving their first earth totem. Earth spirits dwell beneath dirt and stone, but a rite is needed to reach them. At Kodo Rock in Mulgore and Spirit Rock in Durotar, Minor Manifestations of Earth linger beyond ordinary sight, among lesser elemental presences. Only initiates who drink Earth Sapta, brewed by shamanic mentors, can cross from the physical world into the elements.

When an initiate makes contact, the spirit grants the earth's blessings and a piece of rough quartz. The novice can use it as the spiritual focus for making an Earth Totem.

npc:minor-manifestation-of-water.text: Minor Manifestation of Water. Along North Tide's Run, the Minor Manifestation of Water waits for shamans on Silverpine Forest's coast. First, its corrupted counterpart must be defeated before the peaceful spirit will speak. West of the Sepulcher, the Minor Manifestation of Water waits along North Tide's Run. For a shaman in training, meeting the spirit is an essential rite. Water elementals embody life, renewal, and fluidity, yet a malevolent blight can corrupt them. An initiate must face and defeat a corrupted manifestation before the pure spirit reveals itself. Once the corruption is cleansed, the spirit guides shamans on their sacred journey to fashion a Water Totem.

npc:misha.text: Misha. Beside Rexxar, Misha roams Kalimdor as his loyal bear companion. Rexxar is the half-ogre beastmaster and Champion of the Horde, and she stays close as he travels. Misha walks beside Rexxar, a solitary half-ogre who trusts beasts more than people. The brown bear and the wandering beastmaster have forged a fierce, protective bond through many wildernesses and bloody battles. Misha is a seasoned warrior, not merely a tame pet. She fought beside Rexxar against Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore at Theramore Isle, helping secure the young Horde's survival. Away from battle, her keen senses and strength extend Rexxar's will. Travelers on the long tracks through the Stonetalon Mountains, Desolace, and Feralas may find Misha padding beside Rexxar. She is fierce enough to tear apart any predator that threatens them. In an untrustworthy world, she remains Rexxar's steadfast anchor.

npc:misha-tor-kren.text: Misha Tor'kren. At the Tor'kren Farm in western Durotar, Misha Tor'kren waits for word of her son. Kron went west toward the Southfury River to hunt crocolisks, but has not returned. Misha Tor'kren tends her farm southeast of Thunder Ridge, near the ridge. Her son Kron went west toward the Southfury River to hunt crocolisks and prove his mettle. He never came home. Durotar's frontier dangers stretch the orcish watchtowers thin, and Misha has heard no word of him. She needs travelers to search the riverbanks for signs of her son.

npc:mitsuwa.text: Mitsuwa. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Mitsuwa mourns a group of trolls slain on their journey through Ashenvale. He calls on Horde champions to recover their stolen charms. At Zoram'gar Outpost on the Zoram Strand, Mitsuwa serves the Horde alongside Marukai. Thistlefur furbolgs from northern Ashenvale ambushed and slaughtered a group of traveling trolls bound for the outpost. Mitsuwa sees their deaths as a grave offense. He sends warriors to the Thistlefur dens to reclaim the stolen charms and honor his kin's spirits.

npc:monte-gazlowe.text:
Monte Gazlowe. At Ratchet, Monte Gazlowe keeps the port open to traders from every side. He founded the town with the fortune he earned as the Horde’s chief engineer during the building of Durotar and Orgrimmar. Monte Gazlowe runs Ratchet under the Steamwheedle Cartel, where rivals meet to trade. He founded the town on the barren coast after earning a handsome payday for engineering work with the new Horde. Horde, Alliance, and independent traders may barter there, so long as they keep their weapons sheathed and their purses heavy. After the Third War, Warchief Thrall hired Monte Gazlowe as Durotar’s chief engineer to solve urgent problems for the new orc capital. Gazlowe took on the dangerous work of securing freshwater for Orgrimmar. His tunnels broke into underground kobold dens, but the wandering beastmaster Rexxar arrived in time to help blast the caverns shut.

Gazlowe finished his assignments and remains a favored contractor and friend to Thrall. He has even sent his foreman, Rezlak, to keep helping with orc construction across Durotar. Trade brings good earnings to Ratchet, but maritime rivals and thieves trouble Monte Gazlowe’s business. The Southsea Freebooters have camps along the nearby Merchant Coast, where they seize cargo bound for Ratchet and steal goods from raw ore to Gazlowe’s custom-ordered boots.

To protect his profits, the port boss often hires passing sellswords of any allegiance to clear pirate camps, recover stolen shipments, and settle scores with troublemakers at the docks.

npc:moon-priestess-amara.text: Moon Priestess Amara. West of Dolanaar, Moon Priestess Amara keeps watch over the road to Darnassus. Two huntresses stand guard beside her as she watches Teldrassil’s woodland paths. Moon Priestess Amara watches the road west of Dolanaar with Nhemai and Yaeliura, two huntress companions. As a priestess of the Sisterhood of Elune, she offers spiritual guidance while helping keep Teldrassil’s roads secure. Travelers bound for Darnassus can seek directions from her. Those burdened in spirit can also ask her for a path to redemption.

npc:mor-rogal.text: Mor'rogal. At Sun Rock Retreat, Mor'rogal sends Horde travelers toward the dangers and promise of the Stonetalon Mountains. Deep crevices and caverns cut into the Stonetalon Mountains, and Mor'rogal keeps his eye on them. Their twisting passages may hold riches, but they can also bring deadly danger. So Mor'rogal sends brave Horde wanderers to troubled places such as Boulderslide Ravine. Facing those depths tests the spirit of anyone who seeks glory with heart and soul.

npc:morgan-pestle.text: Morgan Pestle. At Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind, Morgan Pestle handles the capital's supplies and alchemical research. He works with his brother William Pestle in Goldshire. Morgan Pestle sells alchemical goods, reagents, and remedies from Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. His brother William keeps a workshop at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, while Morgan tends their family trade in the capital. Supplies come from the rural heartlands, including candles William sends north.

npc:morgan-the-collector.text: Morgan the Collector. At the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, Morgan the Collector directs Defias extortion and gathers stolen goods across Elwynn Forest. From the farmhouse, he coordinates the theft while Goldshire's guard watches nearby. Morgan the Collector takes gold from Elwynn Forest's mines for the Defias Brotherhood. Common bandits harass travelers on the roads, but Morgan directs organized shakedowns. He gathers stolen coin and supplies for the Brotherhood's wider network. His headquarters is the farmhouse at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, where loyal enforcers including Surena Caledon and Erlan Drudgemoor surround him.

npc:mountaineer-barleybrew.text: Mountaineer Barleybrew. At South Gate Outpost, Mountaineer Barleybrew keeps watch over the pass from Dun Morogh to Loch Modan. Dwarven brews help sentries endure the cold. Mountaineer Wellart Barleybrew watches the snowy road to Loch Modan from South Gate Outpost. He serves in Ironforge's border watch. Like other mountaineers in Dun Morogh's bitter winds, he values fine dwarven drink. His name ties him to the renowned Barleybrew clan. He also helps send potent Shimmer Stout to watchmen who need warmth and stamina through long shifts in the mountain passes.

npc:mountaineer-kadrell.text: Mountaineer Kadrell. Across from the Stoutlager Inn in Thelsamar, Mountaineer Kadrell keeps watch over Loch Modan. Mountaineer Kadrell watches over Thelsamar and directs Loch Modan’s dwarven defenses. Troggs, gnolls, and native beasts press against outposts along the valley’s edges. From the town’s center, Kadrell sends reinforcements, relays orders, and considers reports from scouts in the field. Mountaineer Kadrell stays in touch with Thelsamar’s distant forward posts. He coordinates with Mountaineer Stormpike and sends adventurers to report to sentries such as Mountaineer Rockgar. The outposts guard the mountain passes, so Kadrell helps supply them, reinforce their ranks, and carry word of threats.

npc:mountaineer-stormpike.text: Mountaineer Stormpike. At Algaz Station, Mountaineer Stormpike keeps watch over Loch Modan's northern road into the Wetlands. A proud member of Ironforge's Stormpike clan, he guards its supply routes from troggs and kobolds. Mountaineer Stormpike guards the northern road from Algaz Station, where Loch Modan gives way to Dun Algaz. The road descends through the pass into the Wetlands, amid rocky crags and wilderness threats. Stormpike keeps communication open and the way clear for travelers and supply convoys crossing the pass. Kobolds from nearby digs and troggs from beneath the ground trouble northern Loch Modan. Stormpike calls on passing adventurers to disrupt these threats. Kobolds have entered Silver Stream Mine and taken the Miners' League's stored dwarven tools.

npc:mountaineer-thalos.text: Mountaineer Thalos. At Coldridge Pass, Mountaineer Thalos guards the road toward Kharanos, where couriers bring urgent reports. Troggs have overrun the tunnel, and he decides who may cross safely. Troggs have burrowed up from below and made Coldridge Pass dangerous. At its snowy mouth, where Coldridge Valley gives way to Dun Morogh’s deeper crags, Thalos turns back travelers who are not ready. He tests whether couriers have the grit to face the infested tunnel. If they cannot get through, their reports may never reach the wider kingdom. Grelin Whitebeard reports Frostmane troll movements in the secluded valley. A courier carries his account to Grelin’s brother Senir in Kharanos, but first must speak with Mountaineer Thalos. Thalos sends capable travelers through the pass toward Kharanos, where regional commanders coordinate Dun Morogh’s defense. Vital intelligence must reach Ironforge’s military leaders, not vanish in the snow.

npc:mupsi-shacklefridd.text: Mupsi Shacklefridd. Outside Ratchet in the Barrens, Mupsi Shacklefridd helps travelers mend their ties with the Steamwheedle Cartel. Along the coastal road outside Ratchet, Mupsi Shacklefridd helps travelers regain favor with the Steamwheedle Cartel. Steamwheedle guards patrol the edge of the port town as merchants come and go. If the goblins have turned against you, Mupsi offers a way back into their good graces, provided you bring the supplies and labor they demand.

npc:mux-manascrambler.text:
Mux Manascrambler. In Gadgetzan, Mux Manascrambler turns his craft to spirits and occult forces. The goblin engineer studies what others cannot see. Near the center of Gadgetzan, Mux Manascrambler works inside a building behind Driz Plunkbow and his clanking Butcherbots. The Steamwheedle Cartel trades in oil, guns, and salvage, but Mux pursues spirits and supernatural anomalies.

He builds strange devices to detect and distill spectral remnants, and to interact with them. His work brings goblin engineering into the unseen world of the dead.

npc:mydrannul.text: Mydrannul. At the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, Mydrannul keeps basic supplies ready for sentinels, soldiers, and visitors. Mydrannul tends a supply stall among the Warrior's Terrace military pavilions and training grounds. There, Darnassus's defenders and travelers find everyday field gear, from ammunition for archers and gunners to throwing blades, flint, pouches, and simple rations. Sentinels and trainees preparing for duty on Teldrassil can gather the sundries they need.

npc:nalpak.text: Nalpak. Above the Wailing Caverns, Nalpak keeps watch from a cliff-cave. The tauren druid remains faithful to Naralex's vision and guards against the corruption below. Nalpak watches from a hidden cave above the Wailing Caverns' mouth. He remains loyal to Naralex's vision while his master lies trapped in a corrupted slumber below. To hold back the spreading corruption, Nalpak asks passing adventurers to gather deviate hides for leather.

npc:nara-meideros.text: Nara Meideros. In Stormwind's Park, Nara Meideros guides young seekers in Elune's teachings. As a night elf priestess in the human capital, she gives her kin a familiar presence of faith. Across the Great Sea from Kalimdor, Nara Meideros serves Elune in Stormwind City. Night elf druids and priests tend a green refuge in the Park, where she guides young seekers in devotion to the Moon Goddess. Nearby, human priests serve the Holy Light in Cathedral Square. Nara keeps night elves visiting or living in the Eastern Kingdoms close to their own faith.

npc:narain-soothfancy.text: Narain Soothfancy. Along Tanaris’s eastern shore, Narain Soothfancy offers visitors his visions. The gnome lives in a secluded hut just north of Steamwheedle Port, though those who know him value his engineering more than his prophecies. Narain Soothfancy, a retired engineer, lives on Tanaris’s eastern coast just north of the goblin docks. He greets visitors with unopened envelopes pressed to his forehead or guesses at their business. Sometimes he asks if they seek the legendary Ashbringer. His fortune-telling is a show, but his technical knowledge is real. Even the blue dragon Azuregos calls Narain a poor psychic and a brilliant engineer. Nearby rests a handbook titled Soothsaying for Dummies. Narain Soothfancy survived a flying machine crash far south along Land’s End Beach before settling near Steamwheedle Port. An unexpected rescue saved him from the wreck. His eccentric nature and strange obsessions have kept him isolated on the desert shore. There he tinkers with arcane-adjacent technology and offers dubious prophecies to passersby.
