npc:nat-pagle.text: Nat Pagle. On a quiet inlet in Dustwallow Marsh, Nat Pagle fishes and teaches anglers who have proved their patience. He calls fishing an excuse to drink, yet anglers across Azeroth know his mastery. For decades, Nat Pagle has fished the waters of Azeroth. He speaks of the craft without much reverence, calling it a handy excuse to sit back and drink. Yet he knows aquatic life and angling better than anyone alive. He also licenses fishing gear sought by professionals. Nat Pagle makes camp on a small spit along Dustwallow Marsh’s eastern coast, far from the taverns of the Eastern Kingdoms. He keeps clear of faction politics. Alliance travelers sent by trainers such as Grimnur Stonebrand come to him, and so do Horde anglers directed by Lumak in Orgrimmar. Anyone searching the world for rare specimens can earn a lesson from Nat. Nat Pagle once ventured into the ruins of Zul'Gurub. Near waters prowled by the monstrous hydra Gahz'ranka, he misplaced his favorite measuring tape and tackle box.

npc:natalia-mar-alith.text: Natalia Mar'alith. Deep in Hive'Regal, Natalia Mar'alith has vanished among the silithid. The night elf priestess and Cenarion Circle researcher entered the wastes of Silithus with her husband, Commander Mar'alith, then went on an expedition into the hives. At Cenarion Hold, the Cenarion Circle watches the awakening sands. Natalia joined her husband, Commander Mar'alith, in the wastes, hoping to learn why the silithid were returning and what lay among the ancient Qiraji ruins. She then joined an expedition led by Brann Bronzebeard, the famed explorer, with the dwarven researchers Rutgar Glyphshaper and Frankal Stonebridge.

npc:nathanos-blightcaller.text:
Nathanos Blightcaller. At the ruined Marris Stead in the Eastern Plaguelands, Nathanos Blightcaller guards the frontier for Queen Sylvanas Windrunner. Once the only human Ranger Lord of Quel'Thalas, he now trains Forsaken hunters and greets those who approach with biting contempt. Nathanos Marris was raised on Lordaeron's rural outskirts and became a master marksman and a gifted tactician. The high elves of Quel'Thalas trained him, and he grew close to Sylvanas Windrunner. He alone among humans earned the rank of Ranger Lord. The Marris Stead remained his family home. After Prince Arthas and the Scourge swept through Lordaeron following the purge of Stratholme, plague consumed the kingdom. Nathanos made a desperate stand at the Marris Stead, where Ramstein the Gorger, a monstrous abomination, killed him. Raised as a mindless undead thrall, he roamed the blighted fields and slew in the Lich King's name.

Sylvanas broke the Scourge's hold and established the Forsaken in the Undercity. She came for Nathanos, just as he had somehow known she would, and freed his mind from the Lich King's will. His tactical brilliance and fiery loyalty returned, and he joined her side.

npc:nida.text: Hilary. At the Lakeshire docks, Hilary weeps over the necklace she lost in Lake Everstill. Hilary waits by the Lakeshire pier in tears. She fears her father will be angry because she dropped the necklace he gave her into Lake Everstill. Now she hopes someone brave will dive in and find it. Gnoll invasions and Blackrock orc warbands press upon Lakeshire, yet children there have troubles of their own.

npc:nikova-raskol.text: Nikova Raskol. In Old Town, Nikova Raskol seeks justice for her murdered grandson. The elderly Stormwind townswoman turns to adventurers as the Defias Brotherhood rioters remain locked in the Stockade. Nikova Raskol walks Old Town with grief for her beloved grandson, Mac. Defias Brotherhood brigands slew him. The kingdom faces treason on a grand scale, yet Nikova bears the private cost of the Brotherhood's lawless rampage. Many criminals who wreaked havoc were captured and locked in the Stockade. Now a violent inmate rebellion has seized the prison, and the guards have failed to restore order. Nikova turns to adventurers heading inside. She asks them to bring back red Defias bandanas as proof that her grandson's killers have faced retribution.

npc:nissa-firestone.text: Nissa Firestone. Above Ironforge’s Great Forge, Nissa Firestone teaches field medicine to travelers and soldiers. Nissa Firestone tends patients upstairs in the Ironforge Physician shop. The Great Forge’s clang and heat reach her there, while she binds their wounds. Dwarven warriors can endure much, yet blades and claws still break their skin. Before travelers and soldiers set out into Dun Morogh’s snows or farther afield, Nissa teaches basic bandaging and field dressings. These skills can help keep them and their allies alive. Nissa Firestone teaches field medics how to use cloth and lint. When she has taught all she can, she directs them to specialized triage officers in distant outposts. Skilled healers go where Alliance casualties are heaviest.

npc:nogg.text: Nogg. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Nogg puts his craft to work for the Horde. He studies strange mechanical salvage from deep within Gnomeregan. Nogg keeps an independent engineering workshop in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. Adventurers and craftsmen seek the mechanical skill of a goblin in a city famed for orcish steel and strength. He eagerly examines unusual devices and trinkets brought from Alliance lands or underground ruins. Salvage from Gnomeregan draws Nogg's special attention. Horde operatives recover intricate rings and other remnants from the fallen gnomish capital. Few minds in Durotar can take apart those strange clockwork devices, decipher them, and adapt them for Horde use.

npc:nori-pridedrift.text: Nori Pridedrift. In Coldridge Valley, Nori Pridedrift sends warm Mornbrew out to those who face the cold. He brews and sells the drink, hiring swift couriers to carry it while it is still hot. Nori Pridedrift sends Scalding Mornbrew across the frozen reaches of Coldridge Valley. The cold bites hard, and a cup brings welcome warmth to mountaineers and freezing sentries. Nori brews the coffee-like drink, then sends it out with couriers who must race the mountain air to keep it scalding. His supply of sturdy mugs is limited, so he expects runners to bring them back promptly.

npc:novice-elreth.text: Novice Elreth. At Deathknell's chapel, Novice Elreth guides the newly risen Forsaken. She sends them against the mindless Scourge near the graves and helps them face the sorrow left by the plague. Within Deathknell's desecrated chapel, Novice Elreth guides the newly risen undead. They struggle to understand their horrific awakening, while the Forsaken must organize quickly to secure their territory. Elreth sends them south to gather paws from wolves and wings from bats. She also directs them toward Lordaeron's tragic aftermath, including the sorrow of her friend Marla Fipps. Marla's husband Samuel killed her after joining the mindless Scourge.

npc:oben-rageclaw.text: Oben Rageclaw. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Oben Rageclaw's spirit wanders, unable to wake or pass on. The Gnarlpine furbolgs still control his sleeping body. Oben Rageclaw entered Ban'ethil Barrow Den to commune with nature and wander the Emerald Dream, as many Druids of the Claw do. When the Gnarlpine furbolgs fell to corruption and overran the barrows, he lay defenseless in his trance. A corrupted Gnarlpine shaman used dark rituals to take control of Oben's comatose body. His spirit remained behind as an anguished ghost, unable to wake or pass on.

npc:ogtinc.text: Ogtinc. High above the Ruins of Eldarath in Azshara, Ogtinc guides hunters who seek to test their craft against Kalimdor’s fiercest beasts. He left his tribe to serve nature and became a trusted ally and mentor to the Cenarion Circle. Ogtinc camps on a bluff southeast of Timbermaw Hold and keeps watch over Azshara’s shattered lands. He left his kin and gave his bow and knowledge of survival to the Cenarion Circle. Many furbolg remain bound to their tribes, while others fell to corruption after the Third War. Ogtinc chose another path. Seasoned trackers know Ogtinc for his knowledge of Kalimdor’s wilderness. He tests hunters who have honed their skills across the continents, sending them after rare trophies: courser antlers, sea serpent scales, and parts of green dragonkin. Through these trials, hunters learn to honor the natural world and preserve its balance, rather than take life without thought.

npc:ogunaro-wolfrunner.text: Ogunaro Wolfrunner. In Orgrimmar’s Valley of Honor, Ogunaro Wolfrunner tends the Horde’s foremost wolf kennel beside the Hunter’s Hall. He breeds and trains fierce wolves for orc champions and their trusted allies. Beside the Hunter’s Hall in the Valley of Honor, Ogunaro Wolfrunner tends Orgrimmar’s battle wolves. Orcs and wolves have shared a bond for generations, across Draenor’s plains and Durotar’s wilderness. It rests on mutual respect, not simple domestication. Ogunaro entrusts only the hardiest beasts, from dire wolves to agile timber prowlers, to warriors who have proven their strength and worth to the warchief.

npc:old-murk-eye.text: Old Murk-Eye. Near the Westfall Lighthouse, Old Murk-Eye stalks the southern coast. His kind revere him, while sailors fear the deadly danger he brings to anyone who comes near the lighthouse. Old Murk-Eye hunts in the surf around the Westfall Lighthouse. He is far tougher and more aggressive than the murlocs common along Westfall’s shores. His attacks have brought grief to local mariners, so the spectral Captain Grayson seeks his death. Grayson offers a bounty for Old Murk-Eye’s pristine scales, hoping to break his hold on the shallows.

npc:orendil-broadleaf.text: Orendil Broadleaf. At Maestra's Post in western Ashenvale, Orendil Broadleaf tends to the sick. His knowledge of forest plants helps him make remedies for young lives in the troubled woodlands. At Maestra's Post on Ashenvale's western border, Orendil Broadleaf tends to the sick. He knows the local herbs and how to use them in healing remedies. Travelers passing through gather rare plants and other natural ingredients for him. As tension and conflict press closer to the forest, Orendil keeps his attention on protecting his kin and easing their ailments.

npc:orenthil-whisperwind.text: Orenthil Whisperwind. In Shadowglen, beneath Teldrassil’s boughs, Orenthil Whisperwind welcomes those setting out. Orenthil Whisperwind lives among the night elves in Shadowglen, beneath Teldrassil’s canopy. Little is known of his past.

npc:ormak-grimshot.text: Ormak Grimshot. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Ormak Grimshot teaches hunters to face the wilds. With Grimfang beside him, he trains Horde hunters to track, shoot, and tame beasts. In the Hunter's Hall, Ormak Grimshot trains Horde trackers and marksmen. Grimfang, his wolf, stays at his side as he teaches hunters to survive Kalimdor's wilderness. Orc and troll hunters who have completed their trials in Durotar learn from him to tame and command wild beasts, then form lasting bonds with their animal companions.

npc:ormer-ironbraid.text: Ormer Ironbraid. At Whelgar's Excavation Site, Ormer Ironbraid holds his ground against the raptors that drove the dwarven workers away. He seeks allies to reclaim the dig. Ormer Ironbraid came to the Wetlands with the dwarves who seek Titan relics and ancient history at Whelgar's Excavation Site. Their work stirred fierce raptors, or drew the beasts to the dig. Now raptors prowl the ruins where Ormer's team hoped to study ancient earthenware and tablets. Their presence has halted the work, and Ormer's anger runs deep. Ormer will not leave the dig, though he cannot drive out the raptors alone. He asks travelers to kill them, starting with the smaller beasts and moving on to larger, fiercer ones. The artifacts remain to be recovered, but the fight is personal now. Ormer wants vengeance for the work disrupted and the dwarven pride wounded by the raptors' presence.

npc:orokk-omosh.text: Orokk Omosh. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh seeks apprentices for his family's smithing craft. With no children to inherit it, he hopes worthy Horde smiths will carry the Omosh armorcraft secrets onward. Orokk Omosh is the last smith of his line in the Valley of Honor. He has no children to inherit his craft, and he will not let his family's techniques die with him. So he sets demanding trials of metalwork for capable Horde blacksmiths. Those who prove their dedication earn the revered secrets of Omosh armorcraft. Among the artisans, Orokk is known for his boisterous delight in true mastery. When smiths complete his craftsmanship trials, he often performs the Omosh Dance of Joy. His jubilant celebration of traditional smithing echoes through Orgrimmar's halls.

npc:orphan-matron-battlewail.text:
Orphan Matron Battlewail. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orphan Matron Battlewail shelters children left without families by war. With Tosamina, she raises young orcs. In Orgrimmar, a young capital already touched by war, Orphan Matron Battlewail and Tosamina shelter children who have lost their kin to violence. They nurture the Horde's next generation in the orphanage of the Valley of Honor.

The orphanage opens its doors to passing adventurers. During Children's Week, travelers are called upon to mentor the children.

npc:orphan-matron-nightingale.text: Orphan Matron Nightingale. In Cathedral Square, Orphan Matron Nightingale cares for Stormwind’s orphaned children. With Matron Shellene, she gives them shelter and guidance, and welcomes Alliance adventurers during Children's Week. Outside the orphanage, south-east of the Cathedral of Light, Orphan Matron Nightingale cares for children left without homes or parents. Recent wars, gnoll attacks, and the rise of the Defias Brotherhood have brought many to her door. Under the Church of the Holy Light’s watch, Nightingale and Matron Shellene give them shelter, basic care, and guidance. Matron Nightingale knows children need hope as well as food and shelter. Each Children's Week, she asks Alliance heroes to take an orphan on journeys across Azeroth. She hopes that meeting celebrated champions will build their confidence and show them the wider world beyond the city walls. Above all, she wants them to know they are not forgotten.

npc:osric-strang.text: Osric Strang. In Stormwind's Old Town, veteran armor merchant Osric Strang supplies weary travelers and Alliance defenders with sturdy gear. His shop, Limited Immunity, offers heavy mail and plate armor, along with shields. Osric Strang runs Limited Immunity, where fighters can find heavy armor and shields. He also helps couriers arriving from nearby settlements, including Sentinel Hill in Westfall, by giving them a point of contact in the capital.

npc:overlord-mok-morokk.text: Overlord Mok'Morokk. Brackenwall Village is where Overlord Mok'Morokk rules the Stonemaul ogres of Dustwallow Marsh. Rexxar chose him for his strength, but now he is a tyrant who will not defend his clan from the black dragonflight. Rexxar defeated Kor'gall, the former chieftain, and led the Stonemaul clan in defense of Durotar. When he left, he put Mok'Morokk in command, trusting his strength in battle. He was wrong to trust him. Mok'Morokk chose intimidation and comfort over care for his kin. From Brackenwall Village, he demands tribute he has not earned and bullies anyone who questions his rule.

npc:pao-ka-swiftmountain.text:
Pao'ka Swiftmountain. Among Highperch's cliffs, Pao'ka Swiftmountain is trapped by the wyverns he came to study. He traveled south with Motega Firemane, but curiosity brought him too near their nesting grounds. Pao'ka came to Thousand Needles with Motega Firemane to study the canyon beasts. His father feared the journey was too perilous, and now Pao'ka's plight has proved him right.

The young scholar followed a mountain trail behind a solitary tauren totem, drawn by Highperch's wyverns. The territorial beasts drove him into the crags. Now he is trapped and terrified, with swooping wyverns barring his way back to Whitereach Post.

npc:parqual-fintallas.text: Parqual Fintallas. In the Undercity's Apothecarium, Parqual Fintallas keeps his love of Lordaeron's history. Though once human, he now lives among the Forsaken and greets travelers with courtesy, sharing his deep knowledge of ancient lore. Parqual studied Lordaeron's history as a respected human scholar, surrounded by the kingdom's records. The plague of undeath killed him and raised him among its many victims. Under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, he eventually broke free. Many Forsaken embrace cold pragmatism and turn from their former lives. Parqual keeps his scholarly passion and pleasant manners, though the knowledge he seeks has changed since his human life. Parqual lives among the bubbling vats and alchemists of the Undercity's Apothecarium. Its grim surroundings do not lessen his knowledge of Azeroth's history. Travelers facing difficult trials of the mind, including the elusive Test of Lore, are sent to him. He directs them to the Scarlet Monastery's library to find a book, then puts a question of his own to them.

npc:pilot-bellowfiz.text: Pilot Bellowfiz. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Bellowfiz keeps Ironforge's war machine ready. The Siege Brigade calls him “Fizzer,” and he tends Jetsteam, the heavy dwarven machine he pilots. Just outside Ironforge, Bellowfiz tunes Jetsteam and gathers what the machine needs in the field. Pilot Stonegear, his fellow driver, joins him in debating vehicle designs, armor plating, and engine output. Their work keeps Khaz Modan's mechanized strength ready across the kingdom.

npc:pilot-hammerfoot.text: Pilot Hammerfoot. At North Gate Outpost, Pilot Hammerfoot watches the pass and searches for a missing fellow pilot. The Siege Brigade’s engines guard the route, but the mountain hills are dangerous. Between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan, the passes are Pilot Hammerfoot's to watch. He guards Ironforge’s siege engines for the Siege Brigade. The rough mountain ground makes those engines dangerous to drive. Now one pilot is missing, and savage beasts roam the nearby hills. Finding him matters.

npc:pilot-longbeard.text: Pilot Longbeard. In Ironforge's Military Ward, Pilot Longbeard watches for word from mechanics far away. He is stationed in the Hall of Arms and keeps close to gnomish tinkerers and fellow racing enthusiasts in the Shimmering Flats. Pilot Longbeard serves with the Ironforge Siege Brigade in the Military Ward. He listens eagerly for news from mechanics across the continent. Among them are the Brassbolts brothers, who tinker on Kalimdor's salt flats. Longbeard points travelers bound for Kalimdor toward the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. There, gnomish inventors push the bounds of machinery alongside their goblin rivals.

npc:pilot-stonegear.text: Pilot Stonegear. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Stonegear readies the Trollplow for battle. Called “Stone,” the dwarf mechanic and driver serves in the Ironforge Siege Brigade. He seeks rare materials to improve the machine's engine and armor, and travelers in Dun Morogh help him find them. Pilot Stonegear works among siege tanks and fellow pilots just outside Kharanos. His pride is Trollplow, a heavy siege tank built to break enemy lines. Stone knows a driver's life in battle depends on sound gears, strong plates, and steady steam pressure. So he keeps improving the tank's fighting power and making its cramped cockpit more livable. Off duty, Pilot Stonegear debates engineering plans with fellow pilots such as Pilot Bellowfiz. The depot's standard designs never satisfy him. He seeks unusual ores and volatile minerals to improve Trollplow's armor and munitions. Travelers cross Dun Morogh's snowy wilderness and dangerous caves to find the supplies he needs.

npc:pixel.text:
Pixel. At Splintertree Post, Pixel carries Warsong goods through dangerous Ashenvale for a fee. She keeps the saw blades until paid and seeks other cargo worth carrying. From Splintertree Post, where the Horde holds a fortified post in Ashenvale, Pixel carries freight for the Warsong Clan. She takes goods through active war zones to support the clan’s logging work, guided by coin and contracts.

The saw blades stay with her until she is paid. For this shipment, she wants a deadly blunderbuss to guard herself on the road. She also pays travelers for satyr horns, much sought after in Ratchet.

npc:piznik.text: Piznik. Deep in Windshear Mine, Piznik watches the Venture Company workers. Once second in the operation, he now waits for a chance to strike back at Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle. Before Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle took control of Windshear Crag, Piznik ranked second across the whole operation. When Gerenzo seized authority, the Venture Company pushed Piznik aside and sent him deep into Windshear Mine. Piznik has not accepted the demotion quietly. He watches the mine’s movements and waits for a chance to take revenge on the boss who demoted him.

npc:pozzik.text: Pozzik. At the Mirage Raceway, Pozzik tests goblin engineering against a gnome rival. Once among Undermine’s most respected engineers, he now builds experimental rocket cars on the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Pozzik made his name among goblin tinkerers before settling in Thousand Needles. He was one of Undermine’s most respected engineers, mastering complex internal combustion, propulsion, and dangerous chassis construction. He left that reputation behind for the salt flats, where he pushes high-speed machines to their limits. At the Mirage Raceway, Pozzik works with Fizzle Brassbolts, his longtime gnome counterpart. Goblin explosives and gnomish calibration have long stood as rivals, yet the two built a sprawling track across a dried lakebed. Now their racing outfits test prototype rocket cars to prove whose engineering rules the track. Pozzik seeks resourceful adventurers to find parts and lighten his designs.

npc:priestess-a-moora.text: Priestess A'moora. Within Darnassus, Priestess A'moora serves Elune in the Temple of the Moon. She tends its rites and sacred offerings, including one tied to the fate of Lady Sathrah. Priestess A'moora tends the rites of Elune in Darnassus. Within the Temple of the Moon, she serves the spiritual needs of the city and keeps the old devotions alive. While other members of the Sisterhood oversee defenses or diplomacy, A'moora attends to sacred matters concerning Teldrassil's natural spirits. Lady Sathrah was a great spider beloved of Elune, and the temple kept her silvery dew for its healing powers. When Sathrah fell into madness, A'moora sent young adventurers to the northern borders of Teldrassil near Wellspring Lake to end her suffering and bring back her silvery spinnerets. At the temple's fountain, the spinnerets are offered to Elune so Sathrah may be reborn at peace.

npc:priestess-anetta.text: Priestess Anetta. Within Northshire Abbey, Priestess Anetta teaches new priests the first rites of the Holy Light. A human cleric, she belongs to the Brotherhood of Northshire. Priestess Anetta keeps to the quiet library wing on Northshire Abbey’s ground floor. Defias bandits and kobolds trouble the valley. She reminds those who pass that the Light may be the one thing that saves them someday. New human priests come to Priestess Anetta in the cloister with a hallowed letter of introduction. She teaches them holy words to mend flesh and call down smiting radiance against evil. Under her guidance, the young acolytes prepare to carry the Light beyond Northshire’s secluded walls.

npc:priestess-josetta.text: Priestess Josetta. In Goldshire, Priestess Josetta guides young priests beyond their first trials at Northshire. She teaches them faith, devotion, and service to others. From an upstairs room in the Lion's Pride Inn, Priestess Josetta tends to the people of Elwynn Forest. Travelers, guards, and local workers come within her reach there. She gives spiritual care among ordinary folk, serving the Holy Light wherever people need comfort. After their first studies at Northshire Abbey, young priests come to Priestess Josetta for guidance. She sends them into the countryside to aid wounded guards and comfort those who suffer. Their work teaches them that priesthood asks for more than prayers learned by heart. They must put the Light to work and help mend a broken world. Priestess Josetta regrets that she did not travel farther when she was young. She chose familiar ground over the wider roads of Azeroth. Though content with her sacred service in Goldshire, she urges young disciples to be bolder and carry their faith to distant frontiers.

npc:prospector-ironband.text: Prospector Ironband. At Ironband's Excavation Site, Prospector Ironband leads a search through Khaz Modan's buried past. He directs the Dwarven Explorers' Guild's work in southeastern Loch Modan, seeking the heritage of the dwarven people. Despite setbacks and hostile creatures, he sends reports and relics to Ironforge. Prospector Ironband leads the dig at Ironband's Excavation Site in southeastern Loch Modan. Like other field researchers in the Explorers' Guild, he believes Khaz Modan's soil holds truths about the origins of the dwarven race. His camp digs trenches and sifts rubble for ancient relics, stone tablets, and earthen artifacts. The work is slow, but Ironband remains resolute and welcomes capable travelers who can safeguard the operation. Troggs and wildlife threaten the excavation in Loch Modan's rugged wilds. They endanger the dig's supplies and equipment, and relics or survey tools may be stolen or wrecked before the Guild can examine them. Ironband relies on visiting Alliance travelers to guard cargo shipments and hold off raiders. He also asks them to look into missing Guild contacts in the neighboring badlands.

npc:prospector-remtravel.text: Prospector Remtravel. In southern Darkshore, Prospector Remtravel leads the Explorers' League dig among ancient relics. His scattered focus and the dangers around camp make the work perilous. The Explorers' League sent Prospector Remtravel across the sea to establish a dig in southern Darkshore. Night elves guard their ancestral lands, yet the League's search for Azeroth's origins brings its prospectors into forgotten places. Remtravel uncovers fossils and ancient stones. Aggressive wildlife and hostile local threats make the camp hard for one scatterbrained dwarf to manage.

npc:prospector-ryedol.text: Prospector Ryedol. South of Hammertoe's Digsite, Prospector Ryedol watches over the Explorers' League's work in the Badlands. He searches for dwarven relics and keeps hope alive amid troggs and beasts. From a hill south of Hammertoe's Digsite, Prospector Ryedol directs the Explorers' League's work. The dry valley holds ancient titan secrets and traces of dwarven heritage, yet troggs, coyotes, and drakes threaten the expeditions. Dark Iron dwarves have stolen dwarven gear, so Ryedol sends out efforts to recover it. The League has lost much in these wastes, and he searches ruined outposts for signs of hope.

npc:prospector-stormpike.text: Prospector Stormpike. In Ironforge, Prospector Stormpike sends aid to distant archaeological digs. The blunt, short-tempered dwarf of the renowned Stormpike clan can also decipher coded messages with a sharp mind. From the Library of the Hall of Explorers, Prospector Stormpike coordinates excavations across Khaz Modan and beyond. He sends supplies to distant sites, even blasting powder. Idle chatter tries his patience, yet he is devoted to uncovering dwarven history. His keen mind can break intricate ciphers and help scouts face secret threats.

npc:prospector-whelgar.text:
Prospector Whelgar. At Whelgar's Excavation Site in the Wetlands, Prospector Whelgar's search for titan relics has stalled. Raptors have overrun the dig, and he seeks hardy adventurers to recover ancient artifacts. Prospector Whelgar leads an Ironforge dwarf expedition in the Wetlands. His camp lies east of Menethil Harbor, where he searches for the history of the dwarven race. Ancient stone relics once filled the valley, but territorial raptors drove his team into hiding. Still, Whelgar refuses to leave his duty unfinished.

He hopes to recover valuable relics before predators or rival scoundrels ruin the site. The Goaz Stone is among them.

npc:quartermaster-lewis.text: Quartermaster Lewis. At Sentinel Hill in Westfall, Quartermaster Lewis keeps supplies moving to the People's Militia. He serves the defenders and travelers holding the frontier against the Defias Brotherhood. Quartermaster Lewis keeps the People's Militia supplied from Sentinel Tower. Stormwind's royal leaders offer little aid to impoverished Westfall, so Sentinel Hill relies on local volunteers and the provisions they can gather. Lewis hands out dry rations, fresh water, arrows, shot, and throwing blades. The fighters on watch need these basics to endure Defias raids.

npc:quinn-yorick.text: Quinn Yorick. At the Ivar Patch, Quinn Yorick lies wounded and hidden from the ghoul that struck him. The Forsaken scout cannot finish his mission or retreat alone. Quinn Yorick is a Forsaken scout hiding upstairs in a ruined farmhouse at the Ivar Patch. Ivar the Foul, a ghoul in the farm’s barn in northern Silverpine Forest, wounded him in a fierce clash. Quinn and his sister Rane were sent to scout Silverpine and report to High Executor Hadrec. Too badly hurt to finish their mission or retreat safely alone, he waits in hiding. Travelers serving the Forsaken bring him healing and face the creature that nearly tore him apart.

npc:ragnar-thunderbrew.text:
Ragnar Thunderbrew. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Ragnar Thunderbrew keeps the family tavern supplied and its patrons fed. Across Dun Morogh, the dwarven brewer is known for the family's Beer Basted Boar Ribs. Ragnar Thunderbrew tends the kitchen and brewing work at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Mountaineers, travelers, and gnome refugees fleeing Gnomeregan gather there. His Beer Basted Boar Ribs, made with dwarven ale, are a Dun Morogh specialty.

Supplies have grown hard to find since his usual meat provider enlisted in the King's Army. Ragnar now depends on wandering mountaineers and hunters to bring fresh crag boar flanks to the kitchen. Across Ironforge territory, the Thunderbrew name is known for dwarven drink and tavern life. Ragnar has kept the distillery running since his older brother, Grimbooze Thunderbrew, disappeared in a drunken haze a few harvests ago.

He guards the family's brewing heritage against thieves such as the Dark Iron dwarves, who stole the recipe for Thunderbrew Lager. With patrons restless, supplies scarce, and disputes breaking out in the tavern, Ragnar keeps the taps flowing and travelers fed in Kharanos.

npc:rahauro.text: Rahauro. On Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, Rahauro sends Horde fighters against threats beneath Orgrimmar. He serves Magatha Grimtotem, coordinating the response to troggs in Ragefire Chasm and the search for a fallen agent’s possessions. Rahauro attends Magatha Grimtotem on Elder Rise’s high terrace. He speaks and acts for the elder crone, who trusts her servants to recruit others. When wild creatures swarm beneath the orcish capital, Rahauro makes the arrangements and sends Horde mercenaries to face them. Troggs in Ragefire Chasm rejected Magatha’s offer of peace. Her envoys went beneath Orgrimmar to parley, but the troggs attacked and killed them. Magatha sees the creatures as a threat to the Horde. So Rahauro sends champions into the caverns to thin their numbers and learn their strength.

npc:raleigh-andrean.text: Raleigh Andrean. In the Undercity, Raleigh Andrean has made a home among the Forsaken. His dealings with those he once knew reveal how little regard he has for his human life. Before the Third War, Raleigh Andrean lived in Lordaeron as a human. He shared his life with his wife, Deliah, and counted Valdred Moray as a friend. Then the Scourge swept through the kingdom. Raleigh was killed and raised as a mindless thrall in service to the Lich King. When the Lich King's grip shattered, Sylvanas Windrunner led an uprising. Raleigh regained his free will and joined the Forsaken in the Undercity.

npc:randis.text: Randis. In Cathedral Square, Randis longs to see the lands beyond Stormwind. During Children's Week, he eagerly travels with willing adventurers across Alliance lands. Randis lives in the orphanage near Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. The realm's conflicts have left many children without family. Each year during Children's Week, Orphan Matron Nightingale gives a whistle to sympathetic heroes and entrusts them with Randis's care. Curious and full of questions, he dreams of adventure and asks riddles. He says he wants to be king of Stormwind when he grows up. Most days, Randis stays in Cathedral Square, so leaving the capital feels like a grand adventure. He remarks that places like Ironforge smell odd. His wonder shows what Alliance heroes fight to protect.

npc:ranger-glynda-nal-shea.text: Ranger Glynda Nal'Shea. Near Auberdine, Ranger Glynda Nal'Shea keeps watch over Darkshore. She sends travelers against dangers on the coast and to investigate strange signs. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea directs scouts from Auberdine as corruption grows and hostile forces press into Darkshore. She watches the wilderness around town and calls on capable travelers to guard the perimeter. Their aid helps protect night elf holdings along the coast. Glynda watches the shore for danger, especially the bolder murlocs south of town. She oversees bounties on threats such as Murkdeep and sends scouts to examine strange finds. One report speaks of a crimson crystal near Darkshore's eastern mountain range.

npc:rau-cliffrunner.text: Rau Cliffrunner. At Freewind Post, Rau Cliffrunner keeps watch over Thousand Needles and studies the Galak centaur. He works with allies in Thunder Bluff to guard his people from threats across the canyon. From Freewind Post, Rau Cliffrunner watches the broad reaches of Thousand Needles. Predators, quilboar, and hostile centaur clans surround the tauren outpost. Rau helps organize the post and investigates dangers before they can threaten the mesa settlements.

npc:razzle-sprysprocket.text: Razzle Sprysprocket. In Kharanos, Razzle Sprysprocket searches for the machinery lost when Gnomeregan fell. With Ozzie Togglevolt, he gathers parts scattered through Dun Morogh’s snowy hills. After Gnomeregan fell, Razzle found refuge in Dun Morogh and opened a workshop in Kharanos. Skilled with delicate mechanisms, he works beside fellow engineer Ozzie Togglevolt. Together, they seek gyro-mechanisms and cog assemblies lost or scavenged during the flight from their irradiated homeland. Wild beasts roam Dun Morogh’s frozen ridges, and Frostmane trolls raid the area. Their presence makes Razzle’s work dangerous. Still, he labors to keep gnomish contraptions working and recover the lost wonders of Gnomeregan.

npc:red-jack-flint.text: Red Jack Flint. In Menethil Keep, Red Jack Flint helps travelers find passage across the sea. The seasoned human mariner sails with the Maiden's Virtue and connects travelers with contacts bound for Kalimdor. Red Jack Flint sails from Menethil Keep as a crewman of the Maiden's Virtue. He knows the sea routes from Khaz Modan to distant shores and helps capable travelers find passage. Across the Great Sea, he directs them to allies such as Fiora Longears in Kalimdor.

npc:rema-schneider.text: Rema Schneider. In Stormwind City, Rema Schneider keeps trade moving from the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. A human citizen, she often helps local shopkeepers and artisans with deliveries. Rema Schneider manages daily trade from the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. The shop lies just west of the stone bridge into Cathedral Square, beside Stormwind's canals. Cloth and finished garments pass between local craftsmen, and Rema depends on couriers to carry supplies from one workshop to another.

npc:remulos.text:
Remulos. In Moonglade, Keeper Remulos guides the druids of the Cenarion Circle. Cenarius has fallen and Malfurion Stormrage sleeps, so Remulos helps lead the Circle. He puts nature’s balance before night elven isolation. Keeper Remulos watches over Moonglade, the druids’ sacred sanctuary north of Mount Hyjal. Immortal, he bears the lower body of a great stag and the antlered torso of an ancient dryad-father. His divine authority and counsel aid the Cenarion Circle while Malfurion Stormrage remains trapped in the Emerald Dream. He works to heal Azeroth’s scars and aids druids in their sacred rites around Lake Elune'ara. Keeper Remulos often clashes with Archdruid Fandral Staghelm over the Circle’s path. Staghelm champions night elven supremacy and sought to restore his people’s lost immortality by planting Teldrassil. Remulos opposed the new World Tree, seeing its planting as hubris.

Remulos also defied Staghelm’s isolationist faction by welcoming Hamuul Runetotem and the tauren into the Cenarion Circle. There, their shamans-turned-druids could learn nature’s closely guarded mysteries and help restore the land alongside others.

npc:remy-two-times.text: Remy "Two Times". In Goldshire, Remy "Two Times" trades goods and buys raw materials. He came from the Redridge Mountains, and earned his name by repeating the ends of his sentences twice. Travelers passing through Goldshire can strike a deal with Remy "Two Times". He seeks profit in troubled Elwynn Forest, and his trade puts coin in their hands. His unusual way of speaking may amuse them. Trade in Elwynn suffers as kobolds overrun the local gold mines and aggressive murlocs infest the riverbanks. Remy pays travelers for pouches of gold dust gathered from kobolds in the mines. Near Crystal Lake, he watches for suspicious murloc movements.

npc:renato-gallina.text: Renato Gallina. In Stormwind's Trade District, Renato Gallina calls travelers to his family's winery. Renato Gallina calls to passers-by among the Trade District stalls. He proclaims his family's vintages the finest in Stormwind. The Gallina family runs a winery along the Canals, and Renato promotes it with pamphlets. Bring one to his sister Suzetta at the shop, and she gives you a free bottle of wine.

npc:renee-lauer.text: Innkeeper Renee. At the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, Innkeeper Renee gives travelers food, drink, and shelter. Innkeeper Renee keeps Brill's central inn, the Gallows' End Tavern. She sells food, drink, and general goods from behind her counter. Renee remarks that the Forsaken have huge appetites. Her tavern gives Tirisfal's undead a cozy place to rest as plague victims make their way in the world. Newcomers to Brill often stop first at Renee's inn. Calvin Montague of Deathknell sends fresh adventurers to her with a nondescript letter. The word is the one Renee has eagerly awaited. Beneath the tavern's floorboards, the cellar also holds a captured Scarlet Crusade zealot.

npc:renzik-the-shiv.text: Renzik "The Shiv". In Stormwind's Old Town, Renzik "The Shiv" directs SI:7's new rogue recruits. The goblin is Spymaster Mathias Shaw's trusted second-in-command, receiving promising agents sent from across the Alliance. Renzik keeps his past to himself. In Stormwind, the goblin has risen to become Spymaster Mathias Shaw's second-in-command in SI:7. He has little patience for pleasantries. When new recruits arrive, he asks whether they are ready to work or need a nap first. Renzik works inside SI:7's secretive fortress in Old Town, second-in-command to Mathias Shaw. Rogue mentors across the Alliance send their most promising agents to him, from Ironforge to Darnassus. Then he sends them to field instructors such as Lucius in Redridge, where they can hone the skills needed to survive in the field.

npc:rezlak.text: Rezlak. Along Durotar’s roads south of Orgrimmar, Rezlak waits for help keeping his supplies moving. The goblin belongs to the Tinkers’ Union and hires travelers to recover lost goods and drive off harpies. Rezlak waits beside the canyon road between Razor Hill and Orgrimmar. He represents the Tinkers’ Union, a goblin syndicate devoted to engineering, supply lines, and practical business. While trade runs smoothly, the factional tensions of Kalimdor matter little to him. Dustwind harpies have raided his cargo caravans and made the routes unsafe. So Rezlak stays at his post and hires passersby to recover supplies and deal with the harpies for profit.

npc:rhinag.text: Rhinag. Near Durotar’s northwestern border, Rhinag waits among the rocks, weakened by scorpids’ venom. The Darkspear troll needs a remedy from a passing traveler before the poison takes its toll. Among the rocks near Durotar’s northwestern border, Rhinag lies weak after a Venomtail Scorpid stung him. The poison has left the Darkspear troll isolated. He needs a venomtail antidote, and his survival depends on whether a passing traveler can find one in time.

npc:ringo.text:
Ringo. Inside a cave on Fire Plume Ridge, Ringo lies overcome by heat. The goblin explorer climbed partway up Un'Goro Crater's active volcano before collapsing. His friend Spraggle Frock waits at Marshal's Refuge, worried for him. Goblins brave dangerous places for wealth or oddities, yet Fire Plume Ridge is harsh even for them. The active volcano rises in the center of Un'Goro Crater. It spews ash, magma, and boiling steam.

Ringo climbed about halfway up its southern face before the suffocating heat overcame him. He left his belongings scattered outside a cave, then crawled inside for shelter. Heat exhaustion left him unable to move.

npc:rivern-frostwind.text:
Rivern Frostwind. At Frostsaber Rock, Rivern Frostwind trains riders and guards Winterspring's frostsabers. His frost tiger Glacier is at his side, and only the most dedicated Alliance champions earn the honor of riding one. From icy Frostsaber Rock, Rivern Frostwind oversees the breeding and care of Winterspring frostsabers. Unlike the nightsabers of Teldrassil and Ashenvale, these cats are bred to endure northern Kalimdor's bitter cold.

Rivern entrusts a saber only to those who prove their commitment to protecting the beasts. They must gather fresh meat from the tundra, clear out Winterfall furbolgs, and drive back rampaging frost giants before he deems them worthy.

npc:roetten-stonehammer.text: Roetten Stonehammer. In Ironforge's Hall of Explorers, Roetten Stonehammer organizes expeditions for Reclaimers Inc. He hires adventurers to recover salvage in distant lands such as Desolace. Roetten Stonehammer handles recovery work for Reclaimers Inc. from the Library in the Hall of Explorers. He connects mercenaries with salvage work across Kalimdor. His associates seek valuable cargo, wreckage, and rare reagents in dangerous lands such as Desolace.

npc:royal-historian-archesonus.text: Royal Historian Archesonus. At the High Seat, Royal Historian Archesonus records calamities for the Ironforge crown. A dwarven scholar in King Magni Bronzebeard’s service, she writes of disasters in the northern human kingdoms and oversees study of ancient dwarven tragedies, including the Dark Iron kingdom’s scorched remains. Royal Historian Archesonus keeps Ironforge’s records near King Magni Bronzebeard’s throne in the High Seat. Her studies reach beyond the Khaz Modan mountains. She wrote 'The Fall of Lordaeron and the Scouring of the Eastweald' and 'On Plagues, Curses, and Blights.' In them, she traces the Scourge’s ruin of humanity’s northern realm. She records the truth of ruinous magic and political collapse with care. Royal Historian Archesonus oversees research into the War of the Three Hammers and Thaurissan’s destruction. She seeks relics and charred tablets from the Smoldering Ruins of Thaurissan in the Burning Steppes, and sends adventurers there to search. Her work examines the cataclysm that scorched the Burning Steppes and bound the Dark Iron clan to the Firelord.

npc:ruga-ragetotem.text: Ruga Ragetotem. At Camp Taurajo, Ruga Ragetotem sends warriors south to prove their strength against the silithid. Those who endure earn a recommendation to Thun'grim Firegaze. Ruga Ragetotem trains warriors at Camp Taurajo who seek to prove their strength in Kalimdor. Silithid have suddenly appeared south of camp and carved hives into the Field of Giants. Ruga sends young fighters to hunt the insectoids and bring back their antennae. Those who endure earn his respect and a recommendation to Thun'grim Firegaze, a renowned armorsmith.

npc:rutgar-glyphshaper.text: Rutgar Glyphshaper. At the Bronzebeard Encampment, Rutgar Glyphshaper studies the silithid hives. The dwarven archaeologist came to Silithus with Brann Bronzebeard’s expedition to uncover the hives’ mysteries in their ancient relics and runes. Brann has wandered into the desert, but Rutgar carries on. Rutgar Glyphshaper came to Silithus with Brann Bronzebeard to explore the vast silithid hives and recover relics buried beneath the desert. Their expedition made camp at the Bronzebeard Encampment, south of Cenarion Hold. Rutgar and his companions often entered the hives for inscribed stones and runic artifacts. At times, Cenarion night elf researchers worked alongside them.

npc:ruul-eagletalon.text: Ruul Eagletalon. At Bloodhoof Village, Ruul Eagletalon keeps watch over the borders. He watches Mulgore’s wildlife, especially the aggressive Windfury harpies pressing into tauren lands. Ruul Eagletalon watches over Bloodhoof Village as young braves arrive from Camp Narache. Mulgore is a peaceful homeland beside the arid Barrens. Yet territorial predators and hostile creatures still press against its pastures. Ruul watches the nearby plains and directs capable travelers against the savage Windfury harpies, which prey on unwary nomads and game.

npc:ruul-snowhoof.text:
Ruul Snowhoof. At Thistlefur Hold in northern Ashenvale, Ruul Snowhoof waits for rescue. Trapped in bear form, the tauren druid depends on Horde allies to free him and guide him to safety. Ruul Snowhoof came to northern Ashenvale and fell into the hands of the corrupt Thistlefur furbolgs. He took bear form, and they mistook him for a wild beast. So they locked him in a wooden cage deep within Thistlefur Hold instead of killing him.

Weakened now, Ruul cannot safely leave his form or fight his way out alone. He waits for Horde allies to open the cage, drive off his captors, and clear a path through the den. He hopes to return to his sister, Yama Snowhoof, at Splintertree Post.

npc:rwag.text:
Rwag. In the Den, Rwag teaches newcomers the first steps of a rogue's craft. The orc trains newly arrived orcs and trolls in stealth, subterfuge, and dirty fighting in Durotar's Valley of Trials, under the Horde's watch. Deep in the Den, Rwag trains young rogues, cutpurses, and thieves before they leave the cave and venture into Durotar. The new Horde honors martial skill and valor in battle. Yet Rwag knows subtlety, poisons, and a well-placed dagger can still mean survival in the unforgiving desert.

Rwag keeps watch over affairs in the Valley. He distrusts the dark practitioners sheltering in the cave, especially the warlock Nartok.

npc:saelienne.text: Saelienne. On Darnassus's Craftsmen's Terrace, Saelienne welcomes travelers and artisans to her inn. There they find food, drink, and a place to bind a Hearthstone in the night elven capital. Innkeeper Saelienne welcomes residents and visitors to her Craftsmen's Terrace inn in Darnassus. Travelers find a quiet place to rest, with night elven refreshments and goods brought through the city port. After long hours at the forge or loom, tradesfolk gather there to recover.

npc:sally-whitemane.text: High Inquisitor Whitemane. At the Scarlet Monastery, High Inquisitor Whitemane directs the Crusade from its Cathedral. A priestess of the Holy Light, she drives the order’s zeal with a consuming hatred of the undead. Alongside Scarlet Commander Renault Mograine, she leads its military and ideological campaigns across Lordaeron. Whitemane rose swiftly through the Scarlet Crusade. Now she commands the grand Cathedral of the Scarlet Monastery as its High Inquisitor. Her mastery of Holy magic is feared, and her unshakable conviction makes her one of the Crusade’s foremost symbols. She brings the Light against all she deems unclean without mercy.

npc:salma-saldean.text: Salma Saldean. At Saldean's Farm, Salma Saldean welcomes travelers and offers meals for help around the homestead. She and her husband, Farmer Saldean, tend their Westfall farm while bandits threaten the farms and Stormwind has left the region. Salma Saldean welcomes travelers to a farm that has endured while neighboring homesteads burned or fell to the Defias Brotherhood. A hearty pot waits on the stove, and she looks for capable hands to help around the farmstead. Salma feeds her family and visitors with what Westfall provides. She teaches travelers to make Goretusk liver pie and Westfall stew from wild boar, vultures, murlocs, and stray okra.

npc:sara-balloo.text: Sara Balloo. In Ironforge's Military Ward, Sara Balloo grieves for Sully and holds to the words he left behind. Sara Balloo keeps vigil in Ironforge's Military Ward, where weapons ring and soldiers drill. Her husband, Sully Balloo, fell in battle far from home, leaving her with grief and memories. A final letter crossed the mountains from the place where he died. Sully's words from his last days bring Sara some measure of closure.

npc:sara-timberlain.text:
Sara Timberlain. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain sews gear for Stormwind's soldiers. She makes useful armaments from salvaged cloth and leather. On the western edge of Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain sews outside a small cottage. Axes ring through the camp as workers fell trees. Though the settlement lies far from other settled lands, wolves and murlocs prowl nearby. Sara still welcomes travelers.

She turns scraps of linen and salvaged bandanas into sturdy gear. Her skill has earned official recognition. Stormwind's military forces commission her to supply armaments made of cloth and leather.

npc:scooty.text: Scooty. From Booty Bay’s busy pirate port, Scooty keeps a teleport link to Gnomeregan. The goblin engineer trusts his craft and his transponders, though the experimental pad lies in the fallen gnome city. For the Horde, his device opens a perilous route into Dun Morogh. Among Booty Bay’s wharves and workshops, Scooty pursues ambitious tinkering for the Steamwheedle Cartel. While many goblins favor gunpowder and explosives, he works to move matter across great distances. His transponders keep a working link to a teleportation pad inside Gnomeregan. Horde forces rely on his craft to reach the subterranean gnome stronghold without crossing dangerous Alliance territory. Experimental goblin teleporters rarely run without a hitch. After hearing of a new gnomish rig in Gnomeregan, Scooty and his partner Sovik built the Transpolyporter 6000. Scooty cheerfully admits it has exploded a dozen or so times. Crossing continents as scattered matter carries clear physical dangers, yet Scooty remains sure of his genius. To him, every mechanical failure is a small obstacle on the road to innovation.

npc:scout-riell.text: Scout Riell. At Sentinel Hill, Scout Riell watches Westfall from the roof of its stone watchtower. She serves the People's Militia and tracks the Defias Brotherhood, asking travelers to bring back the outlaws' red silk bandanas. Bandits and harvest golems threaten Westfall. Stormwind's royal army is absent, and the crown refuses aid. So the People's Militia must defend the region alone. The bandanas travelers bring back give Riell proof of the Defias Brotherhood's crimes.

npc:scout-thaelrid.text: Argent Guard Thaelrid. Wounded near the Pool of Ask'ar, Argent Guard Thaelrid lies cut off in Blackfathom Deeps. The night elf scout entered the submerged ruins for the Argent Dawn, and now he has seen what gathers below. The Argent Dawn sent Scout Thaelrid into Blackfathom Deeps after reports of foul rites reached the order from the Zoram Strand. The Dawn watches for rising evils and unnatural corruption across Azeroth. Thaelrid was to judge the threat, watch the flooded temple, and report back. Then the order could decide where aid was most needed.

npc:searn-firewarder.text: Searn Firewarder. In Grommash Hold, Searn Firewarder guides Horde shamans toward the elements. Inside Grommash Hold, Searn Firewarder guides shamans who seek the elements. Many Darkspear trolls commune with spirits through witch doctors and voodoo rites. Searn points initiates toward distant mentors and the rites of the Call of Fire, Call of Water, and Call of Air. Through them, shamans learn to commune with the elemental spirits of fire, water, and air. Searn stands among the Horde's high command in Orgrimmar.

npc:seer-graytongue.text: Seer Graytongue. On Red Cloud Mesa, Seer Graytongue guides young tauren through their first tribal trials. Near Camp Narache in Mulgore, he teaches them to honor the Earthmother before they enter the wider world. Young tauren braves and spellweavers come to Seer Graytongue atop Red Cloud Mesa. He guides those setting out from Camp Narache through sacred steps, among them the Rites of the Earthmother. The trials test their resolve against Mulgore’s harsh plains and dangerous beasts. Through each one, Graytongue teaches honor, patience, and reverence—virtues every tauren carries into adulthood.

npc:seer-ravenfeather.text: Seer Ravenfeather. At Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa, Seer Ravenfeather guides young tauren in the ways of the spirits and Mulgore's land. At Camp Narache, Seer Ravenfeather teaches young tauren who have chosen the shamanic path. Red Cloud Mesa is sacred ground where they prove themselves. She prepares new practitioners for their duties before they travel farther into Mulgore. Her lessons teach them to commune with elemental forces and honor the Earth Mother. Seer Ravenfeather guides new shamans through their first spiritual steps and the traditional Call of Earth rite. Under her guidance, initiates prepare ceremonial saptas and seek communion with earthen spirits among the mesa's stony outcrops. The bond they forge anchors their elemental magic.

npc:seereth-stonebreak.text: Seereth Stonebreak. Near Greatwood Vale, Seereth Stonebreak watches the land's troubles. The orc shaman camps on the border of the Stonetalon Mountains and the Barrens, guiding travelers through threats to the wilds and the Horde's presence. From her camp near Greatwood Vale, Seereth Stonebreak watches over Horde lands. She is an orc shaman who follows the elements' harmony and guards the Horde's territories. When the land's spirits cried out against goblin plunder, the Horde sent her to Stonetalon. Now she watches the landscape and guides travelers through dangers on the wild frontier. Across the Stonetalon range, ruthless goblin ventures and mechanical shredders cut through ancient woodlands. Their work has badly shaken the mountains' spiritual balance. Seereth sends Horde envoys to confront the invaders and seek counsel from elder lorekeepers. She hopes their efforts will ease the land's distress.

npc:senator-mehr-stonehallow.text: Senator Mehr Stonehallow. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, Senator Mehr Stonehallow has arrived at the front lines to face a trogg infestation. The Ironforge politician and Explorers' League member oversees its containment and calls on eager adventurers to cull the beasts before they overrun the quarry. Senator Mehr Stonehallow has left Ironforge's Senate halls for Gol'Bolar Quarry. A dwarf devoted to governance and the Explorers' League's historical pursuits, he knows the dangers facing the realm. When Rockjaw troggs clawed up from deep rock, Stonehallow came to the mining pit himself. He believes debate alone cannot protect the workers. So he offers bounties to capable travelers who can drive back the aggressive troggs and reclaim the quarry.

npc:senior-surveyor-fizzledowser.text: Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser. In Gadgetzan, Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser searches the desert for water. He investigates trouble around the town’s supply and asks adventurers to find the missing Junior Surveyor Scrimshank.

npc:sentinel-arynia-cloudsbreak.text: Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak. At Oracle Glade on Teldrassil, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak watches over the northern groves. She guards the enchanted waters and woodland wildlife. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak keeps watch in Oracle Glade, one of Teldrassil's most secluded reaches. Far from Darnassus, she serves the Sentinel army beneath ancient trees and beside ethereal springs. There, she guards the wilderness from disturbance. Disharmony stirs among Teldrassil's creatures, though the tree was born sacred. Arynia asks passing adventurers and young night elves to look into local troubles. Strange wildlife and mystical signs around the enchanted springs both concern her.

npc:sentinel-aynasha.text: Sentinel Aynasha. Along Darkshore’s wild borders, Sentinel Aynasha scouts dangers threatening night elven lands. She watches enemy movements and carries urgent intelligence across the frontier. Sentinel Aynasha scouts and fights with the Sentinels where night elven lands meet hostile incursions. She carries urgent messages across rough country and watches for enemy patrols. Her skill with a bow and knowledge of survival help her cross contested ground.

npc:sentinel-elissa-starbreeze.text: Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze. Across the bridge from Auberdine, Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze watches over Darkshore's coast. From an upper floor, she tracks dangers in the wilderness and guides travelers toward them. Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze directs Auberdine's defenses from across the bridge. Other Sentinels patrol Darkshore's coast and woodlands, while she keeps watch from the upper floor of a building northeast of the town inn. She stays alert for disturbances across the region. Her directions send travelers as far north as the Tower of Althalaxx, so threats in the shadows do not take Auberdine by surprise.

npc:sentinel-farsong.text: Sentinel Farsong. At Silverwing Grove, Sentinel Farsong guards Ashenvale’s southern border. She rallies champions against the Warsong Outriders in Warsong Gulch. Sentinel Farsong watches Silverwing Grove as the Warsong clan cuts lumber and pushes into night elf lands. She calls Alliance champions to strike at the Warsong Outriders and sends field reports to Silverwing command. Her work checks the Horde’s advance and helps protect the woods.

npc:sentinel-onaeya.text: Sentinel Onaeya. At Maestra's Post, Sentinel Onaeya, a night elf guardian, rallies aid for Ashenvale's northern edge. She guards the forest and calls travelers to defend the outpost and help fellow sentinels. Maestra's Post guards the road from Darkshore into Ashenvale. Sentinel Onaeya watches the lodge outside the settlement and directs its defense. Hostile wildlife and corrupting forces threaten night elf settlements nearby. Tensions along the border add to the danger. Sentinel Onaeya learns that furbolgs attacked Sentinel Aynasha in Darkshore while she carried an important message. Aynasha is poisoned, so Onaeya asks travelers to protect her until the antidote takes effect. She rewards those who keep her safe.

npc:sentinel-selarin.text: Sentinel Selarin. In Auberdine, Sentinel Selarin seeks aid for Ashenvale’s defenders. She brings Raene Wolfrunner’s appeal to the coastal settlement as dangers threaten the forest. Sentinel Selarin brings Raene Wolfrunner’s appeal from Ashenvale to Auberdine. Threats across the forest have stretched its garrison thin. So Selarin follows the forest road north into Darkshore, seeking Terenthis and help from the sentinels and scouts stationed on the coast. Terenthis cannot answer Selarin’s appeal in person, so she stays in Auberdine and calls on travelers passing through Darkshore. She sends capable adventurers south to Astranaar, where they can bring their blades and spells to Raene Wolfrunner’s beleaguered forces.

npc:sentinel-thenysil.text: Sentinel Thenysil. In Astranaar, Sentinel Thenysil watches Ashenvale and the road south into Stonetalon. She tracks military movements and keeps scouts in neighboring lands, especially where allied forces move south. At her post in Astranaar, Sentinel Thenysil helps guard Ashenvale as hostility grows. Night elf lands across the region face steady encroachment, so the outposts must keep in touch. Much of the garrison defends the forest road. Thenysil sends Alliance volunteers beyond Ashenvale to aid distant allies. Sentinel Thenysil shares a close friendship and military bond with Kaela Shadowspear, an operative sent into the Stonetalon Mountains. When Thenysil learns Kaela was sent with an eccentric gnome mage, she takes the strange pairing as a sign of serious trouble in the peaks. Concerned for her comrade, she sends capable travelers south to support them and asks for a report on the mission.

npc:sentinel-tysha-moonblade.text: Sentinel Tysha Moonblade. Along Darkshore's road, Sentinel Tysha Moonblade keeps watch over a troubled coast. West of Ameth'Aran, she guides travelers and seeks help against the restless spirits haunting the ruins. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade watches the road through Darkshore. East of her, cursed Highborne ghosts and malevolent banshees haunt Ameth'Aran's ancient stone pillars. Auberdine's defenses are stretched thin by dangers along the coast. Tysha asks capable travelers to uncover how Ameth'Aran fell and put its restless dead to rest.

npc:sentinel-velene-starstrike.text: Sentinel Velene Starstrike. At Silverwind Refuge, Sentinel Velene Starstrike guards central Ashenvale. She protects the sanctuary and nearby waters from rogue elementals and reckless sorcerers, keeping their magic from corrupting the ancient woodland. At Mystral Lake, Sentinel Velene Starstrike keeps watch from Silverwind Refuge. Night elf sentinels across Ashenvale work to preserve the forest's balance and defend elven sanctuaries. Silverwind Refuge gives travelers a place to rest in the central woods. Velene helps keep the area safe. Peace around Silverwind Refuge is easily disturbed. Velene watches Mystral Lake, where unruly elemental spirits and reckless mage summoners trouble the wilderness. She directs champions against rogue water elementals and the careless spellcasters who disturb the spirits of the land.

npc:serge-hinott.text: Serge Hinott. In Tarren Mill, Serge Hinott brews mixtures for the Forsaken war effort. He works beside Apothecary Lydon, preparing concoctions, antidotes, and reagents for the Royal Apothecary Society. In Tarren Mill, Serge Hinott brews remedies and other mixtures for the Forsaken. He works beside Apothecary Lydon, whose duties include chemical development and plague research against nearby human settlements such as Southshore. Hinott specializes in brewing restorative salves and antidotes for field agents and scouts facing poison or other toxic mishaps.

npc:shanda.text: Shanda. In Aldrassil, Shanda guides young night elf priests in the ways of Elune. She serves the Sisterhood of Elune in Shadowglen, teaching prayers, wards, and rites as her students prepare to defend Teldrassil. From Aldrassil, Shanda guides young night elves devoted to Elune. Druids tend Teldrassil's roots and boughs, while priestesses keep the Kaldorei close to the White Lady. Shanda teaches new initiates to call on lunar grace for healing and protective wards. She prepares them to face the corruption creeping into the World Tree's boughs. Young priests who awaken to their calling in Shadowglen come to Shanda to prove their devotion and learn their first prayers. Through rites such as In Favor of Elune, she tests their resolve and gives them blessed regalia. She also teaches basic incantations. Her students learn to tend the wounded with a gentle hand and stand firm against the shadows.

npc:shandris-feathermoon.text: Shandris Feathermoon. At Feathermoon Stronghold on Sardor Isle, Shandris Feathermoon commands night elf forces across Kalimdor. For ten thousand years, she has served as Tyrande Whisperwind's right hand. For ten thousand years, Shandris Feathermoon has stood beside Tyrande Whisperwind as her right hand among the Sentinels. She is one of the night elves' oldest defenders, serving through the long vigil that followed the Sundering. After the Great Sundering, the Sentinels were founded. Shandris became an indispensable commander in the night elf military. From Sardor Isle, General Shandris Feathermoon commands the Sentinel army in the field and oversees Feathermoon Stronghold. The elven fortress watches over Feralas's primal wilds. From the island outpost, she monitors savage gnolls, lingering Gordunni ogres, hate-fueled satyrs, and the Horde's growing power in southern Kalimdor.

npc:shari-stilwell.text: Shari Stilwell. In Brill, Shari Stilwell teaches Forsaken to bear the Light and follow the paladin's path. She is stationed in Tirisfal Glades, where the undead learn holy and martial discipline despite the pain. In Brill, Shari Stilwell trains Forsaken who seek the path of holy warriors. The Light brings the undead excruciating pain, yet she teaches those willing to endure it. She helps newcomers find their footing in Tirisfal Glades through early training and the changes of Forsaken life. Those she guides seek a place in the Forsaken kingdom. Shari shares her family name with Daphne, Merissa, and Jordan Stilwell, a renowned smith among the living in the southern kingdoms. The Scourge's devastation leaves it unknown whether the fall of Lordaeron tore Shari from these kin or whether their bond is distant.

npc:shelene-rhobart.text: Shelene Rhobart. At a Deathguard waystation in Tirisfal, Shelene Rhobart trains leatherworkers for the Forsaken. She supplies cured hides and leather gear for their military and logistical efforts across the blighted lands. Southeast of Brill, Shelene Rhobart works at a Deathguard waystation along the main road to the ruins of Lordaeron. Practical crafts still matter in undeath, both for survival and for war. She turns pelts from Tirisfal's prowling beasts into tough hides, armor, straps, and field gear for Forsaken patrols facing the Scourge and Scarlet crusaders.

npc:shindrell-swiftfire.text:
Shindrell Swiftfire. From Astranaar, Shindrell Swiftfire watches the threats beyond Ashenvale. The night elf sentinel and scout directs Alliance adventurers toward dangers on the coast and in nearby mountain passes, helping defend the town and the western reaches of Kalimdor. From Astranaar’s winding walkways, Shindrell Swiftfire watches beyond Ashenvale’s forest. Sentinels face Horde logging incursions from the east and south, while Shindrell keeps watch farther afield.

Travelers arrive from Darkshore or set out for Stonetalon’s jagged ridges. Shindrell helps keep Astranaar defended against danger from the flank. On Ashenvale’s northwestern shore, the troubled Zoram Strand draws Shindrell’s attention. Hostile naga have risen from the ocean depths, threatening Kaldorei settlements. Their arrival is a grave mystery.

Shindrell sends seasoned fighters to investigate the shore and coordinate with scouts nearby. They seek to contain the serpentine invaders before the naga gain a lasting foothold on ancient night elf lands.

npc:shoni-the-shilent.text: Shoni the Shilent. In Stormwind’s Dwarven District, Shoni the Shilent directs a crew bound for the tunnels beneath Westfall. She seeks power for the machines that could open a path back into Gnomeregan. From Stormwind’s Dwarven District, Shoni the Shilent directs a gnomish assault crew. Troggs hold Gnomeregan, and she means to retake the city. So she sends operatives into the tunnels beneath Westfall for the parts her crew needs. Shoni’s plan rests on the gnomes’ gyrodrillmatic excavationators. These heavy machines must break through Gnomeregan’s underground borders and open a way for an assault. But they lack power. Shoni seeks the intact Gnoam Sprecklesprocket from a working goblin shredder deep in the Deadmines. She also sends adventurers into Gnomeregan to dismantle robots for spare parts to repair her fleet.

npc:sicco-thermaplugg.text: Mekgineer Thermaplugg. In ruined Gnomeregan, Mekgineer Thermaplugg rules from a massive mechanical battle suit. Once High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque’s trusted advisor, he brought about the city’s irradiation in a bid for power. The fallout made him a leper gnome and left him deranged, ruling the ruined halls. For many years, Mekgineer Thermaplugg advised High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, who trusted him completely. Yet Thermaplugg secretly coveted the High Tinker’s office. Even Mekkatorque cannot say what drove his advisor to betray that trust. He can only wonder whether Thermaplugg sought power or wealth, both of which he would have had in time.

npc:sida.text: Sida. In Menethil Harbor, Sida lives apart from her estranged husband, Einar Stonegrip. She spends her days in the Wetlands port and sometimes ventures into the marsh, where she recently lost her bag near Ironbeard's Tomb. Sida keeps to Menethil Harbor, the Alliance port on the Wetlands coast. Her marriage to Einar Stonegrip is strained, and he refuses to travel there while she remains. Still, she sometimes leaves the settlement and ventures into the marsh. On a recent trip toward Ironbeard's Tomb, she lost her personal bag.

npc:sirra-von-indi.text: Sirra Von'Indi. In Darkshire, Sirra Von'Indi studies the records that preserve Duskwood's history. The town's historian knows ancient languages and helps explain mysterious documents and the region's past. In Darkshire Town Hall, Sirra Von'Indi keeps the settlement's archives. While the town guard faces threats in the woods, he studies old texts and preserves the history of Grand Hamlet from before shadow fell across the region.

npc:sister-aquinne.text: Sister Aquinne. In Darnassus, Sister Aquinne studies beneath the Priesthood of Elune at the Temple of the Moon. She serves in the Temple Gardens as a novice acolyte. Sister Aquinne studies with the Priesthood of Elune in the night elf capital. She learns in the Temple Gardens beneath the Temple of the Moon, guided by the High Priestess and elder sisters. When a once-great creature of the forest needed help, Aquinne sent willing travelers to Priestess A'moora inside the temple to learn what must be done.

npc:skorn-whitecloud.text: Skorn Whitecloud. At Bloodhoof Village, Skorn Whitecloud guides young hunters and helps travelers face Mulgore’s dangers. Skorn Whitecloud lives at Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore and teaches young hunters the ways of the hunt. He shows them to respect the wild creatures of the plains. First, they prove themselves against cunning flatland prowlers. Then they take the claws to Melor Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff. Skorn wants every hunter who takes up bow or spear to understand the balance between predator and prey.

npc:skuerto.text: Skuerto. At Refuge Pointe, Skuerto scouts the dangerous Arathi Highlands for the Alliance. Archmage Malin sent him with Apprentice Kryten to gather arcane reagents and recover artifacts once owned by Malin's old master, Archmage Trelane. Skuerto scouts the dangerous Arathi Highlands for the Alliance. The Ironforge dwarf is stationed at Refuge Pointe with Apprentice Kryten. Archmage Malin directs their search for arcane reagents and powerful artifacts once owned by his old master, Archmage Trelane. Skuerto takes pride in scouting the harsh Highlands and bristles when anyone questions his skill. His work brings him near the region's dangers: the hostile Syndicate, Boulderfist ogres, and ancient entities bound to the land.

npc:smith-argus.text: Smith Argus. At Goldshire's forge, Smith Argus keeps travelers and local smiths supplied. He repairs gear, trains new smiths, and sends horseshoes to Redridge while coordinating with Stormwind craftsmen. Near the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Smith Argus works the forge. Gnolls, kobolds, and Defias bandits threaten the area, so he keeps the local militia and passing adventurers equipped. He mends armor and makes sturdy tools. As a blacksmithing trainer, he teaches new smiths to work copper and bronze. Goldshire's central position makes Smith Argus a link in Stormwind's regional supply. Craftsmen in nearby settlements come to him for specialized gear and raw materials. Farrier Verner Osgood in Redridge depends on Argus for horseshoes for pack animals and cavalry. Metalworkers in Stormwind's Dwarven District also arrange deliveries through him.

npc:solm-hargrin.text: Solm Hargrin. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Solm Hargrin prepares young dwarves and gnomes for the work of a rogue. As tensions rise across Azeroth, he believes covert operatives will be vital. Solm Hargrin teaches his pupils to decipher coded messages and use techniques such as Eviscerate. Ironforge relies on mountaineers and warriors, yet some threats call for quieter methods. So he teaches loyalty to the craft and to one another, preparing his pupils for a more unsettled world.

npc:sprite-darter.text: Sprite Darter. Among Feralas's ancient trees, Sprite Darters flit while the Grimtotem seek to capture them. These rare faerie dragons are revered for their spiritual and magical qualities. Sprite Darters glide through Feralas's ancient forests on iridescent wings. Shy and peaceful, these elusive woodland beasts draw the attention of those who study Kalimdor's wild places for their natural power and resistance to magic. The Grimtotem tauren of Feralas have begun rounding up and caging many Sprite Darters, though no one knows why. Kindal Moonweaver, a concerned night elf, seeks allies to break the cages and free the trapped hatchlings before the Grimtotem bend them to their will. Sprite Darters also interest those who study primal power. At Camp Mojache, Witch Doctor Uzer'i, a troll spiritualist, studies the natural energies and muisek within them. He seeks their essence to understand the unique magic thriving throughout Feralas.

npc:stitches.text: Stitches. Along Duskwood's western road, Stitches marches east toward Darkshire, crushing the Night Watch and unwary travelers in his path. Near Abercrombie's shack, northeast of Raven Hill Cemetery, Stitches sets out east along the road to Darkshire. Unholy sorcery and harvested corpses have made him an undead abomination. His immense strength and malice overwhelm the Night Watch checkpoints. Across from Vul'Gol Ogre Mound and outside the Rotting Orchard, he tears through the defense camp and outpost, slaughtering travelers and town defenders as he goes.

npc:supervisor-raelen.text: Supervisor Raelen. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Supervisor Raelen keeps timber moving toward Stormwind. She directs the laborers, tracks their daily quotas, and watches over the lumber supply. Supervisor Raelen directs the woodcutters at Eastvale Logging Camp, near Marshal Patterson and the camp’s wagons. The camp lies on eastern Elwynn’s edge, near the Redridge Mountains, where the work brings trouble. Raelen coordinates the crews and keeps them focused on their quotas despite hazards in the surrounding woods. She sees that gathered timber is processed, bundled, and sent toward Stormwind.

npc:suzetta-gallina.text: Suzetta Gallina. At the Gallina Winery in Stormwind City, Suzetta Gallina tends her family's wine trade. Along Stormwind's Canals, Suzetta Gallina helps run the Gallina Winery. Its shelves hold wines brought from across the kingdom and wines made there. The family supplies taverns, nobles, and common folk. Her work keeps the capital's trade moving through troubled times.

npc:syral-bladeleaf.text: Syral Bladeleaf. In Dolanaar, Syral Bladeleaf guides night elves arriving from Shadowglen. She speaks for the Council of the Forest and directs newcomers to the caretakers, herbalists, and elders who tend Teldrassil's crown. Syral Bladeleaf guides new arrivals through Dolanaar beneath Teldrassil's canopy. Speaking for the Council of the Forest, she sends night elves to village leaders and herbalists nearby. Her guidance leads travelers to Denalan, a botanist at Lake Al'Ameth, and helps them bring supplies to the village elders. Syral carries out the Council of the Forest's work in Dolanaar. She helps medicinal elixirs reach those in need and makes sure disturbances to the local ecosystem receive swift attention.

npc:syurna.text: Syurna. In Darnassus, Syurna trains night elf rogues in the Cenarion Enclave. She guides new scouts, spies, and covert operatives, then tests their stealth and cunning. Syurna teaches rogues to move unseen through Darnassus. In the Cenarion Enclave, she trains them in evasion, lockpicking, and deadly strikes. The Sentinels show the Kaldorei’s strength in arms, while the Sisterhood of Elune keeps their spiritual wisdom. The Kaldorei also rely on shadows and stealth, and Syurna sharpens the eyes and blades that guard Teldrassil. Syurna tests young operatives beyond the enclave’s lessons. She sends promising initiates into deeper fieldwork to learn whether they have the instincts to survive beyond the World Tree’s boughs. There, they must prove they can serve the Alliance in perilous frontier lands.

npc:tabetha.text: Tabetha. At her farmstead deep in the Quagmire, Tabetha teaches aspiring spellcasters and aids those seeking mastery of arcane and occult relics. North of the Stonemaul Ruins, Tabetha lives in a secluded shack with her apprentices. She chose solitude over the academic hierarchies of the Eastern Kingdoms. Spellcasters cross Kalimdor's beasts and mire to seek her guidance, drawn by her mastery of the arcane. Tabetha welcomes Alliance and Horde initiates who are willing to learn. Though human, she teaches mages and helps warlocks with dangerous bindings such as the Orb of Orahil. Her history with Menara Voidrender reaches into esoteric magic beyond faction allegiance.

npc:tai-jin.text: Tai'jin. At the Razor Hill barracks, Tai'jin teaches young Darkspear priests the balance of light and shadow. She passes on troll spiritual traditions and rites such as the Hex of Weakness. Tai'jin guides young priests from the Razor Hill barracks as they set out across Durotar. Orcs here chiefly follow shamanism or warlock arts. Darkspear trolls bring their communion with spirits and loas to the Horde. Tai'jin teaches the first principles of priesthood and the balance of light and shadow, rooted in troll heritage.

npc:taiga-wisemane.text: Taiga Wisemane. Along Desolace's western coast, Taiga Wisemane keeps watch. From Shadowprey Village, he looks for dark sorceries stirring across the wastes. Shadowprey Village is a Darkspear troll fishing settlement by the ocean. Taiga Wisemane has taken up station there to watch the dark sorceries stirring across Desolace. He knows spiritual corruption is seeping into the soil, and keeps his attention eastward. Shadow cults and demonic remnants fester among the ancient ruins.

npc:takar-the-seer.text: Takar the Seer. East of Camp Taurajo, Takar the Seer keeps to his lone camp in the Barrens. Though Horde lands surround him, he remains loyal to the Alliance and shares occult knowledge with certain travelers. East of Camp Taurajo, Takar the Seer lives alone beneath a simple tent. Tauren braves and orc patrols watch the Barrens around his camp, yet leave his remote clearing undisturbed. He distrusts curious Horde visitors but rarely starts a fight. Instead, he watches the horizon and keeps to himself, far from Stormwind's politics. A few visitors travel beyond Takar's camp to seek his knowledge. Alliance warlocks from the Eastern Kingdoms come for his cryptic counsel as they try to bind dangerous beings from beyond this world. His knowledge of hidden forces and the craft of souls draws these practitioners to his remote, perilous camp.
