npc:takata-steelblade.text: Takata Steelblade. At Ghost Walker Post, Takata Steelblade leads the Horde's fight against demonic corruption in Desolace. Keldran sent him from Orgrimmar with Maurin Bonesplitter, and Takata now hunts satyrs allied with the Burning Blade. Keldran sent Takata Steelblade from Orgrimmar to Desolace to uncover and purge demonic subversion. Takata works from Ghost Walker Post, an isolated Tauren encampment. From there, he coordinates the fight against Legion-aligned forces in the wastes. Maurin Bonesplitter tracks and attacks the Burning Blade cultists. Takata turns his forces against their demonic allies, the satyrs. His strikes have devastated Desolace's corrupted satyrs, aiming to break the cult's local power and stop its taint from spreading.

npc:tal.text:
Tal. At Thunder Bluff, Tal tends the Horde’s chief wind rider roost above the plains of Mulgore. He sends seasoned wyverns carrying travelers across Kalimdor. On Thunder Bluff’s central mesa, Tal tends the wind rider roost that links the tauren capital with the rest of the Horde. He cares for the loyal wyverns and keeps them healthy and well-fed for long journeys across Kalimdor.

From the roost, Tal sends messengers to Camp Taurajo and scouts across the Barrens to Orgrimmar. These flights keep the towering mesa city in touch with its allies.

npc:talen.text: Talen. Along the Zoram Strand, Talen searches the coast for kaldorei relics. Nearby naga and Horde outposts make his work dangerous. At his camp beside the Zoram Strand, Talen studies the past rather than taking up arms. Naga and Horde outposts make the coast dangerous, yet he searches ruins beneath the waves and sands for lost kaldorei relics. He relies on travelers to face the Wrathtail naga and recover artifacts, including pristine statuettes and the Ring of Zoram, held by their leader Ruuzel.

npc:tallow.text:
Tallow. At Tarren Mill, Tallow watches the front lines for the Dark Lady and the Horde. The Forsaken warrior helps organize strikes against Alliance threats in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Tallow stands with the Forsaken and Horde forces holding Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Conflict stirs across the region. Southshore humans are nearby, Syndicate outlaws prowl the roads, and hostile wildlife ranges beyond town.

Tallow sends capable adventurers against the Boulderfist ogres of the Arathi Highlands to test their strength. Then he directs them to aid the besieged outpost of Hammerfall.

npc:talvash-del-kissel.text:
Talvash del Kissel. In Ironforge's Mystic Ward, the gnome jeweler Talvash del Kissel is down on his luck. He fled Gnomeregan when the troggs overran it, then fell into debt amid rumors of questionable dealings. Now he turns to adventurers to recover lost treasures and restore shattered relics. His eye for gems and ancient baubles makes him a valued contact for those exploring Uldaman. Talvash once earned respect as a jeweler in Gnomeregan, until the troggs overran the city and destroyed his livelihood along with his home. He escaped with the surviving refugees to Ironforge and set up camp in the Mystic Ward. Yet relocation brought little relief.

Rumors of questionable dealings and unpaid obligations gathered around him, leaving the craftsman in deep financial distress. Unable to rebuild his trade through conventional means, he now relies on freelance adventurers to recover lost assets and salvage his reputation. Talvash has kept his precision with gems and his skill at judging their worth. When explorers in the Badlands uncover an ancient, shattered necklace deep in Uldaman's Titan vault, few craftsmen in the Eastern Kingdoms can make sense of its intricate enchantments. Restoring its power takes rare components and painstaking work. Talvash is eager to do it, both to clear his debts and prove his skill endures.

npc:tammra-windfield.text: Tammra Windfield. At Sun Rock Retreat, Tammra Windfield guides Horde travelers in honoring the land's renewal. She watches over the Stonetalon wilderness and the safety of her kin. Sun Rock Retreat shelters the Horde among the crags of Stonetalon. Harpies, Venture Company loggers, and predators threaten the settlement. Tammra Windfield watches over the mountain wilderness and the travelers who enter. Her gentle manner is matched by the resolve to keep a home safe in such rugged country. Tammra honors the Earth Mother by tending to nature's steady rhythm of growth and decay. She asks travelers to help renew the land and bring forth new life. Conflict and exploitation have harmed Stonetalon, so she works to heal the mountain soil and let life flourish again. Tammra's care reaches beyond the wilds to the companions and kin who travel Stonetalon's dangerous trails. When travelers or family vanish among the crags, she is among the first to seek reliable aid. Sun Rock Retreat endures through loyalty, mutual protection, and harmony with nature.

npc:tannok-frosthammer.text: Tannok Frosthammer. At Thunderbrew Distillery near Kharanos, Tannok Frosthammer waits for supplies from Coldridge Valley. Trogg attacks have closed the roads to Anvilmar. At Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Tannok Frosthammer watches for deliveries and listens for news. Troggs have poured through Coldridge Pass, closing the usual route from Coldridge Valley and cutting off regular word from Anvilmar. Hands Springsprocket, a gnome tinkerer, carries supplies and news through the dangerous, snowy pass. Tannok shares the worry of many Bronzebeards as subterranean troggs creep closer to their doorsteps.

npc:tarindrella.text:
Tarindrella. In Shadowglen, Tarindrella watches Teldrassil's sheltered woods. The dryad joins night elf protectors in investigating corruption among the World Tree's wildlife. Tarindrella dwells in Shadowglen, a protected glade atop Teldrassil. Dryads are fierce caretakers of nature, born of the demigod Cenarius. Many live deep in ancient Kalimdor forests such as Ashenvale, but Tarindrella watches over this young grove.

She is a bridge between the wild spirits and the young night elf defenders taking their first steps beyond Aldrassil. Her chief concern is a taint creeping through the forest. She sends reliable adventurers to drive back local pests and gather clues to its source. Teldrassil is the new crown of the night elf people, yet sickness has reached its groves. Furbolgs once lived peacefully in their homes, but now they have gathered as the Gnarlpine tribe. Grells and grellkin tainted by wicked Fel Moss infest the hills around Shadowglen. Tarindrella suspects the moss is behind these changes. She directs initiates to confront the grells and bring back samples, hoping to halt the corruption before it overtakes the young grove.

npc:tarrel-rockweaver.text: Tarrel Rockweaver. At Menethil Harbor’s bridge, Tarrel Rockweaver waits anxiously for news of his wife, Merrin. He fears for her safety after she joined an inland archaeological expedition. Trade and military shipments pass over Menethil Harbor’s bridge, where Tarrel Rockweaver keeps watch. His wife, Merrin Rockweaver, joined Prospector Whelgar’s prestigious archaeological expedition deeper in the Wetlands. Violent raptors overran the excavation site and cut off regular word from the team. Stranded in town, Tarrel asks travelers to scout east toward Whelgar’s Excavation Site and learn whether Merrin survived.

npc:tatternack-steelforge.text: Tatternack Steelforge. At the Barrens frontier, Tatternack Steelforge offers work to travelers who can handle raw metal and dangerous wildlife. The orc smith studies local ores to arm Horde forces against threats across the plains. Horde outposts across the Barrens need weapons against wild beasts, centaur raiders, and hostile quilboar. Tatternack Steelforge brings his people's metalworking knowledge to the frontier. He seeks practical weapons and unusual geological specimens to strengthen the Horde's foothold against those threats.

npc:tenaron-stormgrip.text: Tenaron Stormgrip. High in Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip guides young night elves through their people's recent history. He also asks them to gather water from a moonwell. Tenaron Stormgrip guides young night elves along Aldrassil's winding wooden platforms. From Shadowglen's central tree, he watches the local woods and their moonwells. He teaches novices about their spiritual bond with the World Tree. Tenaron sends initiates to gather a phial of water from the moonwell north of Aldrassil. Along the way, he teaches them what followed the Battle of Mount Hyjal. Their journey carries on through Teldrassil and into Darnassus.

npc:teronis-corpse.text: Teronis' Corpse. On an island in western Ashenvale, Teronis' Corpse lies in Lake Falathim. The night elf scout left Astranaar seeking Dartol's Rod to help cleanse the forest. Teronis was a night elf scout sent from Astranaar by Raene Wolfrunner to recover Dartol's Rod. The ancient relic could cleanse corrupted woodland magic. Teronis searched Lake Falathim, but hostile murlocs swarmed the island and killed him. His journal remains there, while the murlocs took the rod's radiant gemstone.

npc:thadius-grimshade.text: Thadius Grimshade. At Nethergarde Keep, Thadius Grimshade seeks knowledge in divination and darker magic. Though long gone from Aerie Peak, he remains loyal to his kin. Thadius Grimshade lives within Nethergarde Keep, far from the open skies and roaring winds favored by most Wildhammer dwarves. He came to the edge of the tainted Blasted Lands to study arcane divination and darker mystic lore. Though apart from his clan, he still cherishes his homeland and gryphonkind. When folk from Aerie Peak seek his aid, he offers his rare skill in scrying.

npc:thalia-amberhide.text: Thalia Amberhide. At Freewind Post, Thalia Amberhide waits for Lakota Windsong to return safely. Her friend was taken by the Grimtotem clan in Thousand Needles. At Freewind Post, Thalia Amberhide waits for word of Lakota Windsong. Arnak Grimtotem and his kin captured her close companion. Thalia needs passing Horde travelers to search the canyon depths, free Lakota, and guide her back up the lifts to the mesa settlement.

npc:tharek-blackstone.text: Tharek Blackstone. At the forge in Kharanos, Tharek Blackstone makes and repairs tools for local craftsmen. His trade keeps him busy, so he hires travelers to carry finished crates to Beldin Steelgrill at Steelgrill's Depot. Beldin's mechanostrider depot just outside town needs heavy wrenches, gears, and replacement tools. Tharek sends each crate there with a passing traveler, keeping deliveries moving while he stays at the forge. Craftsmen across Kharanos also rely on the tools he makes and repairs. Tharek has earned respect across Dun Morogh through his work at the anvil. He holds no military title, yet people in town turn to him for odd jobs, supply runs, and help coordinating local efforts.

npc:tharnariun-treetender.text: Tharnariun Treetender. In Auberdine, Tharnariun Treetender watches for sickness in Darkshore’s wilds. The night elf naturalist studies the corruption spreading through plants and animals, seeking ways to protect them. Tharnariun Treetender watches the woods beyond Auberdine’s port. Satyrs and foul shoreline washaways threaten the village, yet his work is with the natural world around it. He believes neglecting nature invites ruin. So he studies the decline of the local woods and seeks ways to fight the sickness spreading across the forest floor.

npc:the-defias-traitor.text: The Defias Traitor. At Sentinel Hill, The Defias Traitor has revealed the Brotherhood's hidden base to spare his life. The People's Militia caught him stealing Farmer Saldean's wagon and now holds him beneath the watchtower.

npc:theldurin-the-lost.text:
Theldurin the Lost. Theldurin the Lost wanders the Badlands alone, wary and half-mad. He fled the Twilight's Hammer with sacred relics after learning what the cult intended. Theldurin wanders the barren hills of the Badlands with bags of explosives, gripped by wild paranoia. He once belonged to the Twilight's Hammer. When the cult sought to awaken a primordial elemental power trapped beneath the earth, he recoiled in terror.

He rejected its teachings and fled into the desert. He carried the Scroll of Myzrael, hoping to keep his former masters from unleashing an ancient horror upon the world. His escape cost him his sanity, but his defiance dealt a serious blow to the cult's plans.

npc:therylune.text: Therylune. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, Therylune waits for help to escape the Twilight's Hammer cultists who hold her captive. Therylune is a dryad, a daughter of Cenarius who guards nature. She came from the tranquil woodlands of northern Kalimdor to the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore. There, Twilight's Hammer cultists ambushed her at the ancient excavation. Surrounded by their swarms, she cannot fight her way free alone. She needs an escort through the cultists and out to safety.

npc:therysil.text: Therysil. At the Shrine of Aessina in central Ashenvale, Therysil waits for news of her sister. A daughter of Cenarius, she guards the wild and its spirits, while Therylune remains in the hands of the Twilight's Hammer cultists. Therysil keeps watch beside the waters of the Shrine of Aessina, in Ashenvale's ancient woods. As a dryad and daughter of Cenarius, she is bound to defend the wild and its spirits. Now her thoughts turn to Therylune, captured nearby by the deranged Twilight's Hammer cult. Therysil waits for a wandering ally to help rescue her sister.

npc:thor.text: Thor. At Sentinel Hill, Thor keeps Westfall linked to Stormwind by gryphon flight. His trained mounts carry travelers and urgent messages over dangerous roads. Thor tends the gryphon roost at Sentinel Hill, linking Westfall's defenders with the rest of the kingdom. On the ground, the People's Militia faces bandits, gnolls, and malfunctioning harvest golems. His gryphons carry travelers and military dispatches above those perilous roads. Reports from Gryan Stoutmantle and urgent requests for aid can reach the court in Stormwind far sooner than a messenger on foot.

npc:thorgas-grimson.text: Thorgas Grimson. Inside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Thorgas Grimson teaches new hunters to face Dun Morogh's frozen wilds. The seasoned outdoorsman trusts experience in the cold to teach survival. Inside Anvilmar, Thorgas Grimson guides new mountaineers and scouts. He leaves dry lessons behind and sends young hunters into the freezing winds. With bow or gun in hand, they track Dun Morogh's rugged beasts firsthand.

npc:thorgrum-borrelson.text: Thorgrum Borrelson. Above Thelsamar, Thorgrum Borrelson keeps travelers flying across Loch Modan. His roost links the valley with Ironforge and the nearby mountain passes. Thorgrum Borrelson keeps the gryphon roost on the bluff above Thelsamar. His trained gryphons carry the Alliance across Loch Modan, where troggs and gnoll packs threaten the roads. They pass through South Gate Pass to the Great Forge in Dun Morogh, then fly onward toward the Wetlands and beyond.

npc:thorvald-deepforge.text: Thorvald Deepforge. At the Valley of Kings, travelers bound for Loch Modan find Thorvald Deepforge ready with weapons. He helps defend the pass between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Thorvald Deepforge supplies weapons at the Valley of Kings. Troggs and roaming wildlife threaten the mountain passes between Khaz Modan's heartland and its outlying lands. Travelers from Dun Morogh and those bound deeper into Loch Modan can find blades and axes here, ready to defend dwarven lands.

npc:thran-khorman.text: Thran Khorman. At Anvilmar, Thran Khorman readies new warriors for the dangers of Coldridge Valley. Thran Khorman drills dwarven recruits and visiting gnomes on Anvilmar’s grounds. Gruff and demanding, he has little patience for anyone without the grit for front-line fighting. The Third War has ended, yet troggs still press into Coldridge Pass. So Thran demands relentless practice with axe, mace, and shield, keeping Ironforge’s defenders ready.

npc:thunderaan.text: Thunderaan. In Silithus, Thunderaan's scattered bindings may open the way to his return. Ragnaros struck down the Prince of Air and sealed away the essence he could not consume. Highlord Demitrian waits for those who recover both halves. During the Elemental Sundering, fire and air warred deep within Azeroth for five thousand years. Ragnaros sought Thunderaan's destruction and power. Baron Geddon and Garr, his lieutenants, ambushed and betrayed the Prince. Then Ragnaros struck him down with Sulfuras, the Firelord's hammer. Thunderaan's essence was too mighty for Ragnaros to consume in full. Ragnaros could not devour all of the Prince of Air's essence. He sealed what remained in a talisman of elemental binding, then shattered it into two flawless halves so Thunderaan could not reform. Baron Geddon received one half and Garr the other. Both were hidden in the volcanic depths of the Molten Core beneath Blackrock Mountain.

npc:tommy-joe-stonefield.text: Tommy Joe Stonefield. On the river west of Stonefield Farm, Tommy Joe Stonefield longs for Maybell Maclure. Their families have feuded for years, so he depends on secret notes and quiet riverbanks to keep their love hidden. Tommy Joe Stonefield waits by the river west of Stonefield Farm, watching the Maclure homestead across the water. The Stonefields and Maclures have clashed for years over land, pride, and farmyard squabbles. Their elders keep the feud alive, yet Tommy Joe has fallen in love with Maybell Maclure. The two cannot meet openly without angering both households. Gramma Stonefield, Tommy Joe’s sympathetic grandmother, helps them exchange secret notes and tokens of affection.

npc:tormus-deepforge.text: Tormus Deepforge. At Ironforge’s Great Forge, Tormus Deepforge keeps weapons flowing to the Alliance. He forges weapons for young warriors and mourns his mentor, Sturgy Ironband. Beside the Great Forge fires, Tormus Deepforge oversees the Bronzebeard clan’s metalwork. He still hammers steel himself, though he mourns Sturgy Ironband, his mentor. Dark Iron dwarves overran Sturgy’s smithing compound south of Helm’s Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh. A load of strange umbral ore had arrived there.

npc:torwa-pathfinder.text: Torwa Pathfinder. At Un'Goro Crater's entrance, Torwa Pathfinder watches and tracks the wilds. The lone tauren hunter camps below the ramp from Tanaris, studying the basin's primordial wildlife and dangerous predators. Adventurers who seek to test themselves against its legendary beasts come to him for guidance. Torwa Pathfinder camps at the crater's eastern base, where Tanaris's desert gives way to jungle. He respects Un'Goro's wild forces and watches newcomers in his own way, knowing careless wanderers can become prey. His camp gives travelers a place to pause before they enter the jungle depths. Torwa Pathfinder spends much of his time tracking Lar'korwi, a fierce and cunning raptor in the crater's north. Brute strength alone will not bring down such a predator. He teaches hunters to study its feeding habits, then use fresh carcass meat and glands as bait to draw Lar'korwi into the open. Torwa Pathfinder studies poisonous plants and aggressive ape colonies, as well as the crater's raptors. He sends travelers to gather venom from volatile bloodpetals and watch powerful beasts such as U'cha, the mighty gorilla. Torwa seeks to understand how nature's deadliest defenses work in isolation.

npc:treshala-fallowbrook.text: Treshala Fallowbrook. In Darnassus, Treshala Fallowbrook waits at home for word of her husband. Heralath Fallowbrook has gone far away, into Razorfen Kraul in the Barrens. On the second floor of a Tradesmen's Terrace workshop, Treshala Fallowbrook waits for word from her husband. Heralath journeyed to Razorfen Kraul in the Barrens, where thorny growth surrounds the quilboar warrens. Their marriage is marked by a pendant of bonding, which Heralath carried with him.

npc:tsunaman.text: Tsunaman. At Sun Rock Retreat, Tsunaman watches Kalimdor’s currents for signs of unrest. He works with the Horde against forces that threaten the waters. Near the path from Sun Rock Retreat to the Charred Vale, Tsunaman serves the Tribunal of the Tides. Its high-ranking members are aligned with Neptulon, the Tidehunter. With the Horde, Tsunaman watches for elemental unrest across Kalimdor, especially disturbances spreading from the submerged caverns of Blackfathom Deeps. Tsunaman hates fire in every form. The burning lands of the Charred Vale and incursions by fire elementals keep him fuming. Around camp, he sometimes marches to nearby cooking fires and campfires, then smacks them out with a heavy fist of water.

npc:tyrion.text: Tyrion. Inside Stormwind Keep, Tyrion watches the court and aids covert work. The gnome gathers intelligence with Elling Trias and helps counter plots against the kingdom. Tyrion watches the halls of Stormwind Keep and keeps an eye on the palace. He also stays in touch with contacts beyond official oversight. Elling Trias, a cheese merchant in the Trade District, trusts Tyrion with sensitive matters. Trias runs a discreet information network and sends reliable operatives to Tyrion when the House of Nobles' bureaucracy must be bypassed.

npc:ukor.text:
Ukor. Outside the Valley of Trials, Ukor rests after carrying food south from Razor Hill. The grounds had enough provisions already, but he hopes his people can still use them. Ukor rests by the eastern road outside the Valley of Trials, tired after carrying food south from Razor Hill. Orc peons spend their days cutting lumber or hauling rocks for harsh taskmasters. Ukor chose to bring provisions to the recruits on his own initiative.

He crossed Durotar’s red plains, where scorpids and boars prowl, only to find the training grounds already well stocked. His bundle was not needed. Now he asks passing young adventurers to carry it north to Innkeeper Grosk.

npc:ula-elek.text: Ula'elek. In Sen'jin Village, Ula'elek forges armor for warriors across the Horde. This Darkspear smith works with Thun'grim Firegaze, shaping specialized gear through traditional troll craft and trophies gathered across Kalimdor. Ula'elek serves the Darkspear as an armorsmith in Sen'jin Village. Nearby quilboar and sea crawlers threaten the coastal settlement, so the tribe needs sturdy armor and sound blades. Ula'elek's skill also brings seasoned warriors from across the Horde to his forge. Young warriors who visit Thun'grim Firegaze at his overlook in the Barrens are sent south to Sen'jin Village. The veteran trusts Ula'elek to forge Brutal Gauntlets for battle-hardened fighters. The work calls for rare materials, especially swollen, uncloven hooves from the satyrs draining the forest's magic in northeastern Ashenvale.

npc:umpi.text: Umpi. In Tarren Mill, Umpi suffers through Apothecary Lydon's experiments. The frog is kept in the Royal Apothecary Society's workshop for tests of toxins and plague brews. In Tarren Mill, Umpi is a frog who bears the cost of Apothecary Lydon's experiments. He tests his formulas on living flesh, giving Umpi lethal brews such as the Elixir of Suffering and the Elixir of Agony. The poisons kill her. Then Lydon re-animates her for another dose in service of the Royal Apothecary Society.

npc:undertaker-mordo.text:
Undertaker Mordo. At Deathknell's crypt, Undertaker Mordo greets Forsaken as they wake to a world changed. He tells them they are free of the Lich King's control and sends those with their wits toward Queen Sylvanas's cause. The bodies that never stir are cast into the fire. In Tirisfal Glades, corpses break free of the Scourge at Deathknell's crypt. Newly awakened Forsaken find a world they no longer recognize. Undertaker Mordo tests their sanity and tells them what they have become. Then he directs them to serve Queen Sylvanas Windrunner. Some bodies brought to the crypt never wake. Mordo soon casts them into the fire. Those who stir meet his dry impatience and little ceremony.

If the newly risen have kept their wits, Mordo sends them up the steps and down the road to the chapel. There, Shadow Priest Sarvis explains their new existence. The mindless zombies overrunning the village's north are Sarvis's concern, so he sends the newly risen to destroy them.

npc:ur-kyo.text: Ur'kyo. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, Ur'kyo guides priests in shadow and light. The Darkspear look to him as their spiritual leader and greatest priest, and he teaches their traditions in the Horde capital. From Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, Ur'kyo guides Darkspear mystics and visiting priests. The Darkspear fled the Echo Isles and made a home in Durotar beside Thrall's Horde. Their sacred traditions still hold the tribe together, so Ur'kyo keeps the old practices alive through his teaching. Priests who come to Ur'kyo find a patient teacher of faith and old rites. He teaches the Hex of Weakness and the defensive ward called Shadowguard. Horde priests also seek his counsel on the coalition's many spiritual ways, from troll voodoo and ancestral customs to foreign disciplines.

npc:uzzek.text: Uzzek. Southwest of Far Watch Post, Uzzek trains warriors crossing the eastern Barrens. The battle-hardened orc survived many skirmishes across Kalimdor and now tests promising Horde fighters. Southwest of Far Watch Post, Uzzek trains young warriors near the eastern edge of the Barrens. He endured brutal combat in the recent wars. Now he tests those learning to defend themselves against the savage wildlife and raiders troubling the crossing.

npc:valstag-ironjaw.text: Valstag Ironjaw. At Menethil Keep, Valstag Ironjaw helps guard the road between Loch Modan and the coast. He warns the garrison of dangers to travelers and supplies. Valstag Ironjaw serves with the dwarven garrison inside Menethil Keep in Menethil Harbor. Dragonmaw orcs and ravenous wildlife threaten their communications and supplies. So he helps coordinate defenses on the main roads, especially the perilous way through Dun Algaz toward Loch Modan. Hostile forces crowd the Algaz Gauntlet, putting travelers and supply convoys between Menethil Harbor and Loch Modan at risk. Valstag sends capable adventurers against the brigands and orcs in the passes. He also carries military reports between forward scouts and commanders such as Captain Stoutfist.

npc:vanndar-stormpike.text: Vanndar Stormpike. At Dun Baldar, Vanndar Stormpike leads the Stormpike Expedition through the frozen peaks of Alterac Valley. He seeks ancient relics and raw resources while waging war against the Frostwolf orcs. Vanndar Stormpike leads the dwarven excavation in Alterac Valley as a veteran mountain king of Ironforge. After the Third War, he marched the Stormpike Guard into the northern mountains in search of hidden mineral riches and long-lost titan artifacts. Dun Baldar became his fortified base. He claims the valley as ancestral ground and rightful Alliance territory, and directs its outposts, bunkers, and frontline advances. Under Vanndar's command, retreat is never sounded. Vanndar's mining and prospecting reached into the Frostwolf clan's home, and a brutal mountain war began. The orcs demanded his withdrawal, but he refused to yield an inch. He vowed that Alterac Valley would belong to the dwarves. From his throne room deep within Dun Baldar, Vanndar oversees the defense against Frostwolf incursions, with marshals and bodyguards at his side. He also sends Alliance champions to break enemy lines and claim the valley.

npc:varok-saurfang.text: Varok Saurfang. In Orgrimmar, Varok Saurfang commands the Horde's forces under Warchief Thrall. He brings the strength and hard-won experience of the Old Horde's wars to the young Horde. Varok Saurfang carries the Old Horde's wars into the present. Few living warriors can match his record, and many regard him as unstoppable in battle. As High Overlord in Orgrimmar, he helps hold together Thrall's newborn Horde. Varok Saurfang defends the Horde and enforces Thrall's rule against threats. He does not seek battle for its own sake. He despises warmongering and fights for honor and the Horde's survival.

npc:velarok.text: Velarok. Among the ash and slain dwarves in Searing Gorge, Velarok Windblade asks travelers to help him forge vengeance. Southeast of Thorium Point, Velarok Windblade camps in the wastes of Searing Gorge. Dark Iron dwarves lie dead around him, slain in the fight he says began with his father's murder. He asks travelers to gather what he needs to make the Torch of Retribution. The enchanted weapon is meant for the Dark Irons and Ragnaros's minions.

npc:velora-nitely.text:
Velora Nitely. In the Undercity's Trade Quarter, Velora Nitely forges armor for the Forsaken and the Horde. Once among Lordaeron's finest armorsmiths, she now makes dry jokes that rarely land. Near the anvils in the Undercity's Trade Quarter, Velora Nitely makes armor for the Horde. Before the Third War devastated the north, Lordaeron celebrated her as an exceptional armorsmith. Undeath took her life and warmth, but left her skill untouched.

Velora works with Horde crafters across continents, including Thun'grim Firegaze in the Barrens. She reinforces heavy battle plate and forges the formidable Brutal Legguards from hardened materials such as Dragonmaw shinbones. At the forge, Velora Nitely keeps trying to make jokes, though they rarely land. Many of her somber Forsaken kin brood over their cursed fate, but she still makes room for levity. Death seems to have ruined her timing. Her quips sound flat, morbid, and thoroughly unfunny to the living and the dead alike, yet she keeps cracking them.

npc:ventaari-brightwish.text: Ventaari Brightwish. In Thendal Village, Ventaari Brightwish welcomes travelers from across Azeroth and offers them The Gift of Skysight. Ventaari Brightwish welcomes newcomers to Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. As a Skyborne resident, she helps visitors from both the Alliance and the Horde. Through The Gift of Skysight, Ventaari introduces them to her people's traditions.

npc:verna-furlbrow.text:
Verna Furlbrow. Near Westfall’s northern border, Verna Furlbrow waits beside her broken wagon. Outlaws drove her from the family pumpkin patch, and the road toward Elwynn Forest left her stranded. Verna and her husband farmed pumpkins in northern Westfall until lawlessness drove them away. Outlaws took the farm, so they loaded what they could onto their cart and set out for Elwynn Forest with their horse, Old Blanchy. Their wagon broke down just down the road from the abandoned Jansen Stead.

The broken axle keeps them from going on. Verna faces the elements, bandit raids, and scavengers, and depends on travelers to keep her household fed and guarded. Verna still welcomes those forced to the roadside. Known across the region for creating Westfall Stew, she shares meals and warm fires with wandering transients and refugees who have suffered similar fates.

Her cooking pot needs ingredients from the fields: boar snouts, murloc eyes, okra, and stringy vulture meat. From what the harsh frontier provides, Verna makes hearty meals for the destitute.

npc:veron-amberstill.text: Veron Amberstill. At Amberstill Ranch in eastern Dun Morogh, Veron Amberstill raises the rams Ironforge riders trust. Veron breeds and trains mountain rams for the high cold country. Their sure feet and thick coats carry them over Khaz Modan’s steep slopes and through its blizzards. Veron raises them for dwarven scouts, mountaineers, and traveling adventurers. He offers standard and swift mounts to fellow dwarves. Riders from other peoples must prove loyalty to Ironforge’s throne before he parts with a ram.

npc:veronica-nials.text: Veronica Nials. At Refuge Pointe, Captain Veronica Nials directs Stromgarde's defense as her kingdom crumbles. Her forces face Syndicate treachery and Boulderfist ogres in the Arathi Highlands. After the Third War, Stromgarde shattered. Boulderfist ogres invaded, and the Syndicate betrayed its people. At Refuge Pointe, Captain Veronica Nials commands the surviving Stromgarde defenders. She directs Alliance champions against Syndicate leaders, including Lord Falconcrest and the warlock Marez Cowl. She also seeks badges from fallen soldiers so their families can learn what became of them. When Rhag Garmason and the dwarven defenders of Dun Modr asked Stromgarde for help, Captain Nials had to refuse. Dark Iron saboteurs had devastated the Thandol Span, but her troops could not spare a single blade beyond the Arathi Highlands. Honor and duty bound them to defend their homeland while Stromgarde remained occupied.

npc:vesprystus.text:
Vesprystus. At Rut'theran Village, Vesprystus guides travelers between Teldrassil and mainland Kalimdor. He tends the hippogryph roost beneath the great World Tree. At Teldrassil's southern base, Vesprystus tends the Rut'theran roost. Trained hippogryphs carry travelers from the secluded elven boughs to Darkshore and the mainland. A magical portal links Rut'theran with Darnassus in the canopy above.

Across the strait, Vesprystus works with Auberdine's flight master. Together they carry sentinels, emissaries, and adventurers into Kalimdor.

npc:vidra-hearthstove.text: Vidra Hearthstove. At Thelsamar’s Stoutlager Inn, Vidra Hearthstove cooks blood sausages with game from the surrounding wilderness. Vidra keeps the inn supplied for locals and travelers. Like the innkeeper, she bears the Hearthstove name. Her blood sausages call for fresh game: boar entrails, spider ichor, and bear meat.

npc:volcor.text: Volcor. Deep in southern Darkshore, Volcor lies wounded in Blackwood Den. The night elf scout depends on his bear Grimclaw and Auberdine's defenders to escape the hostile furbolgs. Volcor, a wounded night elf scout, lies inside Blackwood Den. He was tracking the corrupted Blackwood tribe through its underground lair when the furbolgs ambushed him and badly hurt him. Unable to fight his way past them, he sent Grimclaw, his loyal bear companion, into the wilds of Darkshore to seek help in Auberdine.

npc:vorn-skyseer.text: Vorn Skyseer. At Camp Narache, Vorn Skyseer welcomes young tauren as they begin their journeys. He lives among the tents on Red Cloud Mesa and helps newcomers settle into camp life. At Camp Narache, Vorn Skyseer greets young tauren as they begin their rites of passage. They are preparing to leave Red Cloud Mesa for the wider valleys of Mulgore, and his kind welcome helps them settle into camp life. Vorn Skyseer leaves the camp's defense to its braves. He watches over the plains of his homeland, living quietly and without hurry.

npc:warcaller-gorlach.text: Warcaller Gorlach. Across Orgrimmar, Warcaller Gorlach calls Horde champions to distant battlefronts. He rallies travelers and seasoned warriors to answer commands at outposts across Kalimdor and beyond. Warcaller Gorlach walks Orgrimmar's thoroughfares with the Horde's calls for expansion and defense. Among the city's people, he seeks volunteers ready to test their mettle. He sends some to contested Ashenvale. Others he directs to Camp Mojache in Feralas, where scouts face the wilderness. He calls warriors to campaigns in the distant Plaguelands as threats rise abroad.

npc:warlord-goretooth.text:
Warlord Goretooth. At Kargath, Warlord Goretooth directs the Horde's frontier campaigns. From his tower, he watches the Dark Iron dwarves and the danger of Blackrock Mountain. At times, he leaves his lookout to relax by the campfire. Warlord Goretooth directs Horde operations from Kargath's watchtower. The outpost is Orgrimmar's main staging ground against dangers in Blackrock Mountain and the ravines around it. Goretooth oversees patrols and coordinates scouts such as the Kargath Expeditionary Force. He also orders attacks on the Dark Iron clan's ranks and leaders.

Away from his lookout, the stern commander sometimes warms himself by the campfire. There, he trades quips with the Forsaken casters before returning to duty. Warlord Goretooth sees the Dark Iron dwarves as a direct threat to Horde interests in the Eastern Kingdoms. He favors attacks over defense and plans strikes against General Angerforge and Emperor Dagran Thaurissan's forces in Blackrock Depths. Assaulting an ancient stronghold beneath the earth is no small undertaking.

Before approving another push into the mountain, Goretooth often seeks counsel from veteran orcs such as Eitrigg in Orgrimmar.

npc:warmaster-laggrond.text: Warmaster Laggrond. At Alterac Valley's entrance, Warmaster Laggrond prepares Horde fighters for the Frostwolf clan. From the valley entrance in the Alterac Mountains, he calls warriors to aid the Frostwolves. Warmaster Laggrond directs the Horde's fight against the Stormpike Expedition at Alterac Valley's entrance. The cold is bitter there. He accepts only capable fighters to represent the Frostwolf clan and the wider Horde. Warmaster Laggrond sends new combatants through the Proving Grounds before they enter battle. As warriors fight across the frozen peaks, he measures their standing. Those who earn renown among the Frostwolves receive his honor.

npc:warsong-outrider.text: Warsong Outrider. On the road east from Ashenvale, the Warsong Outrider keeps watch over the Horde's frontier. She scouts for the Warsong clan, watches travelers, and sends word to its forward encampments. She holds her fire unless provoked. Far from Splintertree Post and the lumber camps, the Warsong Outrider watches the road between Ashenvale and Azshara's shattered ruins. She tracks troop movements along the route. Her bow and toxic stingers are ready, but she fires only at Alliance trespassers who attack her.

npc:watch-captain-parker.text: Watch Captain Parker. At Three Corners, Watch Captain Parker keeps watch over the road to Lakeshire. He patrols the junction and tracks the gnoll packs gathering nearby, guarding travelers bound for town. Watch Captain Parker guards the roads where Elwynn Forest, Duskwood, and Redridge meet at Three Corners. Stormwind has few troops to spare, and little official help reaches the region. So Parker and the other lone watchmen must keep the crossroads clear of bandits, prowling predators, and raiding gnolls. Gnoll camps gathering north and east of Parker’s post hold his attention. As the packs press closer to the road, he sends able-bodied travelers to warn Deputy Feldon in Lakeshire. The Redridge gnolls grow bolder, threatening supply convoys and refugees seeking shelter in town. A lonely roadside post can be grim, but kindness reaches Three Corners. Darcy, a server at the Lakeshire Inn, sends Parker a warm lunch while he patrols. Touched by her kindness, Parker asks the traveler who brought it to fetch a bouquet from Lakeshire’s herbalist and carry it back to Darcy. He asks that the herbalist not be told who the flowers are from or for.

npc:watcher-backus.text: Watcher Backus. Along Duskwood’s road, Watcher Backus keeps watch for danger and suspicious traffic tied to Stormwind’s political intrigues. He patrols between Darkshire and Manor Mistmantle, looking for undead and strange travelers. North of Darkshire, Watcher Backus walks a lonely beat past Manor Mistmantle. Like the rest of the Night Watch, he struggles against Duskwood’s curse. Stormwind’s garrison offers little help, so local volunteers guard the misty paths alone. Backus keeps beasts and ghouls at bay along the road.

npc:watcher-dodds.text:
Watcher Dodds. At the crossroads in central Duskwood, Watcher Dodds keeps watch for the Night Watch. From his roadside post, he watches for danger and asks travelers to thin the giant spider population. Watcher Dodds guards the crossroads for the Night Watch, under Commander Althea Ebonlocke. The roads from Darkshire, Raven Hill, and Deadwind Pass meet at his post.

Darkshire's palisades shelter the town, but Dodds watches for threats beyond them. Wolf packs, ravenous ghouls, and oversized spiders roam the roads. From his roadside camp, he asks passing mercenaries to kill spiders emerging from the undergrowth before they overrun the roads.

npc:wilder-thistlenettle.text: Wilder Thistlenettle. In Stormwind’s Dwarven District, Wilder Thistlenettle drinks alone, burdened by old grief. He entered Moonbrook’s Deadmines with his brother and their mining crew, but a cave-in left him the sole survivor. Wilder Thistlenettle drinks away his sorrow in an alehouse near the Dwarven District’s southeastern gates. Years ago, he entered the deep lodes of Moonbrook’s Deadmines with his brother and their companions. A cave-in sealed the rest of the crew underground. Wilder barely reached the surface alive.

npc:wiley-the-black.text: Wiley the Black. At the Lakeshire Inn, Wiley the Black stays clear of trouble. He owes his life to Gryan Stoutmantle and shares what he knows of the Defias Brotherhood. Wiley the Black keeps to the Lakeshire Inn, far from Westfall's turmoil and Redridge's gnoll-infested borders. Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia, once saved his life. Stoutmantle grumbles that he should have let Wiley rot. So when the militia needs insight into the Defias conspiracy, it turns to Wiley. Reluctantly, he shares covert intelligence to repay his debt.

npc:willem.text:
Willem. Outside Northshire Abbey, Willem sends recruits to face the threats gathering in the valley. He serves under Marshal McBride as the Defias Brotherhood presses into Northshire. Deputy Willem watches the gates of Northshire Abbey, where the Stormwind Army holds a foothold in the valley. The kingdom's soldiers are spread across many territories, so small groups like Marshal McBride's garrison must defend the land nearby.

Willem greets incoming volunteers and sends them to aid residents and guard the valley's edges. The Defias Brotherhood is Willem's most pressing concern. Bandits in red bandanas have entered Northshire, stolen supplies, threatened farmer Milly Osworth, and taken footholds among nearby vineyards and hills.

Willem offers bounties on known cutthroats such as Garrick Padfoot. He hopes to break their leadership before they can take the abbey grounds.

npc:williden-marshal.text: Williden Marshal. At Marshal's Refuge, Williden Marshal keeps his expedition alive after beasts drove it from Un'Goro Crater's lower camps. He still hopes the crater's plants, crystals and scientific research will bring discovery and profit. Williden Marshal brought a scientific expedition into Un'Goro Crater to seek discovery and fortune. Strange crystals, unrecorded plants and other resources drew him to the valley floor, where he set up several camps. The crater's beasts soon tore through the research posts. Williden and the survivors fled to the northern cliffs and made their base at Marshal's Refuge. Williden refuses to abandon the expedition after losing its lower camps. From Marshal's Refuge, he asks travelers to search the lowlands for lost food crates, scientific instruments and his expedition journal. Close companions such as Spark Nilminer call him Wil, but Williden takes the work seriously. The expedition's research remains in the valley, beneath the paths of its great predators. Hol'anyee Marshal works alongside Williden at Marshal's Refuge. The two Marshals chose the wild crater in southern Kalimdor for their expedition. Williden still believes Un'Goro's crystal deposits and ancient mysteries can bring them fortune.

npc:winna-hazzard.text: Winna Hazzard. At Bloodvenom Post, Winna Hazzard studies the blight spreading through Felwood's living things. The Forsaken researcher watches local wildlife and experiments on corrupted creatures, often laughing beside her feline companion. At Bloodvenom Post, Winna Hazzard studies Felwood's unnatural decay. The Forsaken researcher watches local wildlife and tests tainted water and venomous samples. Her jovial, manic manner can mask callous motives. With liquids drawn from the land, she corrupts the small kitten at her side.

npc:winstone-wolfe.text: Winstone Wolfe. At Ravenholdt Manor, Winstone Wolfe watches over the estate grounds. He serves Lord Jorach Ravenholdt's secretive organization, hidden between Hillsbrad and the Alterac Mountains. Winstone Wolfe works with Lord Jorach Ravenholdt's syndicate at Ravenholdt Manor. Quiet and watchful, he handles business around the manor and keeps an eye on its grounds and groundskeepers. Only those with discretion and talent pass there undisturbed.

npc:witch-doctor-jin-zil.text: Witch Doctor Jin'Zil. In Malaka'jin, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil turns dark voodoo against the Horde's enemies. The Darkspear mystic keeps to a cave in the southern Stonetalon Mountains and has long been a comrade of Darsok Swiftdagger and the shadow hunter Rokhan. In a cave east of Malaka'jin, Jin'Zil practices the ancient arts of jungle trolls, far from his tribe's coastal home. Bubbling cauldrons and captive prisoners fill his cavern. He gathers exotic reagents from the Stonetalon crags and weaves blessings and curses to defend the Horde's mountain camp. Jin'Zil is an old friend of Darsok Swiftdagger and the shadow hunter Rokhan. Darsok leads the Horde's frontline skirmishes against night elves and harpies. Jin'Zil wages the war through spirit and alchemy, using forest magic and volatile voodoo to weaken threats before they reach the camp gates.

npc:witch-doctor-uzer-i.text: Witch Doctor Uzer'i. At Camp Mojache, Witch Doctor Uzer'i seeks to bind the spirits of powerful natural creatures into weapons for the Horde. He calls those lingering spirits muisek and studies magic the night elves have used for millennia. Witch Doctor Uzer'i studies Feralas's natural magic through the old rites of troll spiritualism. Night elves have drawn on forest beast spirits for millennia, and Uzer'i believes the Horde should claim that power. He calls a creature's lingering spirit muisek. His vessels shrink fallen beings and trap their spirits before they escape, so he can store and study their essence. Capturing muisek is only the beginning of Uzer'i's ambition. He gathers sinew, enchanted minerals, and petrified splintered logs from the creatures whose spirits he traps. Then he joins those materials with bound muisek. Through his rites, he binds ancient forest spirits into weapons for the Horde. Uzer'i also follows rumors of hidden places of power across Azeroth, including the ancient, submerged Sunken Temple.

npc:wizlo-bearingshiner.text: Wizlo Bearingshiner. At Whitereach Post, Wizlo Bearingshiner waits for help after centaur attacked his caravan. The goblin tinkerer survived alone, while his clients still await their wares. He asks travelers to recover a valuable Hypercapacitor Gizmo from the wreckage. Wizlo Bearingshiner waits with the tauren at Whitereach Post, along the canyon road. Centaur attacked his caravan and left him as its only survivor. His clients still await their wares, and he fears he will not deliver them in time. Wizlo's best gizmo hangs around the neck of a fierce panther caged beside his ruined caravan, north of Whitereach Post. Even the centaur avoid the beast. Wizlo offers travelers the cage key and a reward for recovering the hypercapacitor. He does not know what the device does.

npc:wizzle-brassbolts.text: Wizzle Brassbolts. At the Mirage Raceway, Wizzle Brassbolts gathers local materials for the gnomish team's experimental rocket cars. He works with fellow tinkerers on the salt flats of Thousand Needles. On the Shimmering Flats, gnomish and goblin engineers race rocket cars at high speed. Wizzle Brassbolts works with the gnomish crew to keep their machines whole against speed and abrasive salt. He asks travelers to hunt local wildlife, including sturdy turtles in the basin. Their hard shells may make fuel tanks strong enough to hold his brother's corrosive new rocket fuel. Wizzle keeps in touch with friends across the continents. Pilot Longbeard sends couriers with racing helmets for the brothers. Their help keeps the gnomish team supplied at its remote testing ground on the Shimmering Flats.

npc:wizzlecrank-s-shredder.text:
Wizzlecrank's Shredder. In Sludge Fen, Pilot Wizzlecrank waits inside the stolen machine, trapped among Venture Company operators. Without its key, the shredder cannot move, and its engine must be started before he can try to escape. Deep in Sludge Fen, Pilot Wizzlecrank waits inside a motionless shredder. Hostile Venture Company mercenaries surround the machine in the polluted basin. He climbed aboard to steal it, then learned a key was needed to unlock its movement column.

When another operator asked if all was well, Wizzlecrank panicked and blamed a mechanical problem. Now he remains sealed inside, with guards and overseers nearby. He hopes someone will fetch the key before the Venture Company grows suspicious.

npc:wrenix-the-wretched.text: Wrenix the Wretched. In Ratchet, Wrenix the Wretched works beside his strange apparatus, helping crack tough locks. The goblin tinker offers tools for opening secure caches. Wrenix the Wretched works beside his machinery in Ratchet, the goblin port on the Barrens coast. A tinker of the Steamwheedle Cartel, he knows mechanisms and contraptions. He can bypass locks and salvage what lies beyond them. Rogues and scouts working the coast can turn to him for help. Wrenix keeps his gizmotronic apparatus close at hand. With it and his mechanical skill, he supplies thieves' tools and lock-picking instruments. Those seeking to recover stolen Southsea pirate contraband along the Merchant Coast can put the tools to use.

npc:wynne-larson.text: Wynne Larson. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Wynne Larson supplies robes to mages across the kingdom. Since Dalaran and Quel'Thalas fell in the Third War, she relies on local craftsmen and points spellcasters toward rare materials for enchanted garments. Before the Third War, Dalaran and Quel'Thalas supplied the finest woven fabrics and enchanted vestments. Their destruction crippled the old trade routes and arcane textile making. Now Wynne Larson works with local tailors and enchanters such as Lucan Cordell in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. Together, they meet the city's growing need for robes and spellwoven gear. Novice and journeyman mages come to Wynne's shop for arcane garments. She knows what materials are needed for vestments such as Manaweave Robes and Astral Knot Garments. To find them, she sends spellcasters into dangerous places to recover rare reagents like pristine spider silk. Her work helps keep Stormwind's mages outfitted despite shortages from the north.

npc:xavathras.text: Xavathras. Among the ruins at Constellas, Xavathras directs the Jadefire satyrs' work. He serves Xavaric and corrupts an ancient moonwell in Felwood. At the Ruins of Constellas in Felwood, Xavathras commands the Jadefire satyrs. Their tents stand among old elven stonework, beside a moonwell he seeks to defile for Xavaric, another satyr. Xavathras poisons its pure waters with demonic energy, deepening the corruption gripping the forest. Night elves such as Eridan Bluewind seek his death, for his work threatens any effort to restore the woodland.

npc:yeh-kinya.text: Yeh'kinya. At Steamwheedle Port, Yeh'kinya sends travelers in search of lost troll relics. The jungle troll scholar says he seeks ancient lore and artifacts to understand dark powers. Among Steamwheedle Port's goblins and dockworkers, Yeh'kinya studies history and spirits. He sends travelers across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms in search of rare magical items. Some are ancient eggs in the Hinterlands. Others are stone prophecy tablets buried in Zul'Farrak. Yeh'kinya says this work serves the peaceful study of ancient troll history, though his focus on the blood god Hakkar draws suspicion.

npc:yvette-farthing.text: Yvette Farthing. In Brill, Yvette Farthing shares the Gallows' End Tavern with her father, Coleman. She remembers a love that ended when the Scourge came to Lordaeron. Before the Third War, Yvette loved Thurman Agamand, heir to the prosperous Agamand Mills. When the Scourge plague drew near, she and her father, Coleman, begged Thurman to leave the estate. He refused, bound to his family's legacy. Yvette and Thurman both died and rose into undeath. Yvette found a place among the free-willed Forsaken in Brill, but she did not know what had become of Thurman.

npc:zaldimar-wefhellt.text: Zaldimar Wefhellt. Upstairs at the Lion's Pride Inn, Zaldimar Wefhellt guides young mages through their first spells. When they outgrow his lessons, he sends them to Stormwind City for further training. Upstairs at the Lion's Pride Inn, Zaldimar Wefhellt teaches novice mages the first arts of arcane, fire, and frost. Once an apprentice outgrows those lessons, he sends them north to Stormwind's Mage Quarter. There, Jennea Cannon can teach them more.

npc:zamja.text: Zamja. In Orgrimmar’s Drag, Zamja teaches Horde travelers to cook. The Darkspear troll shows cooks how to make meals from Kalimdor’s beasts. Zamja cuts meat and teaches Horde travelers to cook in the Drag. In Durotar and the Barrens, cooking turns raw game into rations for the rugged road. Cooks who have mastered the basic recipes can seek further training in Gadgetzan, to the south.

npc:zangen-stonehoof.text: Zangen Stonehoof. At the High Rise bonfire, Zangen Stonehoof keeps the flames alive and aids tauren kin across Kalimdor. Each evening, the central fire burns in Thunder Bluff. Zangen Stonehoof tends the communal bonfire atop Thunder Bluff's High Rise. Each evening, as twilight falls over Mulgore, he lights the fire above the city's highest bluffs. Its flames warm the tribes gathered beneath High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. Zangen also aids allies beyond Mulgore's mesa with spiritual and ritual work across the continent. Zangen helps Rau Cliffrunner, stationed south in Thousand Needles. When Rau needed water from a night elf moonwell for sacred rituals, Zangen called on dependable Horde adventurers to cross Ashenvale's contested forests. They filled a phial in the ancient groves and sent it south to Freewind Post. Through such aid, Zangen helps preserve ancient rites and support scattered tauren posts.

npc:zankaja.text: Zankaja. In Orgrimmar, young Zankaja waits anxiously for word of her mate, Dogran. He serves at the Crossroads, along the dangerous frontier of the Barrens. In Orgrimmar, Zankaja waits for news of Dogran, her mate. After earning a promotion, he went south to strengthen the Crossroads outpost in the Barrens. The assignment honors a warrior, but the frontier is harsh. Quilboar, centaur, and aggressive beasts threaten those who serve there. When Dogran failed to send word or return as expected, Zankaja began asking travelers to seek news of him.

npc:zardeth-of-the-black-claw.text: Zardeth of the Black Claw. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Zardeth of the Black Claw guards a hidden warlock cabal. He lives in chambers beneath the Slaughtered Lamb and passes as an ordinary patron. When curious nobles look too closely, he ends their inquiries for good. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb, tunnels shelter those who practice darker arts. Above them, the Mage Quarter's spires study arcane discipline in the open. Zardeth of the Black Claw works in the crypts and guards warlocks hiding beneath the city guard's nose. The Alliance condemns fel magic, so the cabal keeps its presence secret and removes threats before royal investigators arrive.

npc:zargh.text: Zargh. At the Crossroads, Zargh provisions travelers bound for the Barrens wilds and sends choice cuts to Orgrimmar. At the Crossroads, Zargh sells cured meat, shank, and game from the surrounding plains. Travelers setting out into the wilderness can stock up at his shop. He also sends choice cuts across Durotar to Innkeeper Gryshka in the Valley of Strength in Orgrimmar.

npc:zarlman-two-moons.text: Zarlman Two-Moons. In central Mulgore, Zarlman Two-Moons guides the spiritual life of Bloodhoof Village. Baine Bloodhoof tends its daily affairs, while Zarlman communes with the spirits and guides young tauren through the Rite of Vision. Zarlman Two-Moons tends the spirits while Baine Bloodhoof commands Bloodhoof Village's defenses and daily affairs. The village turns to Zarlman to keep harmony with the spirit world. He joins the struggles of the plains to the voices of ancestors, honoring the Earth Mother and ancestral wisdom. Zarlman guides maturing tauren through the Rite of Vision, a traditional trial each must undertake. He teaches initiates to prepare sacred draughts and heed ancestral portents. Young hunters, shamans, and warriors seek their destined path and spirit guides through the rite. Zarlman teaches that strength on the plains means little without spiritual clarity.

npc:zarrin.text: Zarrin. Behind Dolanaar's inn, Zarrin teaches young night elves and visitors to cook with Teldrassil's native plants and animals. He tends an open hearth where they learn to prepare meals. Behind Dolanaar's inn, Zarrin tends an open cooking fire and teaches Kaldorei cooking. Teldrassil's native plants and animals feed those who live here. Zarrin shows visitors how to forage and prepare meals at home.

npc:zenn-foulhoof.text: Zenn Foulhoof. East of Dolanaar, Zenn Foulhoof asks travelers for forest reagents, while night elves keep watch.

npc:zevrost.text: Zevrost. In Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow, Zevrost guides Horde initiates through fel magic. He teaches summoning rites and the handling of dark artifacts. Beneath Orgrimmar, the Cleft of Shadow is where Zevrost mentors warlocks in Thrall’s capital. Orcs remember the demonic corruption of their past, so fel practitioners work under strict watch. Zevrost teaches them the discipline to command demons without yielding to corruption. He says fel ruins only those who lack inner strength. Zevrost guides warlocks beyond spells and curses toward greater dark undertakings. Initiates seeking implements such as the Orb of Orahil or the means to summon a fiery Felsteed often come through his hands. For further study, he sends ambitious practitioners to other masters, including Menara Voidrender in the Barrens. There they can push their command of shadow magic to its limits.

npc:zjolnir.text:
Zjolnir. In Sen'jin Village, Zjolnir raises raptors for Darkspear riders and trusted Horde champions. These trained mounts carry deep cultural pride for troll riders. Near Sen'jin Village, Zjolnir tends the pens where he raises the fierce raptors favored by the Darkspear. Their wild nature calls for an expert hand before they can be raised and saddled for war.

He gives these prized mounts freely to fellow trolls who have learned the riding arts. Other Horde members must first earn exalted trust with the Darkspear tribe before he will entrust them with a raptor.

npc:zor-lonetree.text:
Zor Lonetree. At Grommash Hold, Zor Lonetree weighs the Horde’s concerns beyond Durotar. His grasp of Alliance politics helps the court judge affairs across Kalimdor. From Grommash Hold, Zor Lonetree watches beyond Durotar. He advises the Horde’s high leadership and understands human and Alliance politics with unusual care. When foreign curiosities reach Orgrimmar, he studies them. When trouble stirs among the land’s spirits, he directs travelers toward it.

His work keeps the warchief’s court informed on political and spiritual matters. Zor Lonetree has examined noble jewelry recovered from human settlements. He has also followed disturbances among the spirits of the Stonetalon Mountains.

npc:zureetha-fargaze.text: Zureetha Fargaze. In the Valley of Trials, Zureetha Fargaze watches for threats to young Horde recruits. Alongside Foreman Thazz'ril, she sends them to uncover and root out the Burning Blade cult hidden in Durotar. Zureetha Fargaze watches for dangers beyond the work and discipline Foreman Thazz'ril oversees. The Burning Blade cult has entered the Valley of Trials in secret. It has corrupted lesser demons and gathered strength in the nearby Burning Blade Coven. She sends untested adventurers to recover medallions from cultists, confirm the danger and disrupt the cult's early efforts. Then she directs seasoned recruits farther into Durotar.

topic:agamaggan.text:
Agamaggan. In the War of the Ancients, Agamaggan gave his life against the Burning Legion. His blood and fallen body gave rise to the Razorfen, now home to the quilboar. Ten thousand years ago, Agamaggan joined the fight against the Burning Legion. The mighty demigod charged with terrifying force, yet fell in the War of the Ancients. His sacrifice helped save Azeroth from ruin. Agamaggan fell in the southern Barrens, and his body changed the land. His blood soaked the soil, and thorny vines rose from the dry earth to form the Razorfen. The quilboar hold this ground sacred. They see Razorfen Kraul as his resting body and Razorfen Downs as his gaping skull.

Across the Barrens, crystallized Blood Shards are believed to be remnants of his spilled blood. Quilboar geomancers and shamans draw power from the lingering primal energy within them. The quilboar revere Agamaggan as their divine forefather. To them, the surrounding brambles are the living armor their creator left to shelter them from hostile neighbors. They believe his spirit watches over them, lending vigor to their warriors and earth magic to their geomancers.

They defend the thorns against tauren, orcs, and centaur. They believe it is their sacred duty to guard the fallen body of the boar god who birthed them.

topic:alliance.text:
Alliance. Across Azeroth, the Alliance now gathers its peoples around Stormwind. Its roots lie in Lordaeron's ruin, and its heart is Stormwind City, beside Ironforge's dwarves, the exiled gnomes, and Kalimdor's night elves. The modern Alliance descends from the Alliance of Lordaeron. During the Second War, Sir Anduin Lothar led Stormwind refugees north and united the Seven Kingdoms, dwarves, and high elves against the Old Horde.

The Scourge and the Third War ravaged the north. Lordaeron lay in ruins, and survivors were driven into scattered resistance. The restored Kingdom of Stormwind filled the void. Today it is the foremost seat of human leadership, carrying honor and faith into a fractured world. In the Eastern Kingdoms, the Alliance rests on the steadfast bond between humans and the dwarves of Ironforge, ruled by King Magni Bronzebeard. Gnomes also live among the dwarves, driven from Gnomeregan by a devastating trogg uprising.

High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque guides the exiled gnomes. They bring their brilliant engineering to the Alliance war effort, believing the coalition must survive if they are ever to reclaim their irradiated home. Across the Great Sea, the reclusive night elves left millennia of isolation after the Battle of Mount Hyjal. They lost their immortality and now clash bitterly with the Horde over logging in Ashenvale. So the kaldorei allied with their newfound mortal companions.

Cultural friction remains. Some traditionalists condemn the presence of humans and dwarves in ancient forests. The Alliance offers vital military and diplomatic help to guard Kalimdor from demonic remnants and Horde expansion. The Alliance faces strains within its own ranks. King Varian Wrynn vanished under mysterious circumstances while traveling to a diplomatic summit. His young son Anduin took the throne under Highlord Bolvar Fordragon's regency.

Relations with former human allies have also frayed. The maritime kingdom of Kul Tiras keeps its distance, while Sylvanas Windrunner's undead Forsaken hold the ruins of Lordaeron.

topic:brotherhood-of-northshire.text:
Brotherhood of Northshire. At Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest, the Brotherhood of Northshire guides the faithful and trains new defenders. Once called the Clerics of Northshire, the order was rebuilt after its losses in the First War. Centuries ago, missionaries from Lordaeron traveled south and founded Northshire Abbey in Stormwind. They served its people through the Holy Light and sought to soothe the realm. First called the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics, they showed compassion even to injured gnolls and jungle trolls during past border wars.

When the Orcish Horde crossed the Dark Portal, the clerics went unarmed and without armor to heal fallen soldiers. Their healing sustained the Stormwind Army, so the orcs made them targets. The order was decimated, and the abbey was ransacked and burned. The surviving clerics fled north across the sea to Southshore with Sir Anduin Lothar. The slaughter of Northshire’s clerics shook the human kingdoms. Archbishop Alonsus Faol saw that faith alone could not withstand an axe without armor and martial discipline. He joined surviving clerics with devout knights to form the Knights of the Silver Hand. These warriors bore the Light’s sacred power and a knight’s skill in battle. Northshire’s fallen healers laid the foundation for the holy warriors who broke the Horde in the Second War. After Stormwind was reclaimed and the Dark Portal destroyed, Archbishop Faol rebuilt Northshire Abbey and reorganized the order as the Brotherhood of Northshire. Today, the abbey is a quiet place where new recruits begin their service to the realm. Priestess Anetta, Brother Sammuel, and Brother Paxton help tend the valley’s spiritual needs, preserve ancient texts in the library, and train defenders against brigands, wolves, and the gathering shadows across Elwynn Forest.

topic:centaur.text: Centaur. Centaur clans still roam central Kalimdor, where they once drove the tauren close to extinction. Their line began with Zaetar and Theradras, and the Horde's arrival changed the course of their war with the tauren. Centaur legend begins in Maraudon, beneath Desolace. Zaetar was an immortal son of the demigod Cenarius. Princess Theradras was daughter of Therazane, the elemental lord. Together they sired the first centaur. Soon after they emerged, the barbaric offspring turned on Zaetar and killed him. Grief-stricken, Theradras trapped his spirit in Maraudon's winding caverns. She shielded her vicious children as they multiplied across Kalimdor. From Desolace, centaur spread across Kalimdor and waged brutal war against its native peoples. The nomadic tauren suffered most. Driven from their fertile ancestral home in Mulgore, they fled across the Barrens as centaur warbands burned their settlements and hunted them for sport. By the Third War, centuries of pursuit had brought the tauren near extinction. They fled the endless marauders across the savannah. The balance shifted when Warchief Thrall and the newly arrived orcish Horde landed on Kalimdor. Thrall made a pact with Cairne Bloodhoof. Orcish steel joined with tauren might, and together they crushed the aggressive Kolkar warbands and broke their hold on the plains. The tauren could safely establish Thunder Bluff and reclaim Mulgore. Their exile ended, and a debt of blood and honor bound them to the Horde. Centaur remain a threat across central Kalimdor despite their defeats. Their society is divided among warring clans, chiefly the Kolkar, Gelkis, Magram, and Maraudine. Each follows a khan, and the clans feud over territory and water. Their infighting keeps them from uniting. Yet raiding parties still strike trade caravans and settlements across Durotar, the Barrens, Thousand Needles, and the borders of Mulgore.

topic:defias-brotherhood.text: Defias Brotherhood. Across Stormwind’s southern lands, the Defias Brotherhood wages war on the kingdom. Bandits, brigands, and assassins terrorize the farmlands. From a hidden redoubt, they seek to overthrow the corrupt House of Nobles and lay waste to Stormwind.

topic:druid.text: Druid. Across Kalimdor, Druid protect the wild and heal the wounded with nature’s power. They draw on wild spirits, the celestial bodies, and the Emerald Dream, and take beast forms to defend the land. Night elves have followed this path for ages, tauren have renewed it, and the Skyborne keep their own traditions. Druidism binds its followers to nature and to the demigod Cenarius. Druids call up roots to hold their foes, draw power from the moon and stars, and use healing plants to mend bone and flesh. Their charge is to preserve the world’s balance and guard the wild from corruption and exploitation. Shapeshifting is the druid’s mark. Through spiritual devotion, druids channel the primal nature of Azeroth’s beasts. They take a bear’s thick hide to endure attacks, become lithe feline hunters to strike from shadow, or assume aquatic and avian forms to cross sea and sky. In animal form, their mouths rarely shape mortal words, yet their strength rivals the wild’s fiercest predators. Cenarius taught Malfurion Stormrage the druidic arts ten thousand years ago. Later, the Cenarion Circle gave mortal druidism its order. From sacred Moonglade, it watches over druids across Kalimdor, apart from mortal factions and political disputes. For ages, only night elf men belonged, spending centuries in the Emerald Dream. After the Third War, night elf women and tauren joined them. The Skyborne learned druidism long ago. When common folk joined the Shal'nan's rebellion against Prince Tortheldrin in Eldre'Thalas, they took up nature magic, influenced by the Cenarion Circle to the north. Tortheldrin scorned the practice as beneath the Highborne. Their descendants still follow that path: the Nightclaw Druids of Shadowgale Forest on Zephras Isle remain largely apart from other Skyborne factions.

topic:druids-of-the-fang.text: Druids of the Fang. In the Wailing Caverns, the Druids of the Fang pursue their design. These rogue night elves severed ties with the Cenarion Circle and took serpent forms under Lord Serpentis. Their true origin remains a mystery to outsiders. They seek to seize the underground waters and remake the Barrens as their own paradise. Naralex led young druids into the Wailing Caverns to restore the Barrens. The land had once been a lush sanctuary, and he hoped to bring it back. Beneath the caverns, they reached natural fissures and springs. Naralex entered an induced slumber to channel the living energies of the Emerald Dream into those waters. He hoped to revive the scorched savannah above.

topic:dwarf.text:
Dwarf. In Khaz Modan, dwarves keep to the mountain homes they carved from stone. Once earthen, they changed under the Curse of Flesh and now live across Khaz Modan and beyond. King Magni Bronzebeard rules from Ironforge, beneath the peaks of Dun Morogh, a steadfast heart of the Alliance. Dwarves began as earthen, beings forged by the titans who slept for ages in Uldaman's vaults. The Curse of Flesh changed them into creatures of blood and bone. They took the name dwarves and made their home in Khaz Modan, named for the titan Khaz'goroth. Beneath Dun Morogh's peaks, they carved the stronghold of Ironforge.

Their bodies endure hardship, and their keen eyes find stone and ore. They bring fierce resolve to the forge and to battle. Their halls ring with roaring hearths, and ale is a favored drink. After High King Modimus Anvilmar died, the dwarves fought over Ironforge. The Bronzebeard, Wildhammer, and Dark Iron clans each sought power, and their struggle became a civil war. The Bronzebeards took the mountain and drove the other clans out.

Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan of the Dark Irons then waged war against both rivals. His forces were driven beneath the Redridge Mountains, where Thaurissan accidentally summoned Ragnaros the Firelord. Flames consumed the Dark Iron realm, leaving the volcanic wastes of Searing Gorge and the Burning Steppes. The survivors became slaves beneath Blackrock Mountain. The Wildhammers, their home devastated, migrated north to Aerie Peak in the Hinterlands. When the Horde swept across the continent in the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard shut Ironforge's gates against its sieges. Dwarven forces fought beside the Alliance of Lordaeron in heavy plate armor and with muskets, while gryphon riders took to the sky. Their courage helped break the Horde.

Ironforge remains one of the Alliance's steadfast defenders. The dwarves have also welcomed their displaced gnome cousins into their halls. Across Khaz Modan, they uncover titan ruins in search of answers about their ancient origins.

topic:earth-mother.text:
Earth Mother. Across Azeroth, the Earth Mother’s presence lives in the land and its elements. Tauren say she shaped the world, raised the sun and moon, and guides their lives and hopes for what follows death. Tauren creation myths say the Earth Mother shaped Azeroth before day and night, making it a haven for her coming children. She scraped her nails across the new mountains, and the first fires sparked. Her hands carved rivers and ocean beds, while her laughter gave breath to the wind. Then she lifted the primordial fogs into the sky. The first rains coaxed grass, forests, and grain from the soil. With help from the friendly elements, the Earth Mother brought forth twins: An'she, the sun, and Mu'sha, the moon. She placed the radiant twins in her eyes, so she could rest while keeping them safe. As she opened and closed each lid, day, night, and the seasons began.

Later, she pressed her heart against the fertile earth and breathed the song of life into the land. There she created the shu'halo, the first tauren. She charged the twins and the elements to teach these young mortals to hunt, build, dance, and live in harmony with the wilds. In time, the Earth Mother set An'she and Mu'sha in the sky to watch over the land by day and night. Tauren say her spirit now dwells in the world's rivers, trees, plains, and mountains. Every lesser nature spirit springs from her and returns to her in the end. Tauren believe the Earth Mother's spirit still cradles Azeroth. Her ear listens to the winds for her children's prayers, and her heart beats within the deep stone. Tauren hunters, shamans, and druids give thanks to her for every kill and harvest. They believe all life begins in her embrace, and every tauren spirit returns to her soil upon death.

topic:elemental-plane.text:
Elemental Plane. Across the Elemental Plane, its wards still hold the elementals—though cracks now let them reach Azeroth. The titans made this realm to imprison Azeroth’s chaotic elementals, dividing it into Skywall, Deepholm, the Abyssal Maw, and the Firelands. Breaches have brought violent incursions and catastrophic summonings into Azeroth. Long ago, the elementals served as lieutenants to the Old Gods. The titans defeated the Old Gods, then banished the elemental lords and their many servants to the Elemental Plane. They divided the realm into four domains: Skywall for air, Deepholm for earth, the Abyssal Maw for water, and the Firelands for fire. With the elementals gone, nature calmed and peace returned to Azeroth’s surface. Captivity did not still the elementals’ fury. Across their divided domains, the primordial powers wage endless war against one another. Strong wards bar the way between Azeroth and the Elemental Plane, but they can break. Two centuries ago, near the desperate end of the War of the Three Hammers, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan pierced the veil and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord from the Firelands. His arrival ruptured the Redridge Mountains and forged Blackrock Mountain.

Now, volatile cracks have opened across Kalimdor. Dimensional rifts keep appearing in Silithus, Un'Goro Crater, Azshara, and Winterspring. Hostile elementals pour through and test the mortal world's defenses.

topic:furbolg.text:
Furbolg. Across northern Kalimdor, Furbolg tribes turn on their old allies as madness takes hold. For millennia, they lived in harmony with nature and the night elves. Now demonic corruption and lingering fel magic leave only a few tribes sane. Furbolg packs once fought beside night elves and tauren against the Burning Legion. During the War of the Ancients, ten thousand years ago, chieftain Unng Ak united the tribes. They had long revered the wild god Ursoc. After the Great Sundering, they withdrew into the northern woodlands. There, they kept peaceful ties with night elf druids and forest wardens, living simply among the wild. The Third War shattered the furbolgs’ quiet life. As the Burning Legion crossed Kalimdor, fel taint spread through the soil and canopy of Ashenvale and Felwood. Deeply attuned to the land, the bear-men took the corruption into themselves, and madness seized their tribes.

Wizened shamans were overthrown or silenced by bloodthirsty firebrands. These new leaders channeled fel moss, dark talismans, and corrupt alchemy. Peaceful gatherers became raiders who attack travelers and night elf settlements on sight. Across northern Kalimdor, nearly every major tribe has fallen. The Gnarlpine dwell across Teldrassil, the Blackwood in Darkshore, and the Thistlefur and Foulweald in Ashenvale. The Deadwood and Winterfall live in the northern highlands. Yet a few still hold to their old ways.

Deep in fortified tunnels linking Felwood, Winterspring, and Moonglade, the Timbermaw guard their sanity. Wary and isolated, they defend their hold against their crazed northern kin. They fight to preserve what remains of their uncorrupted culture.

topic:house-of-nobles.text: House of Nobles. In Stormwind Keep, the House of Nobles holds the kingdom’s lands, taxes, and trade. Their refusal to pay the laborers who rebuilt the city set off bloody riots that shook the realm. Stormwind’s greatest patrician families form the House of Nobles, the Crown’s chief council. They own most arable land in Elwynn, Westfall, and Duskwood, and so hold great sway over trade, regional magistrates, and royal decrees. Boy-king Anduin Wrynn and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon rule Stormwind in name. Yet the council can bind the throne in red tape, stall trials, block executions, and meddle in provincial affairs.

topic:human.text:
Human. Across the Eastern Kingdoms, humans still defend their place among the mortal realms. Their old empire broke into seven kingdoms. Now Stormwind is their strongest realm and the Alliance’s chief human power. Long ago, human tribes wandered apart beneath the threat of the Amani forest trolls. Warlord Thoradin of the Arathi saw that division would bring their end. Through diplomacy and conquest, he united the clans and founded the Empire of Arathor, with its fortress capital at Strom.

During the Troll Wars, the beleaguered high elves of Quel'Thalas allied with Arathor. They taught one hundred humans the arts of arcane magic. Together, humans and high elves broke the troll armies. Arathor secured human rule over the central continents, and the alliance laid the ground for future ties among mortal peoples. As Arathor grew secure and prosperous, its distant settlements became powerful city-states, able to stand alone. In time, the empire split into seven realms: Gilneas, Alterac, Dalaran, Lordaeron, Kul Tiras, Stormwind, and Stromgarde, whose first home was Strom.

These kingdoms traded with dwarves, gnomes, and elves, yet peace remained fragile. Border clashes and claims over land stirred rivalries, including old mountain feuds between Alterac and Stromgarde. Court intrigue added to the strain. The kingdoms stayed divided until disasters beyond their borders forced them to act together. The orcish Horde came through the Dark Portal, forcing humanity’s kingdoms to face a common enemy. Stormwind fell in the First War, and its refugees fled north to warn the other realms. King Terenas Menethil II helped forge the Alliance of Lordaeron, joining humans, dwarves, gnomes, and high elves against the Horde in the Second War.

Stormwind was rebuilt with great effort. Then the Scourge plague ravaged Lordaeron, and Dalaran fell during the Third War. The northern human realms lay in smoking ruin.
