Stormwind is the strongest human kingdom left and the heart of the grand Alliance. King Varian Wrynn vanished while traveling to a diplomatic summit. His ten-year-old son, Anduin Wrynn, was crowned king, with Highlord Bolvar Fordragon as regent.

Northward, Lordaeron’s survivors are scattered or dead. Gilneas remains behind its colossal Greymane Wall, leaving Stormwind to carry the burden of humanity’s defense.

topic:hunter.text:
Hunter. Across Azeroth, hunters follow wild trails with loyal beasts at their sides. Bows, rifles, and crossbows let them strike from afar, while traps and primal aspects help control a fight. They track quarry through forests and over snowbound peaks, relying on their wits and bond with nature. Hunters make their lives among Azeroth’s wild places. They study how beasts move, hunt, and defend themselves, earning respect instead of breaking spirits. With patience, they can tame dangerous creatures, from prowling cats to mountain bears and sharp-eyed raptors. These animals become steadfast allies, ready to defend their companions to the death. Hunters fight from a distance with bows, heavy crossbows, and rifles. Their volleys can pierce heavy armor before an attacker draws near. Keen senses lead them along faint footsteps, scents, and other signs left by their quarry. When enemies close in, frost and flame traps, disorienting ambushes, and quick evasive movements keep foes at bay. The hunter’s path takes many forms across Azeroth. Night elf Sentinels use bows and shadowcraft beneath Ashenvale’s canopy, moving in quiet accord with the wilderness. Dwarven riflemen brave Dun Morogh’s freezing crags with hardy bears and master the craft of gunpowder. Across Kalimdor, Tauren and Orc trackers follow ancient nomadic customs. They pursue prey with sacred respect and call on bestial spirits to guide their shots.

In Elwynn Forest, young humans learn from seasoned trackers such as the dwarf Tordrin Sternblade in Northshire Valley and Josephine Carson in Goldshire. The Skyborne learn to track and tame the beasts of Zephras Isle.

topic:leper-gnome.text:
Leper gnome. Across Azeroth, leper gnomes endure the ruin of Gnomeregan. Most still dwell in the city, changed by its toxic fallout and loyal to Mekgineer Thermaplugg. Troggs broke into Gnomeregan during the Third War. Mekgineer Thermaplugg urged High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque to flood the city with radioactive toxins. He claimed they would kill the troggs and spare the gnomes. Instead, eighty percent of the city's inhabitants died. Survivors sealed in the lower levels were warped in mind and body by the fallout. Their pale, pustulant forms became known as leper gnomes. Mekgineer Thermaplugg also succumbed to the poisonous fallout. His complexion changed, and his sanity failed. He named himself techno-overlord and King of Gnomeregan, then gathered the crazed survivors in the Tinkers' Court. Many now mistake surface dwellers for trogg intruders. They attack returning rescue parties with frantic savagery.

The survivors pilot salvaged mechanical constructs and build volatile ordnance. With fanatical devotion, they guard Thermaplugg's kingdom. Most leper gnomes remain trapped in Gnomeregan's contaminated corridors, though a handful have reached the wider world. Some, driven by desperation or dark ambition, have joined the Dark Iron dwarves in Blackrock Depths. Others operate machinery for the Venture Company in Stonetalon. A few serve as lab assistants to the Forsaken's Royal Apothecary Society in the depths of the Undercity.

topic:lich-king.text:
Lich King. In Icecrown, the Lich King commands the undead Scourge from the frozen throne. Kil'jaeden made him from the spirit of the orc shaman ner'zhul. His power drew Prince Arthas Menethil toward corruption, until the two joined atop Northrend's icy peaks. Ner'zhul fled dying Draenor, but Kil'jaeden seized him. The demon lord tore away his body and bound his tormented soul in diamond-hard ice from the Twisting Nether. That glacial prison struck Northrend's northern wastes and formed the frozen throne.

Kil'jaeden meant the Lich King to forge an unstoppable undead vanguard. It would break the mortal kingdoms without the infighting that had ruined the Orcish Horde. Yet Ner'zhul wielded immense telepathic power, and began at once to plot his freedom. Watching dreadlords guarded Ner'zhul closely, so he acted in secret. Through his mind, he ensnared Kel'Thuzad, an exiled Kirin Tor archmage. Kel'Thuzad founded the Cult of the Damned in Lordaeron, where cauldrons of tainted grain spread the Plague of Undeath through the northern kingdoms.

Prince Arthas Menethil rushed to save his people, but desperation drove him to ruthless acts, including the infamous slaughter of Stratholme. Seeking vengeance against the dreadlord Mal'Ganis, Arthas pursued him to Northrend. There Frostmourne waited to steal his soul and make him the Scourge's foremost death knight. For a time, the Lich King summoned Archimonde and yielded command to the Burning Legion. He expected the demons' hubris. Arthas turned the demon hunter Illidan Stormrage toward the Skull of Gul'dan and Tichondrius's death. That helped bring about Archimonde's ruin at Mount Hyjal.

Afterward, a desperate Kil'jaeden ordered Illidan to destroy the frozen throne. Cracks in the icy spire weakened Ner'zhul's power, and Sylvanas Windrunner and her Forsaken broke free. The Lich King summoned his champion back. Arthas returned to Northrend, defeated Illidan at icecrown's foot, climbed the spire, and shattered the ice. He joined with Ner'zhul as one terrible consciousness.

topic:light.text: Light. Across creation, Light flows through living things, and its power is called upon in Azeroth as Holy magic. Faith and will can turn it to healing, shelter, or a strike against darkness. Across creation, Light flows as living energy. In Azeroth, it takes the form of Holy magic, moving through living souls and binding mortal hearts. Mortals may picture it as a conscious protector. Yet Light answers the absolute conviction of the soul that calls upon it. Channeling Light calls for self-abnegation, disciplined meditation, and unshakable will. Priests of the Church of the Holy Light and holy paladins train for years to become clear vessels for its radiance. Through devotion, Light can mend wounds with restorative warmth and shelter the innocent with brilliant wards. It can also strike demons and the risen undead with searing fire. Humans and dwarves revere Light through formal scripture, while other peoples follow their own spiritual traditions. Night elves devote themselves to Elune and channel sacred moonlight, weaving holy magic to cleanse and protect. Tauren honor the sun deity An'she through their own spiritual traditions.

topic:llane-wrynn-i.text:
Llane Wrynn I. Stormwind's defense falters as the First War turns against King Llane Wrynn I and his kingdom. Beloved and proud, Llane cannot accept that his friend Medivh has betrayed humanity, and that refusal dooms the capital. Born to King Barathen Wrynn, Prince Llane grew up with Anduin Lothar and Medivh. As youths, the three friends ventured into Stranglethorn Vale's jungles and clashed with the Gurubashi trolls. In time, Llane took the throne as Stormwind's king. When green-skinned strangers came from the southern swamps, King Llane sent Lothar to investigate the Black Morass. Minor skirmishes became the First War as the Horde overran the forests of Duskwood, Westfall, and Redridge. Messengers seeking aid from Lordaeron and the northern human kingdoms were turned away. Stormwind's long isolation and aristocratic intrigue weakened their pleas.

Even so, Llane and Lothar led a daring counterattack. They broke the Horde's first siege of Stormwind and dealt the invaders their first major defeat.

topic:mage.text:
Mage. For a mage, arcane power answers to study, while the body remains frail beneath cloth armor. Fire, frost, and raw arcane force make mages formidable allies and dangerous foes. They conjure, teleport, and control the field of battle, but their discipline demands deep focus. Misused arcane power has left a perilous legacy. A mage’s path asks for intellect, focus, and years of study. Magi neither commune with spirits nor rely on divine faith; they approach magic as a precise cosmic science. Drawing on arcane energies, they unleash raw destruction, summon searing flame, or chill air into solid ice and howling blizzards. Heavy armor hinders the delicate gestures and concentration their incantations require, so they wear light cloth. Wards, mana barriers, and evasive spells help keep them safe. Human magical tradition began nearly three millennia ago during the Troll Wars. High elven sorcerers taught one hundred humans of the Empire of Arathor to help turn the tide against the Amani. As more humans took up magic, citizens without such skill grew fearful, driving many magi to found the magocracy of Dalaran.

Governed by the Kirin Tor, Dalaran became the northern kingdoms’ central archive of magical study. There, combat magic took shape in traditions that served the Alliance of Lordaeron through the First and Second Wars. Arcane practitioners have never won easy trust. The ancient cataclysm wrought by the Highborne and Dalaran’s fall during the Third War left many wary of magic’s volatile nature. The Church of the Holy Light has long viewed wizardry with suspicion.

Conservative knights have regarded arcane spellcasters as damned souls or a necessary evil in battle. Yet civil and military leaders know a capable magus can bring battlefield supremacy, swift mass transport, and vital defenses against supernatural threats. The arcane belongs to more than the Alliance. Troll and Forsaken mages serve the Horde, and orcs who study the art begin under Mai'ah, a Darkspear mage in the Valley of Trials. Mai'ah teaches that patience and careful judgment matter more than raw power.

Among the Skyborne, the High Order descends from the Highborne of Eldre'Thalas. Their time in Skywall cost them much of their ancestors’ arcane knowledge. With the wind spirits gone from Zephras Isle, they seek to recover it. Skyborne mages fight for the Alliance.

topic:muradin-bronzebeard.text:
Muradin Bronzebeard. Across Khaz Modan and Lordaeron, Muradin Bronzebeard is honored for his skill in war and diplomacy. Brother to King Magni Bronzebeard and Brann Bronzebeard, he helped found the Explorers' League. In Northrend, he is believed to have died when Prince Arthas Menethil claimed Frostmourne. In the Second War, Muradin carried messages between Khaz Modan's mountain halls and the Alliance of Lordaeron. He helped defend Ironforge during the Horde's siege, then marched with Alliance forces through Blackrock Spire to the Dark Portal.

After peace came, Muradin settled in Capital City as Ironforge's official ambassador. Jovial yet formidable, he became a familiar face in the palace and grew close to King Terenas Menethil. He also taught young Prince Arthas the arts of swordplay and combat. Muradin's curiosity ranged beyond politics and war. With his brothers, he helped found the dwarven Explorers' League, devoted to finding lost titan relics and recording the world's farthest corners. He loved Northrend and often traveled north to sketch ancient buildings and document its fierce inhabitants.

The continent's rugged mysteries drew Muradin on his final expedition. He sought lore and relics there, and followed whispers of a forgotten runeblade.

topic:old-god.text:
Old God. Across Azeroth, the Old Gods’ whispers still poison mortal minds and twist the world. Once they ruled the primordial world, until the Titans bound them beneath the earth. Their influence endures. In Azeroth’s first age, the Old Gods ruled through vast bodies of chaotic flesh, among them C'Thun. They took root in the planet’s crust and commanded elemental armies and insectoid swarms. When the Titans arrived, their armies waged an apocalyptic war against the Old Gods. Rather than destroy them, the Titans bound them in vast prisons beneath the earth. The Old Gods have never truly slept beneath their chains, miles of stone and enchanted wards. Their psychic malice seeps into the world and corrupts the vulnerable. During the War of the Ancients, that malice slowly drove Neltharion the Earth-Warder mad and twisted the noble dragon into Deathwing.

As the Great Sundering’s raging waters swallowed Queen Azshara and her Highborne, an Old God answered their desperation. The Old God transformed them into the serpentine naga.

topic:paladin.text:
Paladin. Paladins stand between the innocent and those who would harm them. They wear heavy plate, mend the wounded and strike down the wicked with arms and the Holy Light. Humans and dwarves bear the Silver Hand's legacy in the Alliance. In the Horde, Forsaken who served the Light in life still answer its call, though it burns them. Archbishop Alonsus Faol formed the paladins during the Second War. After the First War left the pious Clerics of Northshire devastated, he saw that healers alone could not stand against orcish warfare. He gathered virtuous knights of Lordaeron and taught surviving clerics to fight with weapons and divine magic. Under Uther the Lightbringer, the Knights of the Silver Hand defended bodies and renewed spirits across humanity's kingdoms. Priests speak for the Holy Light, preaching faith and tending to common folk's spirits. Paladins take up arms in its name. Their conviction lets them strengthen allies with auras, seal blessings upon them and mend fatal wounds. Against unholy horrors, the Light courses through their blows and burns undead and demonic foes with righteous fury. The fall of Lordaeron in the Third War scattered the original order, but its ideals endure. Humans in the south and dwarves of Ironforge have taken up its mantle. In sanctuaries such as the Cathedral of Light and the Hall of Mysteries, they train and pledge sword and shield to justice. They defend the Alliance against gathering shadows. Some knights of Lordaeron returned from the grave as Forsaken. Those who served the Light in life still keep their vows, and it still answers them, though each prayer sears their dead flesh. Aramis Hammerhand trains the risen paladins in the chapel at Deathknell, while Shari Stilwell continues their instruction in Brill.

Tyr's Watch, an order of Forsaken paladins, holds Bandarion Keep in western Tirisfal. Their path is lonely. They wield the power that burned their people, and Sylvanas Windrunner tolerates the order while watching it closely.

topic:priest.text:
Priest. Across Azeroth, Priest traditions shape belief, mend flesh, and guard souls. Some draw on the radiant power of faith, while others reach into the terrifying depths of the Void. Their paths range from the Church of the Holy Light to the Sisterhood of the Moon Goddess and shadowy Forsaken cults. Priests guide the spiritual lives of their communities. While warriors test their strength with steel, priests draw power from conviction. Their divine connection can soothe grievous wounds, lift fallen companions from death's threshold, and weave mystic barriers against harm. On the field, their presence can mean the difference between survival and annihilation. The priesthood does not serve only benevolent ends. Life holds both light and darkness, and priests walk a perilous line between healing and devastation of the mind. Those who master the holy arts call down searing righteous vengeance upon their enemies. Practitioners of Shadow magic delve into the Void to dominate minds, twist willpower, and inflict agonizing pain from afar. No single faith guides every priest in Azeroth. Among humans, dwarves and gnomes, the Church of the Holy Light teaches a philosophy of virtue. After the First War, it shaped its fragile Clerics of Northshire into a hardened order.

In Kalimdor, the night elven Sisterhood of Elune honors the Mother Moon with starlight and grace, while troll witch doctors beseech the primal Loa. Among the newly risen Forsaken, many have turned from former dogmas to the Cult of the Forgotten Shadow. Its followers preach that darkness and light must exist in delicate equilibrium.

topic:rogue.text: Rogue. Across Azeroth, Rogues choose when to face danger and when to slip away unseen. Light leather, paired blades, and brewed toxins let them strike before foes can react. They serve as scouts, assassins, pickpockets, and agents of factions and hidden syndicates. Rogues favor quiet, quick attacks over the open clashes of frontline warriors. In light leather, they stalk their quarry unseen. When an opening comes, they strike with precision at vital organs or exposed joints. A swift chain of blows weakens an enemy, and a finishing strike can end the fight. A blade alone rarely serves a cutpurse or killer. Rogues brew venoms to numb limbs, slow an escape, or drain a target's strength. Lockpicks, thrown weapons, and tricks that draw attention elsewhere help them slip past guarded walls, disarm traps, and enter vaults that would confound a company of soldiers. Many rogues work alone as highwaymen or street thugs. The finest join intelligence networks and assassin guilds. Stormwind relies on SI:7, while the Forsaken rely on the relentless Deathstalkers. In Orgrimmar, remnants of the Shattered Hand serve the Warchief. The neutral League of Assassins answers to Lord Jorach Ravenholdt.

topic:scarlet-crusade.text:
Scarlet Crusade. Across Tirisfal Glades and the Plaguelands, crimson banners mark the Scarlet Crusade's war on the undead. The crusaders rose from the broken Knights of the Silver Hand to reclaim Lordaeron. Paranoia blinds them to anyone beyond their ranks, whom they brand plague carriers and shoot on sight. After Prince Arthas betrayed Lordaeron and murdered King Terenas Menethil II, the Order of the Silver Hand broke apart. Surviving paladins and priests rallied around leaders such as Alexandros Mograine, saidan dathrohan, and General Abbendis.

They gathered at Hearthglen and Tyr's Hand to reclaim their ruined homeland, then swore to burn away the undead scourge with holy fire. As the war dragged on, tragedy and suspicion took hold. Their desperate resistance hardened into an unyielding, xenophobic crusade. As the Crusade's teachings hardened into madness, moderate commanders recoiled. Lord Maxwell Tyrosus and his followers argued that reclaiming the north required allies across Azeroth, and sought aid from dwarves, gnomes, and night elves. The zealots refused, so Tyrosus and other disillusioned knights left to form the Argent Dawn, devoted to the Holy Light's pure and inclusive tenets.

The Scarlet Crusade made the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades its center of power. There, they slaughter travelers and refugees, convinced that all who walk the Plaguelands carry the Scourge's contagion.

topic:shadow-council.text: Shadow Council. Across Draenor and Azeroth, the Shadow Council served Gul'dan's designs. At the Burning Legion's direction, the secret cabal of warlocks and necrolytes manipulated the clans and drove the Old Horde's invasion. Orgrim Doomhammer later purged its stronghold in Blackrock Mountain. Before the Horde crossed into Azeroth, Gul'dan gathered warlocks, necrolytes, and chieftains who sought their own advantage. The Shadow Council ruled the orcish clans from the shadows and raised Blackhand the Destroyer as a figurehead. Across Draenor, its members spread fel magic. They gave the clans the blood of the demon Mannoroth and bound the orcs to the Burning Legion. The Shadow Council struck a pact with Medivh, the Guardian possessed by Sargeras, to break the barrier between worlds. Through the Dark Portal, its members guided the Horde into the Kingdom of Stormwind. The warlocks watched over the war from their sanctum in Blackrock Spire.

topic:shaman.text:
Shaman. Among the Horde and the dwarves, Shaman seek aid from earth, air, fire and water. Totems help them wield lightning and ancestral healing as they guide their people. Dwarves follow the path too, as the Wildhammer have long done, and the Skyborne Windshapers seek to restore their people's bond with the winds. Shaman petition the primal forces of nature. Earth, air, fire and water are chaotic, locked in constant conflict. Shaman do not enslave them; they ask for aid and try to keep the elements' fury in balance with the mortal world. Wooden and stone totems planted in the soil help them channel these bargains. Through the totems, shaman protect allies, hinder foes and use cleansing water to mend the wounded. Shamanism once formed the ancient foundation of orcish clan life on Draenor. Kil'jaeden and the Shadow Council deceived the shamans into war against the draenei, and the elemental spirits withdrew their favor. Stripped of their gifts, many shamans fell to demonic corruption and became warlocks. The tradition came close to extinction.

After the Second War, Thrall rediscovered the ancient rites under the guidance of Drek'Thar of the Frostwolf clan. As Warchief, Thrall revived shamanism and made it the moral compass of the New Horde. Across Kalimdor, the Horde's allied peoples keep different shamanic traditions. Tauren mystics hold communion with the earth and spirits, a sacred anchor of their culture. Darkspear trolls honor the loa and ancestral wild spirits, blending voodoo with nature rites. Across tribal lines, shaman serve as community elders and advisers. They also defend their people on the front lines. The shaman's path reaches beyond the Horde. Wildhammer dwarves of Aerie Peak have long called on storm and stone. Earthseer Farsen brings their far-seeing craft to Dun Morogh, while dwarves of Ironforge also take up the totem and fight for the Alliance.

High above the world, the Windshapers lead the Skyborne in spiritual matters. The wind spirits of Zephras Isle have fallen silent, so the Windshapers train new shaman in hope of restoring that lost bond. Skyborne who join the Horde follow their path.

topic:shan-do.text: Shan'do. Among the night elves, Shan'do is spoken with deep respect for a mentor and guide. The Darnassian title means “honored teacher” or “honored instructor,” while thero'shan honors a student. In Darnassian, shan'do means “honored teacher” or “honored instructor.” Calling an elder or mentor shan'do shows humility, filial devotion, and lasting respect for their guidance. The Cenarion Circle's history is bound to the title. Before the War of the Ancients, the demigod Cenarius taught Malfurion Stormrage the ways of nature as his shan'do. Malfurion then guided generations of mortal druids. Across Kalimdor, night elves, forest keepers, and reverent allies commonly address him as Shan'do Stormrage. Cenarion druids often use the title for mentors such as Naralex or the slumbering Malfurion. Yet shan'do belongs to the Darnassian language and reaches beyond religious life. It marks the bond between master and pupil, whatever their school of thought.

topic:stonemasons-guild.text: Stonemasons Guild. Stormwind's rebuilding ended in a bitter dispute between the Stonemasons Guild and the House of Nobles. Deadly riots followed, and the guild was dissolved. Its members went into exile, and the scattered artisans' fate remains a mystery. Edwin VanCleef led the Stonemasons Guild as its elected Guildmaster. Its masons matched the skill of the dwarven Royal Stonecutters Union. After the First and Second Wars left Stormwind in ruins, the House of Nobles hired them to rebuild the city and restore the capital to its ancient grandeur. For years, VanCleef and his craftsmen worked across Elwynn. They raised Stormwind Keep's soaring spires and the Cathedral of Light's great arches. Then royal finances collapsed under debts from military campaigns in the south. Guided by aristocratic politics, the House of Nobles refused to pay the agreed salaries and fees. When VanCleef sought restitution, the nobles disbanded the guild without its consent. Fury spread among the laborers who had bled to rebuild the city.

topic:stormwind-kingdom.text:
Stormwind (kingdom). In the years after Lordaeron fell, Stormwind is the Alliance's foremost power and humanity's greatest remaining bastion. Its southern lands include Elwynn Forest, Westfall, Duskwood, and the Redridge Mountains. Sacked in the First War and rebuilt after the Second, the kingdom now has a ten-year-old king, Anduin Wrynn, while Highlord Bolvar Fordragon guides its affairs amid troubles at home and beyond its borders. Stormwind began more than a thousand years ago, founded by descendants of the ancient Arathi empire. They traveled south beyond the crags of Khaz Modan into fertile, forested valleys. Far from the northern kingdoms, Stormwind grew proud of its self-reliance and its faith in the Light. The Orcish Horde came through the Dark Portal, and Stormwind's independence neared its end. In the First War, Stormwind City burned to ash and King Llane was slain. Sir Anduin Lothar led the survivors north across the Great Sea, where he rallied the northern realms into the Alliance of Lordaeron.

After the Orcish threat was crushed in the Second War, refugees returned. They hired the Stonemasons Guild to rebuild their capital with white stone and blue banners. Then the Scourge wiped out Lordaeron during the Third War, leaving Stormwind humanity's greatest remaining bastion.

topic:syndicate.text:
Syndicate. Across northern Lordaeron, the Syndicate holds strongholds and fights to reclaim Alterac. Dispossessed nobles lead this human criminal organization against both the Alliance and the Horde, seeking to restore their lost aristocracy. After King Aiden Perenolde's treachery during the Second War, the kingdom of Alterac collapsed in dishonor. Its aristocracy lost its lands and titles, but the surviving nobles refused to accept exile. They gathered under the late king's son, Prince Aliden Perenolde, and forged the Syndicate.

They marked themselves with orange bandanas and filled their ranks with hired thugs, highwaymen, and hedge wizards. To outsiders, they are brigands who raid caravans, ambush travelers, and extort people. Yet their crimes exist only to fund an organized bid to reclaim their ancestral lands and subjugate the surrounding regions. Across northern Lordaeron, the Syndicate holds fortified ground. In the snowy Alterac Mountains, they fortified the ruined town of Strahnbrad and set camps in the Uplands and Dandred's Fold. Farther south, they hold the crumbling Durnholde Keep in the Hillsbrad Foothills. From there, they harass Southshore and raid supply routes.

Farther east, beyond Thoradin's Wall, Lord Falconcrest commands an occupying Syndicate army in the historic ruins of Stromgarde Keep. There, they battle the battered Stromgarde Militia for control of the Arathi Highlands. The Syndicate's ambitions reach beyond ordinary outlawry, earning them the hatred of nearly every regional faction. They call the Alliance their mortal enemy, believing it stole their rightful heritage. Their attacks often target Southshore officials such as Magistrate Henry Maleb.

Toward the Horde, their scorn is open. Following Aedelas Blackmoore's philosophy, they see orcs as beasts fit for slave labor and seek to restore the internment camps. Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken execute captured Syndicate members on sight. Ravenholdt's clandestine thieves' guild wages a shadow war against Syndicate operatives it considers sloppy and arrogant.

topic:varian-wrynn.text:
Varian Wrynn. Across the Great Sea, Varian Wrynn has vanished on the voyage to Theramore. His ten-year-old son Anduin wears Stormwind's crown under the guidance of Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and Lady Katrana Prestor. Varian's boyhood ended when the First War shattered his life. He watched Garona Halforcen, the assassin, kill King Llane Wrynn as the Old Horde stormed the capital. Anduin Lothar rescued the orphaned prince and fled north with the kingdom's survivors to Southshore.

In Capital City, King Terenas Menethil II took Varian in like a second son. The young prince grew up in exile beside Prince Arthas Menethil, carrying the memory of his burned home. Then the Alliance of Lordaeron broke the Horde and reclaimed Stormwind. At eighteen, Varian took the crown and faced the immense task of rebuilding his ruined kingdom. He hired Edwin VanCleef and the Stonemasons Guild to restore the capital. When the great work was done, the corrupt House of Nobles refused to pay the promised wages.

The stonemasons would not back down, and Varian could not settle the dispute between the entrenched nobility and the furious artisans. Soon, violence filled Stormwind's streets.

topic:war-of-the-ancients.text:
War of the Ancients. As Queen Azshara and her Highborne opened the Well of Eternity, the Burning Legion entered Azeroth. Malfurion Stormrage, Illidan, and Tyrande Whisperwind led the resistance that drove the demons back. The Well's destruction brought the Great Sundering, breaking ancient Kalimdor and changing the world. At the height of the ancient Kaldorei Empire, Queen Azshara and her Highborne sorcerers drew deeply on the Well of Eternity's arcane power. Their spells reached into the Great Dark Beyond and caught the notice of Sargeras, master of the Burning Legion. He promised power and perfection. Then Azshara and her advisor Xavius opened a rift within the Well.

FelHounds, felguard, doomguard, and monstrous commanders poured into Zin-Azshari. They slaughtered those who were not Highborne and began a crusade to purge the world of life. Night elves beyond the Highborne caste rose against the slaughter. Three remarkable leaders gathered the resistance: Malfurion Stormrage, the first mortal druid; Tyrande Whisperwind, a devoted priestess of Elune; and Illidan, Malfurion's gifted brother. Together, they brought common night elves to a desperate frontline against the Legion's onslaught. The war grew to world-shattering proportions when Cenarius rallied the ancient Wild Gods and dragonflights to the fight. To keep Sargeras from setting foot on Azeroth, Malfurion and the resistance tried to collapse the portal over the Well of Eternity. Their desperate gambit cast the demonic host back into the Twisting Nether, but the strain proved too great.

The Well violently imploded and triggered the Great Sundering. Kalimdor broke into separate continents, the world's center flooded to form the Great Sea, and Kaldorei culture changed forever.

topic:warlock.text:
Warlock. Across Azeroth, Warlocks wield forbidden powers that bring fear and distrust. They command demons and cast curses, fire, and shadow magic. Some turn these arts against the Burning Legion and its servants. Where ordinary spellcasters see ruin, warlocks see a path to victory. They strike from afar with shadow and fire, and drain the vital essence and souls of their enemies to fuel their fiercest rites. Brimstone falls from the sky, and agonizing curses break the mind.

Warlocks wear simple cloth and have little strength to withstand a blow. They call horrors to meet danger and sacrifice demonic thralls to preserve their own lives. A warlock's hold over the Twisting Nether begins with small bargains and grows into iron dominion. Novices command mischievous imps to hurl flame. With deeper knowledge of fel magic, they bind voidwalkers from shadowy depths to bear physical punishment, succubi who beguile enemy minds, and ravenous felhunters that devour magical energy.

Each summon demands dangerous focus. The Nether's denizens are ever testing their masters for weakness. Orcish demonology began on Draenor, where Kil'jaeden, a demon lord, tempted Gul'dan with the promise of supreme power. Gul'dan founded the secretive Shadow Council and turned many shaman into masters of fel magic. Demonic magic withered Draenor's fertile plains into a barren red wasteland, and the Old Horde invaded through the Dark Portal.

Among humans, the Kirin Tor forbade demonology and hunted illicit summonings. Yet ambitious mages still fell to the lure of untamed sorcery. Warlocks now walk a narrow path between usefulness and execution. In Stormwind, they meet in hidden, gloomy tavern basements, away from the Cathedral of Light's watchful eyes. In Orgrimmar, they gather in the shadowed chasms of the Cleft of Shadow, watched by Thrall's shamanistic regime.

Their methods inspire revulsion, yet neither the Alliance nor the Horde can dismiss the edge warlock magic brings to a hostile battlefield.

topic:warrior.text:
Warrior. Across Azeroth, Warriors take their place at the front with steel, discipline, and battle rage. They wear heavy plate and wield many weapons, shielding allies or breaking enemy ranks. Every race and civilization has its Warriors, from city guards and royal champions to wandering mercenaries. Warriors rely on strength, discipline, and skill with weapons, not prayers or spells. Heavy plate helps them hold the front. Some brace behind tall shields, enduring blows and drawing danger away from spellcasters and archers. Others carry two-handed polearms, axes, or greatswords. Some fight with a blade in each hand and cut through enemy ranks. In battle, pain and blood kindle a Warrior's rage. It grows as Warriors strike foes and endure their attacks. Skilled fighters shape that force into crushing blows and sweeping weapon strikes. Their battle cries hearten nearby allies and break enemy morale. Every race on Azeroth has its Warriors. Stormwind fields disciplined knights and footmen, while Ironforge calls on its stout mountain guard. The Horde rallies around orcish blademasters, tauren braves, and Forsaken Deathguards.

Honor, defense of their lands, or the promise of coin can lead Warriors to arms. They form the backbone of every standing army.

topic:warsong-clan.text:
Warsong clan. Across Kalimdor, the Warsong clan cuts timber for the young Horde. Once led by the revered chieftain Grommash Hellscream, the clan endured exile, internment camps, and demonic corruption. Now its Outriders work chiefly in Ashenvale, where they clash ceaselessly with the night elves. On Draenor's open plains, the Warsong earned their name through swift attacks by wolf riders. After the Horde fell, the clan evaded capture while other orcs languished in Alliance internment camps. The Warsong wandered the wilderness and kept to their warlike ways. At last, Thrall united with Hellscream, and together they forged the New Horde. During the Third War, the Warsong reached Kalimdor. Thrall sent Hellscream and his clan into Ashenvale to cut timber and build an outpost. Their intrusion enraged the night elves and the forest demigod Cenarius. Facing slaughter, the Warsong drank once more from Mannoroth's demonic blood and killed Cenarius in a frenzy of fel corruption.

Thrall and his allies purged Hellscream of the curse. Grom then gave his life in a fateful fight that destroyed Mannoroth. His sacrifice broke the demon blood curse forever and secured the Warsong's place in Horde history. Today, the Warsong Outriders carry on Grommash's mission in Ashenvale. From Splintertree Post and logging camps, they cut timber for the young Horde in Durotar's arid wastes. Their presence has brought them into bitter conflict with the night elven Silverwing Sentinels. The Warsong hold Warsong Gulch and keep cutting into the ancient forest despite the endless ambushes.

topic:wildhammer-clan.text:
Wildhammer clan. In the Hinterlands, the Wildhammer clan holds to its freedom among the wooded peaks. Driven from Grim Batol centuries ago, the dwarves made Aerie Peak their home and learned to ride wild gryphons. They remain friends of the Alliance and stand ready to defend its skies. Before the War of the Three Hammers, the Wildhammers lived near Ironforge. When High King Modimus Anvilmar died, civil war followed, and the victorious Bronzebeards claimed the city. Thane Khardros led his clan north and built a hold within Grim Batol. Soon, the defeated Dark Irons laid siege to it.

Khardros slew the sorceress Modgud, but her dying curse blighted the mountain and left its halls uninhabitable. The Wildhammers refused an invitation to return under Bronzebeard rule. They chose their freedom and traveled north to the forests and rocky crags of the Hinterlands. The Wildhammers built Aerie Peak in the highlands of their new home. Unlike their kin beneath the earth, they embraced open skies and living rock, and formed a deep spiritual bond with the native gryphons. In secluded aviaries, they forged enchanted stormhammers and became Azeroth's finest aerial cavalry.

During the Second War, Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer marched toward Quel'Thalas and attacked Aerie Peak. Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar and the Alliance came to the clan's aid. In gratitude, High Thane Kurdran Wildhammer pledged his gryphon riders to the coalition. They fought the Horde's enslaved red dragons above Lordaeron and the Great Sea. When the Dark Portal reopened, Kurdran Wildhammer led his riders into Draenor with the Alliance Expedition. He gave up his return to seal the rift, and a colossal statue in Stormwind's Valley of Heroes honors his deed. In Aerie Peak, High Thane Falstad took command.

The human kingdoms later quarreled and fractured, but the Wildhammers remained loyal partners of King Terenas Menethil II. During the Third War, the Scourge swept across Lordaeron. Wildhammer flyers took to the skies again, fighting to defend allied lands and innocent refugees from the walking dead.

topic:world-of-warcraft-forever.text:
World of Warcraft: Forever. World of Warcraft: Forever takes place in the year after the Third War. Thrall's Horde has settled Durotar, and a regent rules Stormwind for its boy-king. The Forsaken hold the Undercity. The world reaches from the Skyborne of Zephras Isle to the contested Riverglades and Shen'dralas, sacred Mount Hyjal and the city of Dalaran rising from its ruins in the Alterac Mountains. The Burning Legion has been driven back at Mount Hyjal, yet the world bears the hurt it left behind. Thrall's Horde of orcs, trolls and tauren has made its home in Durotar and Mulgore. The Forsaken under Sylvanas Windrunner have joined the Horde from the ruins of Lordaeron.

In Stormwind, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon rules as regent for the boy-king Anduin Wrynn while King Varian is missing. The dwarves of Ironforge, the exiled gnomes and the night elves of Teldrassil stand with the Alliance. The Scourge still holds the Plaguelands. The Skyborne, or shen'dorei, descend from night elves who rebelled against Prince Tortheldrin of Eldre'Thalas. Wind spirits carried their island, Zephras Isle, into Skywall, the Elemental Plane of Air, and the Skyborne escaped with it. Ages there made them high elves, and more are now born blue-skinned.

The spirits vanished centuries ago, and Zephras Isle is slowly breaking apart. The Skyborne look back toward Azeroth. Their airships reach the Alterac Mountains near Dalaran and Mulgore's Skywatcher Plateau. They fight for both the Alliance and the Horde. Zephras Isle floats in Skywall as the Skyborne's homeland. East of the Burning Steppes, the Riverglades is an old Stormwind frontier lost in the First War. Loyalists at Farholde Keep hold out against the wilds, Horde outposts and the Twilight's Hammer at Sunnyglade.

Shen'dralas is a rugged borderland between Desolace, Feralas and Mulgore, contested by centaur, quilboar and outcasts. Mount Hyjal, sacred to the night elves, still bears the scars of Archimonde's defeat. In the Alterac Mountains, the Kirin Tor have lowered Dalaran's shield and are rebuilding their city. Off Kalimdor's coast, the Horde and the Alliance battle over the Darkspear Islands. Danger waits beneath cities and in the world's far corners. There is the Hall of Thanes deep under Ironforge and the haunted Ruins of Lordaeron above the Undercity. An excavation site lies in the Wetlands, alongside the City of Dalaran itself.

Farther afield are the Drowned City in Stranglethorn Vale, Krol'dok Stronghold in the Riverglades, Alcaz Prison in Dustwallow Marsh, Blackmaw Hold in Azshara and the Shaper's Terrace in Un'Goro Crater. On Mount Hyjal, the Barrow Deeps and Hyjal Summit test the mightiest war bands. Warriors come from every race. Paladins are human, dwarf or Forsaken, while shaman are orc, tauren, troll, dwarf or Horde Skyborne. Priests are human, dwarf, gnome, night elf, troll or Forsaken. Mages are human, gnome, orc, troll, Forsaken or Alliance Skyborne.

Warlocks are human, gnome, orc, troll or Forsaken. Hunters are human, dwarf, night elf, orc, tauren, troll or Skyborne. Rogues come from every race but the tauren. Druids are night elf, tauren or Skyborne.
